231.s:
puṣkara uvāca
viśanti yena mārgeṇa vāyasā bahavaḥ puraṃ /
tena mārgeṇa ruddhasya purasya grahaṇaṃ bhavet //
231.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
विशन्ति येन मार्गेण वायसा बहवः पुरं /
तेन मार्गेण रुद्धस्य पुरस्य ग्रहणं भवेत् //
231.m: Puṣkara said: / By whichever road many crows enter a city, / by that road will be the capture of the besieged city.

231.s:
senāyāṃ yadi vāsārthe niviṣṭo vāyaso ruvan /
vāmo bhayāturastrasto bhayaṃ vadati dustaraṃ(1) //
231.d:
सेनायां यदि वासार्थे निविष्टो वायसो रुवन् /
वामो भयातुरस्त्रस्तो भयं वदति दुस्तरं(1) //
231.m: If a crow cawing alights in an army for lodging, / being on the left, distressed by fear, and terrified, it foretells insurmountable fear.

231.s:
chāyāṅgavāhanopānacchatravastrādikuṭṭane /
mṛtyustatpūjane pūjā tadiṣṭakaraṇe śubhaṃ //
231.d:
छायाङ्गवाहनोपानच्छत्रवस्त्रादिकुट्टने /
मृत्युस्तत्पूजने पूजा तदिष्टकरणे शुभं //
231.m: When it pecks at a shadow, a limb, a vehicle, shoes, an umbrella, or garments, / there is death; in revering them, respect; in doing what is pleasing to it, good fortune.

231.s:
proṣitāgamakṛtkākaḥ kurvan dvāri gatāgataṃ /
raktaṃ dagdhaṃ gṛhe dravyaṃ kṣipanvahnivedakaḥ //
231.d:
प्रोषितागमकृत्काकः कुर्वन् द्वारि गतागतं /
रक्तं दग्धं गृहे द्रव्यं क्षिपन्वह्निवेदकः //
231.m: A crow going back and forth at the door causes the arrival of a traveller. / Dropping a red or burnt object in the house, it indicates fire.

231.s:
nyasedraktaṃ purastācca nivedayati bandhanaṃ /
pītaṃ dravyaṃ tathā rukma rūpyameva tu bhārgava //
231.d:
न्यसेद्रक्तं पुरस्ताच्च निवेदयति बन्धनं /
पीतं द्रव्यं तथा रुक्म रूप्यमेव तु भार्गव //
231.m: If it should place a red [object] in front, it indicates imprisonment; / likewise a yellow object [indicates] gold, and silver [indicates] silver, O Bhārgava.

231.s:
yaccaivopanayed dravyaṃ tasya labdhiṃ vinirdiśet /
dravyaṃ vāpanayedyattu tasya hāniṃ vinirdiśet //
231.d:
यच्चैवोपनयेद् द्रव्यं तस्य लब्धिं विनिर्दिशेत् /
द्रव्यं वापनयेद्यत्तु तस्य हानिं विनिर्दिशेत् //
231.m: Whatever object it brings, one should predict the acquisition thereof; / or whatever object it carries away, one should predict the loss thereof.

231.s:
purato dhanalabdhiḥ syādāmamāṃsasya chardane /
bhūlabdhiḥ syān mṛdaḥ kṣepe rājyaṃ ratnārpaṇe mahat //
231.d:
पुरतो धनलब्धिः स्यादाममांसस्य छर्दने /
भूलब्धिः स्यान् मृदः क्षेपे राज्यं रत्नार्पणे महत् //
231.m: Upon vomiting raw meat in front, there will be gain of wealth; / upon throwing soil, gain of land; upon offering a jewel, a great kingdom.

231.s:
yātuḥ kāko 'nukūlastu kṣemaḥ karmakṣamo bhavet /
na tvarthasādhako jñeyaḥ pratikūlo bhayāvahaḥ //
231.d:
यातुः काको ऽनुकूलस्तु क्षेमः कर्मक्षमो भवेत् /
न त्वर्थसाधको ज्ञेयः प्रतिकूलो भयावहः //
231.m: A favorable crow brings welfare to a traveler and makes him successful in his endeavor; / but an unfavorable [crow] is to be known as not accomplishing aims and bringing fear.

231.s:
sammukhe 'bhyeti viruvan yātrāghātakaro bhavet /
vāmaḥ kākaḥ smṛto dhanyo dakṣiṇo 'rthavināśakṛt(2) //
:n
1 duṣkaramiti kha.. , cha ca
2 dakṣiṇo 'nnavināśakṛditi ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 339
231.d:
सम्मुखे ऽभ्येति विरुवन् यात्राघातकरो भवेत् /
वामः काकः स्मृतो धन्यो दक्षिणो ऽर्थविनाशकृत्(2) //
:न्
1 दुष्करमिति ख.. , छ च
2 दक्षिणो ऽन्नविनाशकृदिति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 339
231.m:
Coming directly in front while crying out, it causes disruption to the journey. / A crow on the left is remembered as auspicious; on the right, it causes loss of wealth.
[...]
1. Manuscripts kha and cha read "duṣkaram".
2. Manuscripts ga, gha, and ña read "dakṣiṇo 'nnavināśakṛt". / [Page 339]

231.s:
vāmo 'nulomagaḥ śreṣṭho madhyamo dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
pratilomagatirvāmo gamanapratiṣedhakṛt //
231.d:
वामो ऽनुलोमगः श्रेष्ठो मध्यमो दक्षिणः स्मृतः /
प्रतिलोमगतिर्वामो गमनप्रतिषेधकृत् //
231.m: On the left going with the wind is best; on the right is considered middling. / Moving against the wind on the left prohibits traveling.

231.s:
nivedayati yātrārthamabhipretaṃ gṛhe gataḥ(1) /
ekākṣaracaraṇastvarkaṃ vīkṣamāṇo bhayāvahaḥ //
231.d:
निवेदयति यात्रार्थमभिप्रेतं गृहे गतः(1) /
एकाक्षरचरणस्त्वर्कं वीक्षमाणो भयावहः //
231.m: Gone to a house, it indicates the desired purpose for a journey. / But moving with one eye or foot while looking at the sun, it brings fear.

231.s:
koṭare vāsamānaś ca mahānarthakaro bhavet /
na śubhastūṣare kākaḥ paṅkāṅkaḥ sa tu śasyate //
231.d:
कोटरे वासमानश् च महानर्थकरो भवेत् /
न शुभस्तूषरे काकः पङ्काङ्कः स तु शस्यते //
231.m: And dwelling in a hollow, it causes great calamity. / A crow in a barren ground is not auspicious, but smeared with mud it is commended.

231.s:
amedhyapūrṇavadanaḥ kākaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ(2) /
jñeyāḥ patatriṇo 'nye 'pi kākavad bhṛgunandana //
231.d:
अमेध्यपूर्णवदनः काकः सर्वार्थसाधकः(2) /
ज्ञेयाः पतत्रिणो ऽन्ये ऽपि काकवद् भृगुनन्दन //
231.m: A crow whose mouth is full of impure matter accomplishes all ends. / Other birds should also be understood like the crow, O son of Bhṛgu.

231.s:
skandhāvārāpasavyasthāḥ śvāno vipravināśakāḥ /
indrasthāne narendrasya pureśasya tu gopure //
231.d:
स्कन्धावारापसव्यस्थाः श्वानो विप्रविनाशकाः /
इन्द्रस्थाने नरेन्द्रस्य पुरेशस्य तु गोपुरे //
231.m: Dogs staying to the right of an army camp destroy the Brahmins; / at Indra's station, [they destroy] the king; at the gate, the lord of the city.

231.s:
antargṛhe gṛheśasya maraṇāya bhavedbhaṣan /
yasya jighrati vāmāṅgaṃ tasya syādarthasiddhaye //
231.d:
अन्तर्गृहे गृहेशस्य मरणाय भवेद्भषन् /
यस्य जिघ्रति वामाङ्गं तस्य स्यादर्थसिद्धये //
231.m: Barking inside the house, it leads to the death of the master of the house. / The one whose left limb it smells will have attainment of wealth.

231.s:
bhayāya dakṣiṇaṃ cāṅgaṃ tathā bhujamadakṣiṇaṃ /
yātrāghātakaro yāturbhavet pratimukhāgataḥ //
231.d:
भयाय दक्षिणं चाङ्गं तथा भुजमदक्षिणं /
यात्राघातकरो यातुर्भवेत् प्रतिमुखागतः //
231.m: The right limb [it smells] leads to fear, and likewise the left arm. / Coming face-to-face, it disrupts the journey of the traveler.

231.s:
mārgāvarodhako mārge caurān vadati bhārgava /
alābho 'sthimukhaḥ pāpo rajjucīramukhas tathā //
231.d:
मार्गावरोधको मार्गे चौरान् वदति भार्गव /
अलाभो ऽस्थिमुखः पापो रज्जुचीरमुखस् तथा //
231.m: Obstructing the path on a road, it announces thieves, O Bhārgava. / With a bone in its mouth it is evil, causing failure; likewise with a rope or rag in its mouth.

231.s:
sopānatkamukho dhanyo māṃsapūrṇamukho 'pi ca /
amaṅgalyamukhadravyaṃ keśañcaivāśubhaṃ tathā //
231.d:
सोपानत्कमुखो धन्यो मांसपूर्णमुखो ऽपि च /
अमङ्गल्यमुखद्रव्यं केशञ्चैवाशुभं तथा //
231.m: With a shoe in its mouth it is auspicious, and also with a mouth full of meat. / An inauspicious substance or hair in its mouth is likewise unfavorable.

231.s:
avamūtryāgrato yāti yasya tasya bhayaṃ bhavet /
yasyāvamūtrya vrajati śubhaṃ deśantathā drumaṃ //
:n
1 nanvarthasādhaka ity ādiḥ, gṛhe gata ity antaḥḥ pāṭhaḥ ṭa..
pustake nāsti
2 koṭare ity ādiḥ sarvārthasādhaka ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ ṭa..pustake
nāsti
:p 340
231.d:
अवमूत्र्याग्रतो याति यस्य तस्य भयं भवेत् /
यस्यावमूत्र्य व्रजति शुभं देशन्तथा द्रुमं //
:न्
1 नन्वर्थसाधक इत्य् आदिः, गृहे गत इत्य् अन्तःः पाठः ट..
पुस्तके नास्ति
2 कोटरे इत्य् आदिः सर्वार्थसाधक इत्य् अन्तः पाठः ट..पुस्तके
नास्ति
:प् 340
231.m:
The one in front of whom it urinates and walks on will have fear. / An auspicious land or tree upon which it urinates and goes,
[...]
1. The passage beginning with "nanvarthasādhakaḥ" and ending with "gṛhe gataḥ" is absent in manuscript ṭa.
2. The passage beginning with "koṭare" and ending with "sarvārthasādhakaḥ" is absent in manuscript ṭa. / [Page 340]

231.s:
maṅgalañca tathā dravyaṃ tasya syādarthasiddhaye /
śvavacca rāma vijñeyās tathā vai jambukādayaḥ //
231.d:
मङ्गलञ्च तथा द्रव्यं तस्य स्यादर्थसिद्धये /
श्ववच्च राम विज्ञेयास् तथा वै जम्बुकादयः //
231.m: and likewise an auspicious substance, will lead to his attainment of prosperity. / And jackals and other [animals] are to be known like dogs, O Rāma.

231.s:
bhayāya svāmini jñeyamanimittaṃ rutaṅgavāṃ /
niśi caurabhayāya syādvikṛtaṃ mṛtyave tathā //
231.d:
भयाय स्वामिनि ज्ञेयमनिमित्तं रुतङ्गवां /
निशि चौरभयाय स्याद्विकृतं मृत्यवे तथा //
231.m: A groundless cry of cows is to be known to cause fear to the owner; / at night, it leads to fear of thieves, and unnatural [crying leads] to death.

231.s:
śivāya svāmino rātrau balīvardo nadan bhavet /
utsṛṣṭavṛṣabho rājño vijayaṃ samprayacchati //
231.d:
शिवाय स्वामिनो रात्रौ बलीवर्दो नदन् भवेत् /
उत्सृष्टवृषभो राज्ञो विजयं सम्प्रयच्छति //
231.m: An ox bellowing at night brings welfare to its master. / A bull set free confers victory upon a king.

231.s:
abhayaṃ bhakṣayantyaś ca gāvo dattās tathā svakāḥ /
tyaktasnehāḥ svavatseṣu garbhakṣayakarā matāḥ //
231.d:
अभयं भक्षयन्त्यश् च गावो दत्तास् तथा स्वकाः /
त्यक्तस्नेहाः स्ववत्सेषु गर्भक्षयकरा मताः //
231.m: And cows that eat fearlessly, as well as those given away as one's own, [are auspicious]; / those lacking affection for their calves are considered to cause loss of the womb.

231.s:
bhūmiṃ pādair vinighnantyo dīnā bhītā bhayāvahāḥ /
ārdrāṅgyo hṛṣṭaromāś ca śṛgalagnamṛdaḥ śubhāḥ //
231.d:
भूमिं पादैर् विनिघ्नन्त्यो दीना भीता भयावहाः /
आर्द्राङ्ग्यो हृष्टरोमाश् च शृगलग्नमृदः शुभाः //
231.m: Cows striking the ground with their feet, wretched and frightened, bring fear. / Those whose limbs are wet, whose hair stands on end, and who have mud sticking to their horns, are auspicious.

231.s:
mahiṣyādiṣu cāpyetat sarvaṃ vācyaṃ vijānatā /
ārohaṇaṃ tathānyena saparyāṇasya(1) vājinaḥ //
231.d:
महिष्यादिषु चाप्येतत् सर्वं वाच्यं विजानता /
आरोहणं तथान्येन सपर्याणस्य(1) वाजिनः //
231.m: All this should also be declared by a knowledgeable person regarding she-buffaloes and the like. / Likewise, if a horse with a saddle is mounted by another,

231.s:
jalopaveśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ bhūmau ca parivartanaṃ /
vipatkaranturaṅgasya suptaṃ vāpyanimittataḥ //
231.d:
जलोपवेशनं नेष्टं भूमौ च परिवर्तनं /
विपत्करन्तुरङ्गस्य सुप्तं वाप्यनिमित्ततः //
231.m: [or] sitting in water, or rolling on the ground—[these] are not desirable; / or sleeping without cause brings calamity to the horse.

231.s:
yavamodakayordveṣastvakasmācca na śasyate /
vadanādrudhirotpattirvepanaṃ na ca śasyate //
231.d:
यवमोदकयोर्द्वेषस्त्वकस्माच्च न शस्यते /
वदनाद्रुधिरोत्पत्तिर्वेपनं न च शस्यते //
231.m: Sudden aversion to barley and sweets is not praised; / bleeding from the mouth and trembling are not praised.

231.s:
krīḍan vaikaḥ kapotaiś ca sārikābhirmṛtiṃ vadet /
sāśrunetro jihvayā ca pādalehī vinaṣṭaye(2) //
231.d:
क्रीडन् वैकः कपोतैश् च सारिकाभिर्मृतिं वदेत् /
साश्रुनेत्रो जिह्वया च पादलेही विनष्टये(2) //
231.m: Playing alone with pigeons or with mynas indicates death; / with tearful eyes and licking its legs with its tongue, [it leads] to destruction.

231.s:
vāmapādena ca tathā vilikhaṃś ca vasundharāṃ /
svapedvā vāmapārśvena divā vā na śubhapradaḥ //
231.d:
वामपादेन च तथा विलिखंश् च वसुन्धरां /
स्वपेद्वा वामपार्श्वेन दिवा वा न शुभप्रदः //
231.m: And scratching the earth with its left foot, / or sleeping on its left side during the day, does not bestow good fortune.

231.s:
bhayāya syāt sakṛnmūtrī tathā nidrāvilānanaḥ /
:n
1 saparyārhasyeti sādhuḥ
2 vināśakṛditi ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 341
ārohaṇaṃ na ceddadyāt pratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet //
231.d:
भयाय स्यात् सकृन्मूत्री तथा निद्राविलाननः /
:न्
1 सपर्यार्हस्येति साधुः
2 विनाशकृदिति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 341
आरोहणं न चेद्दद्यात् प्रतीपं वा गृहं व्रजेत् //
231.m:
Excreting urine and dung together, or having a face clouded with sleep, brings fear.
[...]
1. "Saparyārhasya" is the correct reading.
2. "Vināśakṛt" in manuscripts ja and ṭa.
Page 341.
If it does not permit mounting, or turns back to the stable,

231.s:
yātrāvighātamācaṣṭe vāmapārśvaṃ tathā spṛśan /
heṣamāṇaḥ śatruyodhaṃ pādasparśī jayāvahaḥ //
231.d:
यात्राविघातमाचष्टे वामपार्श्वं तथा स्पृशन् /
हेषमाणः शत्रुयोधं पादस्पर्शी जयावहः //
231.m: it indicates an obstacle to the expedition; likewise, touching its left flank [is ominous]. / Neighing [and] touching an enemy warrior with its hoof brings victory.

231.s:
grāme vrajati nāgaścen maithunaṃ deśahā bhavet /
prasūtā nāgavanitā mattā cāntāya bhūpateḥ //
231.d:
ग्रामे व्रजति नागश्चेन् मैथुनं देशहा भवेत् /
प्रसूता नागवनिता मत्ता चान्ताय भूपतेः //
231.m: If an elephant enters a village, copulation [there] destroys the country; / a female elephant giving birth or in musth leads to the end of the king.

231.s:
ārohaṇaṃ na ceddadyāt pratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet /
madaṃ vā vāraṇo jahyādrājaghātakaro bhavet //
231.d:
आरोहणं न चेद्दद्यात् प्रतीपं वा गृहं व्रजेत् /
मदं वा वारणो जह्याद्राजघातकरो भवेत् //
231.m: If it does not permit mounting, or turns back to its stable, / or if the elephant sheds its musth, it will cause the death of the king.

231.s:
vāmaṃ dakṣiṇapādena pādamākramate śubhaḥ /
dakṣiṇañca tathā dantaṃ parimārṣṭi kareṇa ca //
231.d:
वामं दक्षिणपादेन पादमाक्रमते शुभः /
दक्षिणञ्च तथा दन्तं परिमार्ष्टि करेण च //
231.m: When it steps over its left foot with its right foot, it is auspicious; / and likewise when it wipes its right tusk with its trunk.

231.s:
vṛṣo 'śvaḥ kuñjaro vāpi ripusainyagato 'śubhaḥ /
khaṇḍameghātivṛṣṭyā tu senā nāśamavāpnuyāt //
231.d:
वृषो ऽश्वः कुञ्जरो वापि रिपुसैन्यगतो ऽशुभः /
खण्डमेघातिवृष्ट्या तु सेना नाशमवाप्नुयात् //
231.m: A bull, horse, or elephant that goes over to the enemy army is inauspicious. / Through the excessive rain of scattered clouds, an army meets destruction.

231.s:
pratikūlagraharkṣāttu tathā sammukhamārutāt(1) /
yātrākāle raṇe vāpi chatrādipatanaṃ bhayaṃ //
231.d:
प्रतिकूलग्रहर्क्षात्तु तथा सम्मुखमारुतात्(1) /
यात्राकाले रणे वापि छत्रादिपतनं भयं //
231.m: Due to adverse planets and lunar mansions, as well as a headwind, / at the time of an expedition or in battle, the falling of umbrellas and the like brings fear.

231.s:
hṛṣṭā narāścānulomā grahā vai jayalakṣaṇaṃ /
kākair yodhābhibhavanaṃ kravyādbhirmaṇḍalakṣayaḥ //
231.d:
हृष्टा नराश्चानुलोमा ग्रहा वै जयलक्षणं /
काकैर् योधाभिभवनं क्रव्याद्भिर्मण्डलक्षयः //
231.m: Men who are joyous and planets that are favorable are marks of victory; / the overcoming of warriors by crows [is unfavorable], and by carnivorous creatures [indicates] destruction of the realm.

231.s:
prācīpaścimakaiśānī śaumyā preṣṭhā śubhā ca dik //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śakunāni nāma
ekatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 vāmaṃ dakṣiṇetyādiḥ, sammukhamārutādityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ
jha.. pustake nāsti
:p 342
:ś atha dvātriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yātrāmaṇḍalacintādiḥ
231.d:
प्राचीपश्चिमकैशानी शौम्या प्रेष्ठा शुभा च दिक् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शकुनानि नाम
एकत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 वामं दक्षिणेत्यादिः, सम्मुखमारुतादित्यन्तः पाठः
झ.. पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 342
:श् अथ द्वात्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
यात्रामण्डलचिन्तादिः
231.m:
The east, west, northeast, and north are most favored and auspicious directions.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-first chapter, named "Omens", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[...]
1. The text beginning with "vāmaṃ dakṣiṇa-" up to "sammukhamārutāt" is not present in manuscript jha.
Page 342.
Now, the two hundred and thirty-second chapter.
Deliberation on the Circle of Kings for an Expedition, etc.

232.s:
puṣkara uvāca
sarvayātrāṃ pravakṣyāmi rājadharmasamāśrayāt /
astaṅgate nīcagate vikale ripurāśige //
232.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
सर्वयात्रां प्रवक्ष्यामि राजधर्मसमाश्रयात् /
अस्तङ्गते नीचगते विकले रिपुराशिगे //
232.m: Puṣkara said: / I will explain all expeditions, based upon the duties of kings. / When [a planet] has set, is in its debilitation, is impaired, or is in an enemy sign,

232.s:
pratilome ca vidhvaste śukre yātrāṃ visarjayet(1) /
pratilome budhe yātrāṃ dikpatau ca tathā ca grahe //
232.d:
प्रतिलोमे च विध्वस्ते शुक्रे यात्रां विसर्जयेत्(1) /
प्रतिलोमे बुधे यात्रां दिक्पतौ च तथा च ग्रहे //
232.m: and when Venus is retrograde or afflicted, one should avoid an expedition; / likewise when Mercury is retrograde, and when the planetary regent of the direction is [adverse].

232.s:
vaidhṛtau ca vyatīpāte nāge ca śakunau tathā /
catuṣpāde ca kintughne tathā yātrāṃ vivarjayet //
232.d:
वैधृतौ च व्यतीपाते नागे च शकुनौ तथा /
चतुष्पादे च किन्तुघ्ने तथा यात्रां विवर्जयेत् //
232.m: And during Vaidhṛta, Vyatīpāta, Nāga, Śakuni, / Catuṣpad, and Kiṃtughna, one should likewise avoid an expedition.

232.s:
vipattāre naidhane ca pratyarau cātha janmani /
gaṇḍe vivarjayedyātrāṃ riktāyāñca tithāvapi //
232.d:
विपत्तारे नैधने च प्रत्यरौ चाथ जन्मनि /
गण्डे विवर्जयेद्यात्रां रिक्तायाञ्च तिथावपि //
232.m: Under a star of adversity, of death, of enmity, or the star of birth, / during a gaṇḍa, and also on an empty lunar day, one should avoid an expedition.

232.s:
udīcī ca tathā prācī(2) tayoraikyaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
paścimā dakṣiṇā yā dik tayoraikyaṃ tathaiva ca //
232.d:
उदीची च तथा प्राची(2) तयोरैक्यं प्रकीर्तितं /
पश्चिमा दक्षिणा या दिक् तयोरैक्यं तथैव च //
232.m: The north and the east: their unity is proclaimed; / the west and the south: their unity is likewise stated.

232.s:
vāyvagnidiksamudbhūtaṃ parighanna tu laṅghayet /
ādityacandraśaurāstu divasāś ca na śobhanāḥ //
232.d:
वाय्वग्निदिक्समुद्भूतं परिघन्न तु लङ्घयेत् /
आदित्यचन्द्रशौरास्तु दिवसाश् च न शोभनाः //
232.m: One should not cross the obstacle arising in the direction of the wind (northwest) or fire (southeast). / The days of the Sun, the Moon, and Saturn are not auspicious.

232.s:
kṛttikādyāni pūrveṇa maghādyāni ca yāmyataḥ /
maitrādyānyapare cātha vāsavādyāni vāpyudak //
232.d:
कृत्तिकाद्यानि पूर्वेण मघाद्यानि च याम्यतः /
मैत्राद्यान्यपरे चाथ वासवाद्यानि वाप्युदक् //
232.m: [The asterisms] beginning with Kṛttikā belong to the east, those beginning with Maghā to the south, / those beginning with Maitrā (Anurādhā) to the west, and those beginning with Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā) to the north.

232.s:
sarvadvārāṇi śastāni chāyāmānaṃ vadāmi te /
āditye viṃśatirjñeyāś candre ṣoḍaśa kīrtitāḥ //
232.d:
सर्वद्वाराणि शस्तानि छायामानं वदामि ते /
आदित्ये विंशतिर्ज्ञेयाश् चन्द्रे षोडश कीर्तिताः //
232.m: All gates are praised; I shall tell you the measurement of shadows: / on Sunday, twenty [aṅgulas] are known; on Monday, sixteen are proclaimed;

232.s:
bhaume pañcadaśaivoktāś caturdaśa tathā budhe /
:n
1 vivarjayet iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
2 dik pūrvā yā tathodīcīti ja..
:p 343
trayodaśa tathā jīye śukre dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ //
232.d:
भौमे पञ्चदशैवोक्ताश् चतुर्दश तथा बुधे /
:न्
1 विवर्जयेत् इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
2 दिक् पूर्वा या तथोदीचीति ज..
:प् 343
त्रयोदश तथा जीये शुक्रे द्वादश कीर्तिताः //

232.s:
ekādaśa tathā saure sarvakarmasu kīrtitāḥ /
janmalagne śakracāpe sammukhe na vrajennaraḥ //
232.d:
एकादश तथा सौरे सर्वकर्मसु कीर्तिताः /
जन्मलग्ने शक्रचापे सम्मुखे न व्रजेन्नरः //
232.m: and eleven on Saturday, proclaimed for all undertakings. / A man should not set out during the ascendant of birth, or when Indra's rainbow is in front.

232.s:
śakunādau śubhe yāyājjayāya harimāsmaran /
vakṣye maṇḍalacintānte kartavyaṃ rājarakṣaṇaṃ //
232.d:
शकुनादौ शुभे यायाज्जयाय हरिमास्मरन् /
वक्ष्ये मण्डलचिन्तान्ते कर्तव्यं राजरक्षणं //
232.m: When an omen and the like is auspicious, he should march for victory, remembering Hari. / Following the deliberation on the circle [of kings], I shall speak of the protection of the king that must be performed.

232.s:
svāmyamātyaṃ tathā durgaṃ koṣo daṇḍastathaiva ca /
mitrañjanapadaś caiva rājyaṃ saptāṅgamucyate //
232.d:
स्वाम्यमात्यं तथा दुर्गं कोषो दण्डस्तथैव च /
मित्रञ्जनपदश् चैव राज्यं सप्ताङ्गमुच्यते //
232.m: The lord, the minister, the fortress, the treasury, and the army, / the ally, and the territory: the kingdom is said to have seven limbs.

232.s:
saptāṅgasya tu rājyasya vighnakartṝn vināśayet /
maṇḍaleṣu ca sarveṣu vṛddhiḥ kāryā mahīkṣitā //
232.d:
सप्ताङ्गस्य तु राज्यस्य विघ्नकर्तॄन् विनाशयेत् /
मण्डलेषु च सर्वेषु वृद्धिः कार्या महीक्षिता //
232.m: He should destroy those who create obstacles for the seven-limbed kingdom; / and prosperity must be achieved by the ruler of the earth in all circles [of kings].

232.s:
ātmamaṇḍalamevātra prathamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhavet /
sāmantāstasya vijñeyā ripavo maṇḍalasya tu //
232.d:
आत्ममण्डलमेवात्र प्रथमं मण्डलं भवेत् /
सामन्तास्तस्य विज्ञेया रिपवो मण्डलस्य तु //
232.m: One's own circle here is the first circle; / the adjacent rulers are known as the enemies of that circle.

232.s:
upetastu suhṛj jñeyaḥ śatrumitramataḥ paraṃ /
mitramitraṃ tato jñeyaṃ mitramitraripustataḥ //
232.d:
उपेतस्तु सुहृज् ज्ञेयः शत्रुमित्रमतः परं /
मित्रमित्रं ततो ज्ञेयं मित्रमित्ररिपुस्ततः //
232.m: The one adjoining [the enemy] is known as a friend; beyond that is the enemy's friend; / after that is known the friend's friend; after that is the enemy's friend's friend.

232.s:
etatpurastāt kathitaṃ paścādapi nibodha me /
pārṣṇigrāhastataḥ paścāttatastvākranda ucyate(1) //
232.d:
एतत्पुरस्तात् कथितं पश्चादपि निबोध मे /
पार्ष्णिग्राहस्ततः पश्चात्ततस्त्वाक्रन्द उच्यते(1) //
232.m: This is stated regarding the front; understand from me also what is behind: / the rearward enemy is behind, and after him is called the rearward ally.

232.s:
āsārastu tato 'nyaḥ syādākrandāsāra ucyate /
jigīṣoḥ śatruyuktasya vimuktasya tathā dvija //
232.d:
आसारस्तु ततो ऽन्यः स्यादाक्रन्दासार उच्यते /
जिगीषोः शत्रुयुक्तस्य विमुक्तस्य तथा द्विज //
232.m: The one after him would be the ally of the rearward enemy, and [the next] is called the ally of the rearward ally. / For the conqueror, joined with or freed from an enemy, O twice-born,

232.s:
nātrāpi niś cayaḥ śakyo vaktuṃ manujapuṅgava /
nigrahānugrahe śakto madhyasthaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
232.d:
नात्रापि निश् चयः शक्यो वक्तुं मनुजपुङ्गव /
निग्रहानुग्रहे शक्तो मध्यस्थः परिकीर्तितः //
232.m: no certainty can be stated here, O best of men! / Capable of punishment and favor, the intermediary is proclaimed.

232.s:
nigrahānugrahe śaktaḥ sarveṣāmapi yo bhavet /
udāsīnaḥ sa kathito balavān pṛthivīpatiḥ //
:n
1 maṇḍaleṣu ca sarveṣu sureśvarasamā hi te ity ardhaśloka
āsārastvityasya pūrvaṃ ṭa.. pustake vartate, parantvasaṃlagnaḥ
:p 344
232.d:
निग्रहानुग्रहे शक्तः सर्वेषामपि यो भवेत् /
उदासीनः स कथितो बलवान् पृथिवीपतिः //
:न्
1 मण्डलेषु च सर्वेषु सुरेश्वरसमा हि ते इत्य् अर्धश्लोक
आसारस्त्वित्यस्य पूर्वं ट.. पुस्तके वर्तते, परन्त्वसंलग्नः
:प् 344
232.m:
Whoever is capable of punishment and favor toward all / is called the neutral king, a powerful ruler of the earth.
[...]
1. The half-verse "maṇḍaleṣu ca sarveṣu sureśvarasamā hi te" occurs before "āsārastu" in manuscript ṭa, but it is unconnected.
Page 344.

232.s:
na kasyacidripurmitraṅkāraṇācchatrumitrake /
maṇḍalaṃ tava samproktametad dvādaśarājakaṃ //
232.d:
न कस्यचिद्रिपुर्मित्रङ्कारणाच्छत्रुमित्रके /
मण्डलं तव सम्प्रोक्तमेतद् द्वादशराजकं //
232.m: No one is an enemy or a friend [by nature]; enemies and friends exist due to a cause. / This circle of twelve kings has been declared to you.

232.s:
trividhā ripavo jñeyāḥ kulyānantarakṛtrimāḥ /
pūrvapūrvo gurusteṣāṃ duścikitsyatamo mataḥ //
232.d:
त्रिविधा रिपवो ज्ञेयाः कुल्यानन्तरकृत्रिमाः /
पूर्वपूर्वो गुरुस्तेषां दुश्चिकित्स्यतमो मतः //
232.m: Enemies are known to be of three kinds: born of the same family, neighboring, and fabricated; / each preceding one is considered more formidable and more difficult to cure than the next.

232.s:
anantaro 'pi yaḥ śatruḥ so 'pi me kṛtrimo mataḥ /
pārṣṇigrāho bhavecchatrormitrāṇi ripavas tathā //
232.d:
अनन्तरो ऽपि यः शत्रुः सो ऽपि मे कृत्रिमो मतः /
पार्ष्णिग्राहो भवेच्छत्रोर्मित्राणि रिपवस् तथा //
232.m: Even an immediate neighbor who is an enemy is also considered by me as fabricated. / The rearward enemy belongs to the enemy, and likewise allies [can become] enemies.

232.s:
pārṣṇigrāhamupāyaiś ca śamayecca tathā svakaṃ /
mitreṇa śatrorucchedaṃ praśaṃsanti purātanāḥ //
232.d:
पार्ष्णिग्राहमुपायैश् च शमयेच्च तथा स्वकं /
मित्रेण शत्रोरुच्छेदं प्रशंसन्ति पुरातनाः //
232.m: One should pacify one's own rearward enemy by means of expedients; / the ancients praise the eradication of an enemy by means of an ally.

232.s:
mitrañca śatrutāmeti sāmantatvādanantaraṃ /
śatruṃ jigoṣurucchindyāt(1) svayaṃ śaknoti cedyadi //
232.d:
मित्रञ्च शत्रुतामेति सामन्तत्वादनन्तरं /
शत्रुं जिगोषुरुच्छिन्द्यात्(1) स्वयं शक्नोति चेद्यदि //
232.m: And an ally turns into an enemy due to immediately bordering; / if the would-be conqueror is able himself, he should eradicate the enemy.

232.s:
pratāpavṛddhau tenāpi nāmitrājjāyate bhayaṃ /
yathāsya nodvijelloko viśvāsaś ca yathā bhavet //
232.d:
प्रतापवृद्धौ तेनापि नामित्राज्जायते भयं /
यथास्य नोद्विजेल्लोको विश्वासश् च यथा भवेत् //
232.m: When majesty increases through that, no fear arises even from an enemy; / in such a way that the people do not become agitated and trust is established,

232.s:
jigīṣurdharmavijayī tathā lokaṃ vaśannayet /
:e ity āgneye mahāopurāṇe yātrāmaṇḍalacintādirnāma
dvātriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha trayastriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ
232.d:
जिगीषुर्धर्मविजयी तथा लोकं वशन्नयेत् /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महाओपुराणे यात्रामण्डलचिन्तादिर्नाम
द्वात्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
षाड्गुण्यं
232.m:
the would-be conqueror, victorious through righteousness, should bring the world under his sway.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-second chapter, named 'Consideration of Expedition, the Maṇḍala, and Other Matters', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirty-third chapter:
The Six Measures of Policy

233.s:
puṣkara uvāca
sāmabhedau mayā proktau dānadaṇḍau tathaiva ca /
daṇḍaḥ svadeśe kathitaḥ paradeśe vravīmi te //
:n
1 śatruṃ jihīrṣurucchindyāditi gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 345
233.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
सामभेदौ मया प्रोक्तौ दानदण्डौ तथैव च /
दण्डः स्वदेशे कथितः परदेशे व्रवीमि ते //
:न्
1 शत्रुं जिहीर्षुरुच्छिन्द्यादिति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 345
233.m:
Puṣkara said: / Conciliation and sowing dissension have been taught by me, and likewise gift and punishment. / Punishment has been described regarding one's own realm; I shall explain it to you regarding a foreign realm.
[...]
1 'Wishing to take the enemy, he should uproot [him]' in manuscripts gha and ña. / [Page 345]

233.s:
prakāśaścāprakāśaś ca dvividho daṇḍa ucyate /
luṇṭhanaṃ grāmaghātaś ca śasyaghāto 'gnidīpanaṃ //
233.d:
प्रकाशश्चाप्रकाशश् च द्विविधो दण्ड उच्यते /
लुण्ठनं ग्रामघातश् च शस्यघातो ऽग्निदीपनं //
233.m: Punishment is said to be of two kinds: open and secret. / Plundering, devastation of villages, destruction of crops, setting fires,

233.s:
prakāśo 'tha viṣaṃ vahnirvividhaiḥ puruṣair badhaḥ /
dūṣaṇañcaiva sādhūnāmudakānāñca dūṣaṇaṃ //
233.d:
प्रकाशो ऽथ विषं वह्निर्विविधैः पुरुषैर् बधः /
दूषणञ्चैव साधूनामुदकानाञ्च दूषणं //
233.m: are open [punishment]; whereas poison, fire, slaying through various secret agents, / defamation of honest persons, and poisoning of waters,

233.s:
daṇḍapraṇayaṇaṃ proktamupekṣāṃ śṛṇu bhārgava /
yadā manyate nṛpatī raṇe na mama vigrahaḥ //
233.d:
दण्डप्रणयणं प्रोक्तमुपेक्षां शृणु भार्गव /
यदा मन्यते नृपती रणे न मम विग्रहः //
233.m: are described as the execution of [covert] punishment. Hear about diplomatic indifference, O descendant of Bhṛgu: / When a king considers, 'War in battle will not [benefit] me,

233.s:
anarthāyānubandhaḥ syāt sandhinā ca tathā bhavet /
sāmalabdhāspadañcātra dānañcārthakṣayaṅkaraṃ //
233.d:
अनर्थायानुबन्धः स्यात् सन्धिना च तथा भवेत् /
सामलब्धास्पदञ्चात्र दानञ्चार्थक्षयङ्करं //
233.m: an escalation would lead to misfortune, and likewise through an alliance; / conciliation finds no ground here, and a gift causes loss of wealth;

233.s:
bhedadaṇḍānubandhaḥ syāttadopekṣāṃ samāśrayet /
na cāyaṃ mama śaknoti kiñcit kartumupadravaṃ //
233.d:
भेददण्डानुबन्धः स्यात्तदोपेक्षां समाश्रयेत् /
न चायं मम शक्नोति किञ्चित् कर्तुमुपद्रवं //
233.m: an escalation of dissension or punishment would occur,' then he should resort to indifference. / [Or if he thinks,] 'This enemy is not able to cause me any injury,

233.s:
na cāhamasya śaknomi tatropekṣāṃ samāśrayet /
avajñopahatastatra rājñā kāryo ripurbhavet //
233.d:
न चाहमस्य शक्नोमि तत्रोपेक्षां समाश्रयेत् /
अवज्ञोपहतस्तत्र राज्ञा कार्यो रिपुर्भवेत् //
233.m: and I am not able [to harm] him,' then he should resort to indifference. / There the enemy should be brought into a condition of being stricken by contempt by the king.

233.s:
māyopāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi utpātair anṛtaiś carat /
śatrorudvejanaṃ śatroḥ śivirasthasya pakṣiṇaḥ //
233.d:
मायोपायं प्रवक्ष्यामि उत्पातैर् अनृतैश् चरत् /
शत्रोरुद्वेजनं शत्रोः शिविरस्थस्य पक्षिणः //
233.m: I shall declare the method of illusion: operating with false portents, / causing terror to the enemy; [for example,] attaching to the tail of a bird,

233.s:
sthūlasya tasya pucchasthāṃ kṛtvolkāṃ vipulāṃ dvija /
visṛjecca tataś caivamulkāpātaṃ pradarśayet //
233.d:
स्थूलस्य तस्य पुच्छस्थां कृत्वोल्कां विपुलां द्विज /
विसृजेच्च ततश् चैवमुल्कापातं प्रदर्शयेत् //
233.m: a large one, that resides in the enemy's camp, a huge firebrand, O twice-born one, / and then releasing it, he should thus display the falling of a meteor.

233.s:
evamanye darśanīyā utpātā bahavo 'pi ca /
udvejanaṃ tathā kuryāt kuhakair vividhair dviṣāṃ //
233.d:
एवमन्ये दर्शनीया उत्पाता बहवो ऽपि च /
उद्वेजनं तथा कुर्यात् कुहकैर् विविधैर् द्विषां //
233.m: In this way many other portents also should be shown. / Likewise he should terrify enemies through diverse illusions.

233.s:
sāṃvatsarāstāpasāś ca nāśaṃ brūyuḥ prarasya ca /
jigīṣuḥ pṛthivīṃ rājā tena codvejayet parān //
233.d:
सांवत्सरास्तापसाश् च नाशं ब्रूयुः प्ररस्य च /
जिगीषुः पृथिवीं राजा तेन चोद्वेजयेत् परान् //
233.m: Astrologers and ascetics should predict the destruction of the adversary; / and by this means the king desiring conquest over the earth should alarm his foes.

233.s:
devatānāṃ prasādaś ca kīrtanīyaḥ parasya tu /
āgatanno 'mitrabalaṃ praharadhvamabhītavat //
233.d:
देवतानां प्रसादश् च कीर्तनीयः परस्य तु /
आगतन्नो ऽमित्रबलं प्रहरध्वमभीतवत् //
233.m: And the favor of deities toward him should be proclaimed to the enemy: / 'Our enemy's army has arrived; strike without fear!'

233.s:
evaṃ brūyādraṇe prāpte bhagnāḥ sarve pare iti /
:p 346
kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāḥ kāryā vācyaḥ śatrurhatas tathā //
233.d:
एवं ब्रूयाद्रणे प्राप्ते भग्नाः सर्वे परे इति /
:प् 346
क्ष्वेडाः किलकिलाः कार्या वाच्यः शत्रुर्हतस् तथा //
233.m:
Thus he should proclaim when battle is joined: 'The enemies have all been broken!'
[Page 346]
War cries and shouts of triumph should be raised, and it should be declared: 'The enemy has been slain!'

233.s:
devājñāvṛṃhito rājā sannaddhaḥ samaraṃ prati /
indrajālaṃ pravakṣyāmi indraṃ kālena darśayet //
233.d:
देवाज्ञावृंहितो राजा सन्नद्धः समरं प्रति /
इन्द्रजालं प्रवक्ष्यामि इन्द्रं कालेन दर्शयेत् //
233.m: The king, bolstered by divine command, should be equipped for battle. / I shall explain sorcery: he should display Indra in due time,

233.s:
caturaṅgaṃ balaṃ rājā sahāyārthaṃ divaukasāṃ /
balantu darśayet prāptaṃ raktavṛṣṭiñcendrapau //
233.d:
चतुरङ्गं बलं राजा सहायार्थं दिवौकसां /
बलन्तु दर्शयेत् प्राप्तं रक्तवृष्टिञ्चेन्द्रपौ //
233.m: a fourfold army [descending] to aid the king on behalf of the gods; / he should display an army arrived, and a rain of blood, and royal guardians,

233.s:
chinnāni ripuśīrṣāṇi prāsādāgreṣu darśayet(1) /
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ sampravakṣyāmi tadvarau sandhivigrahau //
233.d:
छिन्नानि रिपुशीर्षाणि प्रासादाग्रेषु दर्शयेत्(1) /
षाड्गुण्यं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि तद्वरौ सन्धिविग्रहौ //
233.m: and severed heads of enemies displayed upon the tops of temples. / I shall declare the sixfold policy, of which alliance and war are the foremost:

233.s:
sandhiś ca vigrahaś caiva yānamāsanameva ca /
dvaidhībhāvaḥ saṃśayaś ca ṣaḍguṇāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
233.d:
सन्धिश् च विग्रहश् चैव यानमासनमेव च /
द्वैधीभावः संशयश् च षड्गुणाः परिकीर्तिताः //
233.m: Alliance, war, marching, halting, / duplicity, and seeking refuge are declared to be the six measures of policy.

233.s:
paṇabandhaḥ smṛtaḥ sandhirapakārastu vigrahaḥ /
jigīṣoḥ śatruviṣaye yānaṃ yātrābhidhīyate //
233.d:
पणबन्धः स्मृतः सन्धिरपकारस्तु विग्रहः /
जिगीषोः शत्रुविषये यानं यात्राभिधीयते //
233.m: Alliance is traditionally understood as a binding agreement, whereas war is injury. / The movement of one desiring conquest into the enemy's territory is termed marching.

233.s:
vigraheṇa svake deśe sthitirāsanamucyate /
balārdhena prayāṇantu dvaidhībhāvaḥ sa ucyate //
233.d:
विग्रहेण स्वके देशे स्थितिरासनमुच्यते /
बलार्धेन प्रयाणन्तु द्वैधीभावः स उच्यते //
233.m: Remaining in one's own realm while in a state of hostility is called halting. / Setting out with half one's force is called duplicity.

233.s:
udāsīno madhyago vā saṃśrayātsaṃśayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
samena sandhiranveṣyo 'hīnena ca balīyasā //
233.d:
उदासीनो मध्यगो वा संश्रयात्संशयः स्मृतः /
समेन सन्धिरन्वेष्यो ऽहीनेन च बलीयसा //
233.m: Seeking shelter with a neutral or intermediary king is known as seeking refuge. / An alliance should be sought with an equal, not with an inferior, and with one who is stronger.

233.s:
hīnena vigrahaḥ kāryaḥ svayaṃ rājñā balīyasā /
tatrāpi śuddhapārṣṇistu balīyāṃsaṃ samāśrayet //
233.d:
हीनेन विग्रहः कार्यः स्वयं राज्ञा बलीयसा /
तत्रापि शुद्धपार्ष्णिस्तु बलीयांसं समाश्रयेत् //
233.m: War should be waged against an inferior by a stronger king himself; / even then, having secured his rear, he should resort to a stronger ally.

233.s:
āsīnaḥ karmavicchedaṃ śaktaḥ kartuṃ riporyadā /
aśuddhapārṣṇiścāsīta vigṛhya vasudhādhipaḥ //
233.d:
आसीनः कर्मविच्छेदं शक्तः कर्तुं रिपोर्यदा /
अशुद्धपार्ष्णिश्चासीत विगृह्य वसुधाधिपः //
233.m: When, while remaining halted, the ruler of the earth is able to interrupt the enemy's undertakings, / he should remain halted in hostility, even if his rear is not secure.

233.s:
aśuddhapārṣṇirbalavān dvaidhībhāvaṃ samāśrayet /
balinā vigṛhītastu(2) yo 'sandehena pārthivaḥ //
233.d:
अशुद्धपार्ष्णिर्बलवान् द्वैधीभावं समाश्रयेत् /
बलिना विगृहीतस्तु(2) यो ऽसन्देहेन पार्थिवः //
233.m: If powerful but with his rear insecure, he should resort to duplicity. / But that monarch who is undoubtedly assailed by a stronger foe,

233.s:
saṃśrayastena vaktavyo guṇānāmadhamo guṇaḥ /
:n
1 prāsādāgre pradarśayediti ṭa..
2 vigṛhītastu iti kha..
:p 347
bahukṣayavyayāyāsaṃ(1) teṣāṃ yānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
233.d:
संश्रयस्तेन वक्तव्यो गुणानामधमो गुणः /
:न्
1 प्रासादाग्रे प्रदर्शयेदिति ट..
2 विगृहीतस्तु इति ख..
:प् 347
बहुक्षयव्ययायासं(1) तेषां यानं प्रकीर्तितं //
233.m:
should adopt seeking refuge, which is said to be the lowest among the measures of policy.
[...]
1 'should display upon the top of a temple' in manuscript ṭa.
2 'vigṛhītastu' in manuscript kha. / [Page 347]
Marching for them is proclaimed to entail great loss, expense, and effort.

233.s:
bahulābhakaraṃ paścāttadā rājā samāśrayet(2) /
sarvaśaktivihīnastu tadā kuryāttu saṃśrayaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe upāyaṣaḍguṇādirnāma
trayastriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catustriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
prātyahikarājakarma
233.d:
बहुलाभकरं पश्चात्तदा राजा समाश्रयेत्(2) /
सर्वशक्तिविहीनस्तु तदा कुर्यात्तु संश्रयं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे उपायषड्गुणादिर्नाम
त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुस्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
प्रात्यहिकराजकर्म
233.m:
When it brings great gain afterward, only then should the king undertake it. / But one completely bereft of all power should then seek refuge.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-third chapter, named 'Means, the Six Measures of Policy, and Other Matters', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirty-fourth chapter:
Daily Duties of the King

234.s:
puṣkara uvāca
ajasraṃ karma vakṣyāmi dinaṃ prati yadācaret /
dvimuhūrtāvaśeṣāyāṃ rātrau nidrāntyajennṛpaḥ //
234.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
अजस्रं कर्म वक्ष्यामि दिनं प्रति यदाचरेत् /
द्विमुहूर्तावशेषायां रात्रौ निद्रान्त्यजेन्नृपः //
234.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare the perpetual duty which he should perform day by day. / When two muhūrtas remain of the night, the king should abandon sleep.

234.s:
vādyavandisvanair gītaiḥ paśyed gūḍhāṃstato narān /
vijñāyate na ye lokāstadīyā iti kenacit //
234.d:
वाद्यवन्दिस्वनैर् गीतैः पश्येद् गूढांस्ततो नरान् /
विज्ञायते न ये लोकास्तदीया इति केनचित् //
234.m: Awakened by the sounds of musical instruments, bards, and songs, he should then interview secret agents, / men whom no people recognize as belonging to him.

234.s:
āyavyayasya śravaṇaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ yathāvidhi /
vegotsargaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā rājā snānagṛhaṃ vrajet //
234.d:
आयव्ययस्य श्रवणं ततः कार्यं यथाविधि /
वेगोत्सर्गं ततः कृत्वा राजा स्नानगृहं व्रजेत् //
234.m: Then hearing the report of income and expenditure should be done according to rule. / Having then relieved himself, the king should go to the bathhouse.

234.s:
snānaṃ kuryānnṛpaḥ paścāddantadhāvanapūrvakaṃ /
kṛtvā sandhyāntato japyaṃ vāsudevaṃ prapūjayet //
234.d:
स्नानं कुर्यान्नृपः पश्चाद्दन्तधावनपूर्वकं /
कृत्वा सन्ध्यान्ततो जप्यं वासुदेवं प्रपूजयेत् //
234.m: The king should take his bath after first cleansing his teeth. / Having performed the twilight devotion followed by recitation, he should worship Vāsudeva.

234.s:
vahnau pavitrān juhuyāt tarpayedudakaiḥ pitṝn /
:n
1 bahukṣayavyayāyāmiti kha.. , cha.. , ṭa.. ca
2 āsīnaḥ karmavicchedamityādiḥ, rājā samāśrayedityantaḥ
pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake nāsti
:p 348
dadyātsakāñcīṃ dhenuṃ dvijāśīrvādasaṃyutaḥ //
234.d:
वह्नौ पवित्रान् जुहुयात् तर्पयेदुदकैः पितॄन् /
:न्
1 बहुक्षयव्ययायामिति ख.. , छ.. , ट.. च
2 आसीनः कर्मविच्छेदमित्यादिः, राजा समाश्रयेदित्यन्तः
पाठः ज.. पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 348
दद्यात्सकाञ्चीं धेनुं द्विजाशीर्वादसंयुतः //
234.m:
He should offer sacred oblations in the fire and gratify the ancestors with water.
[...]
1 'bahukṣayavyayāyām' in manuscripts kha, cha, and ṭa.
2 The passage beginning with 'āsīnaḥ karmavicchedam' and ending with 'rājā samāśrayet' is missing in manuscript ja. / [Page 348]
Accompanied by the blessings of brāhmaṇas, he should bestow a cow adorned with a golden ornament.

234.s:
anulipto 'laṅkṛtaś ca mukhaṃ paśyecca darpaṇe /
sasuvarṇe dhṛte rājā śṛṇuyāddivasādikaṃ //
234.d:
अनुलिप्तो ऽलङ्कृतश् च मुखं पश्येच्च दर्पणे /
ससुवर्णे धृते राजा शृणुयाद्दिवसादिकं //
234.m: Anointed and adorned, he should look at his face in a mirror / and in clarified butter containing gold; the king should hear [the astrological data of] the day and so forth.

234.s:
auṣadhaṃ bhiṣajoktaṃ ca maṅgalālambhanañcaret /
paśced guruṃ tena dattāśīrvado 'tha vrajetsabhāṃ //
234.d:
औषधं भिषजोक्तं च मङ्गलालम्भनञ्चरेत् /
पश्चेद् गुरुं तेन दत्ताशीर्वदो ऽथ व्रजेत्सभां //
234.m: He should take medicine prescribed by the physician and touch auspicious objects. / He should see his guru, and receiving his blessing, he should then proceed to the assembly hall.

234.s:
tatrastho brāhmaṇān paśyedamātyānmantriṇas tathā /
prakṛtīś ca mahābhāga pratīhāraniveditāḥ //
234.d:
तत्रस्थो ब्राह्मणान् पश्येदमात्यान्मन्त्रिणस् तथा /
प्रकृतीश् च महाभाग प्रतीहारनिवेदिताः //
234.m: Stationed there, O noble one, he should receive brāhmaṇas, ministers, and counselors, / as well as subjects announced by the door-keeper.

234.s:
śrutvetihāsaṃ kāryāṇi kāryāṇāṃ kāryanirṇayam /
vyavahārantataḥ paśyenmantraṃ kuryāttu mantribhiḥ //
234.d:
श्रुत्वेतिहासं कार्याणि कार्याणां कार्यनिर्णयम् /
व्यवहारन्ततः पश्येन्मन्त्रं कुर्यात्तु मन्त्रिभिः //
234.m: Having listened to historical narratives, state affairs, and the resolution of affairs, / he should then inspect legal proceedings and hold counsel with his counselors.

234.s:
naikena sahitaḥ kuryānna kuryādbahubhiḥ saha /
na ca mūrkhair nacānāptair guptaṃ na prakaṭaṃ caret(1) //
234.d:
नैकेन सहितः कुर्यान्न कुर्याद्बहुभिः सह /
न च मूर्खैर् नचानाप्तैर् गुप्तं न प्रकटं चरेत्(1) //
234.m: He should not deliberate with one alone, nor should he deliberate with many, / nor with fools, nor with untrustworthy persons; he should keep it secret, not make it public.

234.s:
mantraṃ svadhiṣṭhitaṃ kuryādyena rāṣṭraṃ na bādhate /
ākāragrahaṇe rājño mantrarakṣā parā matā(2) //
234.d:
मन्त्रं स्वधिष्ठितं कुर्याद्येन राष्ट्रं न बाधते /
आकारग्रहणे राज्ञो मन्त्ररक्षा परा मता(2) //
234.m: He should conduct counsel firmly founded, whereby his kingdom suffers no harm. / In guarding against the apprehension of intent, the preservation of counsel is considered paramount.

234.s:
ākārair iṅgitaiḥ prajñā mantraṃ gṛhṇanti paṇḍitāḥ /
sāṃvatsarāṇāṃ vaidyānāṃ mantriṇāṃ vacane rataḥ //
234.d:
आकारैर् इङ्गितैः प्रज्ञा मन्त्रं गृह्णन्ति पण्डिताः /
सांवत्सराणां वैद्यानां मन्त्रिणां वचने रतः //
234.m: Clever, learned men deduce counsel through physical demeanor and subtle gestures. / Devoted to the counsel of astrologers, physicians, and ministers,

234.s:
rājā vibhūtimāpnoti(3) dhārayanti nṛpaṃ hi te /
mantraṃ kṛtvātha vyāyāmañcakre yāne ca śastrake //
234.d:
राजा विभूतिमाप्नोति(3) धारयन्ति नृपं हि ते /
मन्त्रं कृत्वाथ व्यायामञ्चक्रे याने च शस्त्रके //
234.m: a king attains prosperity, for they uphold the monarch. / Having concluded counsel, [he should engage in] exercise with the discus, vehicle, and weapons.

234.s:
niḥsattvādau nṛpaḥ snātaḥ paśyedviṣṇuṃ supūjitaṃ /
hutañca pāvakaṃ paśyedviprān paśyetsupūjitān //
:n
1 guptaṃ cāprakaṭaṃ carediti ga.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
2 ākāra grahaṇe rājño mantrarakṣā parā matā ity asya sthāne
ākāreṅgitatattvajñaḥ kāryākāryavicakṣaṇa iti ṭa..
pustakapāṭhaḥ
3 rājādhibhūtimāpnotīti ja..
:p 349
234.d:
निःसत्त्वादौ नृपः स्नातः पश्येद्विष्णुं सुपूजितं /
हुतञ्च पावकं पश्येद्विप्रान् पश्येत्सुपूजितान् //
:न्
1 गुप्तं चाप्रकटं चरेदिति ग.. , ज.. , ट.. च
2 आकार ग्रहणे राज्ञो मन्त्ररक्षा परा मता इत्य् अस्य स्थाने
आकारेङ्गिततत्त्वज्ञः कार्याकार्यविचक्षण इति ट..
पुस्तकपाठः
3 राजाधिभूतिमाप्नोतीति ज..
:प् 349
234.m:
When fatigue and other feelings are gone, the bathed king should see well-worshiped Viṣṇu, / see the sacrificial fire into which offerings have been made, and see well-honored brāhmaṇas.
[...]
[Variant reading note:] Manuscripts ga, ja, and ṭa read: “guptaṃ cāprakaṭaṃ caret”.
[Variant reading note:] In place of “ākāra grahaṇe rājño mantrarakṣā parā matā”, the reading in manuscript ṭa is: “ākāreṅgitatattvajñaḥ kāryākāryavicakṣaṇaḥ”.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscript ja reads: “rājādhibhūtimāpnoti”.

234.s:
bhūṣito bhojanaṅkuryād dānādyaiḥ suparīkṣitaṃ /
bhuktvā gṛhītatāmbūlo vāmapārśvena saṃsthitaḥ(1) //
234.d:
भूषितो भोजनङ्कुर्याद् दानाद्यैः सुपरीक्षितं /
भुक्त्वा गृहीतताम्बूलो वामपार्श्वेन संस्थितः(1) //
234.m: Adorned, he should take food that has been carefully tested by gifts [to animals] and other means; / having eaten and taken betel, he should rest lying on his left side.

234.s:
śāstrāṇi cintayed dṛṣṭvā yodhān koṣṭhāyudhaṃ gṛhaṃ /
anvāsya paścimāṃ sandhyāṃ kāryāṇi ca vicintya tu //
234.d:
शास्त्राणि चिन्तयेद् दृष्ट्वा योधान् कोष्ठायुधं गृहं /
अन्वास्य पश्चिमां सन्ध्यां कार्याणि च विचिन्त्य तु //
234.m: He should reflect upon the treatises; having inspected his warriors, the storehouse, and the arsenal, / and having attended to the evening twilight worship and deliberated upon state affairs,

234.s:
carān sampreṣya bhuktānnamantaḥpuracaro bhavet /
vādyagītair akṣito 'nyair evannityañcarennṛpaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe ājasrikaṃ nāma
catustriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
raṇadīkṣā
234.d:
चरान् सम्प्रेष्य भुक्तान्नमन्तःपुरचरो भवेत् /
वाद्यगीतैर् अक्षितो ऽन्यैर् एवन्नित्यञ्चरेन्नृपः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे आजस्रिकं नाम
चतुस्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
रणदीक्षा
234.m:
and having dispatched his spies, after taking his evening meal he should enter the inner apartments. / Entertained with instrumental music, singing, and other arts, the king should conduct his daily routine thus.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-fourth chapter, entitled “Daily Routine,” in the great Agnipurāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirty-fifth chapter.
Consecration for Battle

235.s:
puṣkara uvāca
yātrāvidhānapūrvantu vakṣye sāṅgrāmikaṃ vidhiṃ /
saptāhena yadā yātrā bhaviṣyati mahīpateḥ //
235.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
यात्राविधानपूर्वन्तु वक्ष्ये साङ्ग्रामिकं विधिं /
सप्ताहेन यदा यात्रा भविष्यति महीपतेः //
235.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall explain the martial rule following the procedure for an expedition. / When the expedition of the king is to take place in seven days,

235.s:
pūjanīyo hariḥ śambhurmodakādyair vināyakaḥ /
dvitīye 'hani dikpālān sampūjya śayanañcaret //
235.d:
पूजनीयो हरिः शम्भुर्मोदकाद्यैर् विनायकः /
द्वितीये ऽहनि दिक्पालान् सम्पूज्य शयनञ्चरेत् //
235.m: Hari, Śambhu, and Vināyaka are to be worshipped with sweets and other offerings. / On the second day, having fully worshipped the guardians of the directions, he should lie down to sleep.

235.s:
śayyāyāṃ vā tadagre 'tha devān prārcya manuṃ smaret /
namaḥ śambhoḥ trinetrāya rudrāya varadāya ca //
235.d:
शय्यायां वा तदग्रे ऽथ देवान् प्रार्च्य मनुं स्मरेत् /
नमः शम्भोः त्रिनेत्राय रुद्राय वरदाय च //
235.m: Either upon his bed or before it, having worshipped the gods, he should recall the mantra: / “Obeisance to Śambhu, the three-eyed Rudra, the granter of boons,

235.s:
vāmanāya virūpāya svapnādhipataye namaḥ /
:n
1 saṃviśediti ja..
:p 350
bhagavandevadeveśa śūlabhṛdvṛṣavāhana //
235.d:
वामनाय विरूपाय स्वप्नाधिपतये नमः /
:न्
1 संविशेदिति ज..
:प् 350
भगवन्देवदेवेश शूलभृद्वृषवाहन //
235.m:
the dwarf, the misshapen one, the lord of dreams, obeisance!
[...]
[Variant reading note:] Manuscript ja reads: “saṃviśet”.
O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods, bearer of the trident, whose mount is the bull!

235.s:
iṣṭāniṣṭe mamācakṣva svapne suptasya śāśvata /
yajjāgrato dūramiti purodhā mantramuccaret //
235.d:
इष्टानिष्टे ममाचक्ष्व स्वप्ने सुप्तस्य शाश्वत /
यज्जाग्रतो दूरमिति पुरोधा मन्त्रमुच्चरेत् //
235.m: Tell me, who am asleep, the auspicious and inauspicious in a dream, O Eternal One!” / The royal priest should utter the mantra beginning with “yajjāgrato dūram”.

235.s:
tṛtīye 'hani dikpālān rudrāṃstān dikpatīnyajet /
grahān yajeccaturthe 'hni pañcame cāśvinau yajet //
235.d:
तृतीये ऽहनि दिक्पालान् रुद्रांस्तान् दिक्पतीन्यजेत् /
ग्रहान् यजेच्चतुर्थे ऽह्नि पञ्चमे चाश्विनौ यजेत् //
235.m: On the third day he should worship the guardians of the directions, the Rudras, and those regents of the quarters; / he should worship the planets on the fourth day, and on the fifth day he should worship the two Aśvins.

235.s:
mārge yā devatāstāsānnadyādīnāñca pūjanaṃ /
divyāntarīkṣabhaumasthadevānāñca tathā baliḥ //
235.d:
मार्गे या देवतास्तासान्नद्यादीनाञ्च पूजनं /
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमस्थदेवानाञ्च तथा बलिः //
235.m: There should be worship of those deities on the path, and of rivers and the like, / as well as an oblation to the celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial deities.

235.s:
rātrau bhūtagaṇānāñca vāsudevādipūjanaṃ /
bhadrakālyāḥ śriyaḥ kuryāt prārthayet sarvadevatāḥ //
235.d:
रात्रौ भूतगणानाञ्च वासुदेवादिपूजनं /
भद्रकाल्याः श्रियः कुर्यात् प्रार्थयेत् सर्वदेवताः //
235.m: At night, he should perform worship of the host of spirits, of Vāsudeva and others, / of Bhadrakālī, and of Śrī, and he should pray to all the deities:

235.s:
vāsudevaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ pradyumnaścāniruddhakaḥ /
nārāyaṇo 'bjajo viṣṇur nārasiṃho varāhakaḥ //
235.d:
वासुदेवः सङ्कर्षणः प्रद्युम्नश्चानिरुद्धकः /
नारायणो ऽब्जजो विष्णुर् नारसिंहो वराहकः //
235.m: “Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha; / Nārāyaṇa, the lotus-born [Brahmā], Viṣṇu, Nārasiṃha, Varāha;

235.s:
śiva īśastatpuruṣo(1) hy aghoro rāma satyajaḥ(2) /
sūryaḥ somaḥ kujaścāndrijīvaśukraśanaiś carāḥ //
235.d:
शिव ईशस्तत्पुरुषो(1) ह्य् अघोरो राम सत्यजः(2) /
सूर्यः सोमः कुजश्चान्द्रिजीवशुक्रशनैश् चराः //
235.m: Śiva, Īśa, Tatpuruṣa, indeed Aghora, Rāma, and Satyaja; / the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn;

235.s:
rāhuḥ keturgaṇapatiḥ senānī caṇḍikā hy umā /
lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī durgā brahmāṇīpramukhā gaṇāḥ //
235.d:
राहुः केतुर्गणपतिः सेनानी चण्डिका ह्य् उमा /
लक्ष्मीः सरस्वती दुर्गा ब्रह्माणीप्रमुखा गणाः //
235.m: Rāhu, Ketu, Gaṇapati, Senānī [Kārttikeya], Caṇḍikā, and Umā; / Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Durgā, and the hosts headed by Brahmāṇī;

235.s:
rudrā indrādayo vahnir nāgāstārkṣyo 'pare surāḥ /
divyāntarīkṣabhūmiṣṭhā vijayāya bhavantu me //
235.d:
रुद्रा इन्द्रादयो वह्निर् नागास्तार्क्ष्यो ऽपरे सुराः /
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभूमिष्ठा विजयाय भवन्तु मे //
235.m: the Rudras, the deities headed by Indra, Agni, the serpents, Garuḍa, and the other gods, / residing in heaven, the atmosphere, and on earth—may they grant me victory!

235.s:
mardayantu raṇe śatrūn(3) sampragṛhyopahārakaṃ /
saputramātṛbhṛtyo 'haṃ(4) devā vaḥ śaraṇaṅgataḥ //
:n
1 tatpurata iti kha..
2 rātrāvityādiḥ, satyaja ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ ga.. pustake nāsti
3 mardayantu ca me śatrūniti gha.. , ña.. ca
4 avantu māṃ svabhṛtyo 'hamiti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 351
235.d:
मर्दयन्तु रणे शत्रून्(3) सम्प्रगृह्योपहारकं /
सपुत्रमातृभृत्यो ऽहं(4) देवा वः शरणङ्गतः //
:न्
1 तत्पुरत इति ख..
2 रात्रावित्यादिः, सत्यज इत्य् अन्तः पाठः ग.. पुस्तके नास्ति
3 मर्दयन्तु च मे शत्रूनिति घ.. , ञ.. च
4 अवन्तु मां स्वभृत्यो ऽहमिति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 351
235.m:
May they crush my enemies in battle, having accepted this offering! / With my sons, mother, and servants, O gods, I have sought refuge in you.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscript kha reads: “tatpurataḥ”.
[Variant reading note:] The passage beginning with “rātrau” up to “satyajaḥ” is missing in manuscript ga.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscripts gha and ña read: “mardayantu ca me śatrūn”.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscripts ja and ṭa read: “avantu māṃ svabhṛtyo ’ham”.

235.s:
cāmūnāṃ pṛṣṭhato gatvā ripunāśā namo 'stu vaḥ(1) /
vinivṛttaḥ pradāsyāmi(2) dattādabhyadhikaṃ baliṃ //
235.d:
चामूनां पृष्ठतो गत्वा रिपुनाशा नमो ऽस्तु वः(1) /
विनिवृत्तः प्रदास्यामि(2) दत्तादभ्यधिकं बलिं //
235.m: Following behind the armies, O destroyers of enemies, obeisance to you! / When I have returned [victorious], I shall offer an oblation greater than that already given.”

235.s:
ṣaṣṭhe 'hni vijayasnānaṃ kartavyaṃ cābhiṣekavat /
yātrādine saptame ca pūjayecca trivikramaṃ //
235.d:
षष्ठे ऽह्नि विजयस्नानं कर्तव्यं चाभिषेकवत् /
यात्रादिने सप्तमे च पूजयेच्च त्रिविक्रमं //
235.m: On the sixth day, the victorious bath is to be performed like an aspersion; / and on the seventh day, the day of departure, he should worship Trivikrama.

235.s:
nīrājanoktamantraiś ca āyudhaṃ vāhanaṃ yajet /
puṇyāhajayaśabdena mantrametanniśāmayet //
235.d:
नीराजनोक्तमन्त्रैश् च आयुधं वाहनं यजेत् /
पुण्याहजयशब्देन मन्त्रमेतन्निशामयेत् //
235.m: With mantras prescribed for lustration, he should worship his weapon and mount. / Accompanied by the cry of an auspicious day and the shout of victory, he should listen to this mantra:

235.s:
divyāntarīkṣabhūmiṣṭhāḥ santvāyurdāḥ surāś ca te /
devasiddhiṃ prāpnuhi tvaṃ devayātrāstu(3) sā tava //
235.d:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभूमिष्ठाः सन्त्वायुर्दाः सुराश् च ते /
देवसिद्धिं प्राप्नुहि त्वं देवयात्रास्तु(3) सा तव //
235.m: “May the gods residing in heaven, the atmosphere, and on earth grant you long life! / May you attain divine success, and may this divine expedition be yours!

235.s:
rakṣantu devatāḥ sarvā iti śrutvā nṛpo vrajet /
gṛhītvā saśarañcāpaṃ dhanurnāgeti mantrata //
235.d:
रक्षन्तु देवताः सर्वा इति श्रुत्वा नृपो व्रजेत् /
गृहीत्वा सशरञ्चापं धनुर्नागेति मन्त्रत //
235.m: May all the deities protect [you]!” Hearing this, the king should set out. / Having taken up his bow and arrows with the mantra “dhanurnāga…,”

235.s:
tadviṣṇoriti japtvātha dadyādripumukhe padaṃ /
dakṣiṇaṃ padaṃ dvātriṃśaddikṣu prācyādiṣu kramāt //
235.d:
तद्विष्णोरिति जप्त्वाथ दद्याद्रिपुमुखे पदं /
दक्षिणं पदं द्वात्रिंशद्दिक्षु प्राच्यादिषु क्रमात् //
235.m: and then having muttered the mantra “tad viṣṇoḥ…,” he should step toward the direction of the enemy, / taking thirty-two steps with his right foot in the directions starting with the east successively.

235.s:
nāgaṃ rathaṃ hayañcaiva dhuryāṃś caivāruhet kramāt /
āruhya vādyair gacchet pṛṣthato nāvalokayet //
235.d:
नागं रथं हयञ्चैव धुर्यांश् चैवारुहेत् क्रमात् /
आरुह्य वाद्यैर् गच्छेत् पृष्थतो नावलोकयेत् //
235.m: He should mount his elephant, chariot, horse, and draft animals in order; / having mounted, he should proceed with musical instruments and should not look back.

235.s:
krośamātraṃ gatastiṣṭhet pūjayeddevatā dvijān /
paradeśaṃ vrajet paścādātmasainyaṃ hi pālayan //
235.d:
क्रोशमात्रं गतस्तिष्ठेत् पूजयेद्देवता द्विजान् /
परदेशं व्रजेत् पश्चादात्मसैन्यं हि पालयन् //
235.m: Having gone a single krośa, he should halt and worship the deities and Brahmins. / Thereafter he should enter foreign territory, protecting his own army.

235.s:
rājā prāpya deveśantu(4) deśapālantu pālayet(5) /
devānāṃ pūjanaṃ kuryānna chindyādāyamatra tu //
235.d:
राजा प्राप्य देवेशन्तु(4) देशपालन्तु पालयेत्(5) /
देवानां पूजनं कुर्यान्न छिन्द्यादायमत्र तु //
235.m: The king, having honoured the lord of the gods, should protect the local guardian; / he should perform worship of the deities and must not cut off their revenue here.

235.s:
nāvamānayettaddeśyānāgatya svapuraṃ punaḥ /
:n
1 camūnāṃ pṛṣṭhaś caiva ripunāśo bhavedyatheti ṭa..
2 jitvā śatruṃ pradāsyāmīti ṭa..
3 jaitrā yātrāstviti ṭa..
4 prāptavideśastu iti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
5 deśācārantu pālayediti kha.. / deśācāraṇeṇa pālayediti ga.. , gha.. ,
cha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 352
jayaṃ prāpyārcayeddevān dadyāddānāni pārthivaḥ //
235.d:
नावमानयेत्तद्देश्यानागत्य स्वपुरं पुनः /
:न्
1 चमूनां पृष्ठश् चैव रिपुनाशो भवेद्यथेति ट..
2 जित्वा शत्रुं प्रदास्यामीति ट..
3 जैत्रा यात्रास्त्विति ट..
4 प्राप्तविदेशस्तु इति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
5 देशाचारन्तु पालयेदिति ख.. / देशाचारणेण पालयेदिति ग.. , घ.. ,
छ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 352
जयं प्राप्यार्चयेद्देवान् दद्याद्दानानि पार्थिवः //
235.m:
He should not disrespect the inhabitants of that land, and having returned again to his own city,
[Variant reading note:] Manuscript ṭa reads: “camūnāṃ pṛṣṭhaś caiva ripunāśo bhavedyathā”.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscript ṭa reads: “jitvā śatruṃ pradāsyāmi”.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscript ṭa reads: “jaitrā yātrāstviti”.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscripts ga, gha, and ña read: “prāptavideśastu”.
[Variant reading note:] Manuscript kha reads: “deśācārantu pālayet”; manuscripts ga, gha, cha, ja, and ña read: “deśācāraṇeṇa pālayet”.
having achieved victory, the ruler of the earth should worship the gods and bestow gifts.

235.s:
dvitīye ahani saṅgrāmo bhaviṣyati yadā tadā /
snapayedgajamaśvādi yajeddevaṃ nṛpasiṃhakaṃ //
235.d:
द्वितीये अहनि सङ्ग्रामो भविष्यति यदा तदा /
स्नपयेद्गजमश्वादि यजेद्देवं नृपसिंहकं //
235.m: When battle is to take place on the second day, / then he should bathe the elephants, horses, and others, and worship the deity Nṛsiṃha.

235.s:
chatrādirājaliṅgāni śastrāṇi niśi vai gaṇān /
prātarnṛsiṃhakaṃ pūjya vāhanādyamaśeṣataḥ //
235.d:
छत्रादिराजलिङ्गानि शस्त्राणि निशि वै गणान् /
प्रातर्नृसिंहकं पूज्य वाहनाद्यमशेषतः //
235.m: [He should worship] the royal emblems such as the umbrella, the weapons, and at night the attendants [of Śiva]; / in the morning, having worshipped Nṛsiṃha, his mounts, and everything else,

235.s:
purodhasā hutaṃ paśyedvahniṃ hutvā dvijānyajet /
gṛhītvā saśarañcāpaṃ gajādyāruhya vai vrajet //
235.d:
पुरोधसा हुतं पश्येद्वह्निं हुत्वा द्विजान्यजेत् /
गृहीत्वा सशरञ्चापं गजाद्यारुह्य वै व्रजेत् //
235.m: he should behold the fire offered by the royal priest; having offered fire oblations, he should honour Brahmins. / Having taken up his bow and arrows, and having mounted an elephant or other conveyance, he should set out.

235.s:
deśe tvadṛśyaḥ śatrūṇāṃ kuryāt prakṛtikalpanāṃ /
saṃhatān yodhayedalpān kāmaṃ vistārayedbahūn //
235.d:
देशे त्वदृश्यः शत्रूणां कुर्यात् प्रकृतिकल्पनां /
संहतान् योधयेदल्पान् कामं विस्तारयेद्बहून् //
235.m: Invisible to the enemies in that land, he should arrange his forces; / he should fight few troops in compact formation, but may spread out many at will.

235.s:
sūcīmukhamanīkaṃ syādalpānāṃ bahubhiḥ saha /
vyūhāḥ prāṇyaṅgarūpāś ca dravyarūpāś ca kīrtitāḥ //
235.d:
सूचीमुखमनीकं स्यादल्पानां बहुभिः सह /
व्यूहाः प्राण्यङ्गरूपाश् च द्रव्यरूपाश् च कीर्तिताः //
235.m: A needle-pointed array should be formed by few against many. / Battle arrays are declared to have the form of living beings' limbs and of inanimate objects:

235.s:
garuḍo makaravyūhaś cakraḥ śyenastathaiva ca /
ardhacandraś ca vajraś ca śakaṭavyūha eva ca //
235.d:
गरुडो मकरव्यूहश् चक्रः श्येनस्तथैव च /
अर्धचन्द्रश् च वज्रश् च शकटव्यूह एव च //
235.m: the eagle array, the sea-monster array, the wheel, and likewise the hawk, / the crescent, the thunderbolt, and the cart array;

235.s:
maṇḍalaḥ sarvatobhadraḥ sūcīvyūhaś ca te narāḥ /
vyūhānāmatha sarveṣāṃ pañcadhā sainyakalpanā //
235.d:
मण्डलः सर्वतोभद्रः सूचीव्यूहश् च ते नराः /
व्यूहानामथ सर्वेषां पञ्चधा सैन्यकल्पना //
235.m: the circle, the auspicious-on-all-sides, and the needle array, O men! / Now, the army arrangement of all arrays is fivefold:

235.s:
dvau pakṣāvanupakṣau dvāvaśyaṃ pañcamaṃ bhavet /
ekena yadi vā dvābhyāṃ bhāgābhyāṃ yuddhamācaret //
235.d:
द्वौ पक्षावनुपक्षौ द्वावश्यं पञ्चमं भवेत् /
एकेन यदि वा द्वाभ्यां भागाभ्यां युद्धमाचरेत् //
235.m: two wings, two flanks, and the fifth must be the reserve centre. / If he engages in battle with one or two divisions,

235.s:
bhāgatrayaṃ sthāpayettu teṣāṃ rakṣārthameva ca /
na vyūhakalpanā kāryā rājño bhavati karhicit //
235.d:
भागत्रयं स्थापयेत्तु तेषां रक्षार्थमेव च /
न व्यूहकल्पना कार्या राज्ञो भवति कर्हिचित् //
235.m: he should station three divisions specifically for their protection. / A formation of the battle array should never be undertaken by the king [in person].

235.s:
mūlacchede vināśaḥ syānna yudhyecca svayannṛpaḥ /
sainyasya paścāttiṣṭhettu krośamātre mahīpatiḥ //
235.d:
मूलच्छेदे विनाशः स्यान्न युध्येच्च स्वयन्नृपः /
सैन्यस्य पश्चात्तिष्ठेत्तु क्रोशमात्रे महीपतिः //
235.m: If the root is cut down, destruction follows, so the king should not fight himself; / the ruler of the earth should remain a single krośa behind the army.

235.s:
bhagnasandhāraṇaṃ tatra yodhānāṃ parikīrtitaṃ /
pradhānabhaṅge sainyasya nāśasthānaṃ vidhīyate //
:p 353
235.d:
भग्नसन्धारणं तत्र योधानां परिकीर्तितं /
प्रधानभङ्गे सैन्यस्य नाशस्थानं विधीयते //
:प् 353
235.m:
The rally of broken warriors is said to take place there; / if the commander is broken, the place of destruction of the army is brought about.
[Page 353]

235.s:
na saṃhatānna viralānyodhān vyūhe prakalpayet /
āyudhānāntu sammardo yathā na syāt parasparaṃ //
235.d:
न संहतान्न विरलान्योधान् व्यूहे प्रकल्पयेत् /
आयुधानान्तु सम्मर्दो यथा न स्यात् परस्परं //
235.m: In a battle array, he should station warriors neither too close together nor too dispersed, / so that their weapons do not clash with one another.

235.s:
bhettukāmaḥ parānīkaṃ saṃhatair eva bhedayet /
bhedarakṣyāḥ pareṇāpi kartavyāḥ saṃhatās tathā //
235.d:
भेत्तुकामः परानीकं संहतैर् एव भेदयेत् /
भेदरक्ष्याः परेणापि कर्तव्याः संहतास् तथा //
235.m:
Desiring to break the enemy's army, one should break it only with compact [ranks];
compact [formations] must also be made so that they are protected from being broken by the enemy.

235.s:
vyūhaṃ bhedāvahaṃ kuryāt paravyūheṣu cecchayā /
gajasya pādarakṣārthāś catvārastu tathā dvija //
235.d:
व्यूहं भेदावहं कुर्यात् परव्यूहेषु चेच्छया /
गजस्य पादरक्षार्थाश् चत्वारस्तु तथा द्विज //
235.m:
One should fashion a formation that brings about division among enemy formations at will;
and four [men] are [stationed] for the purpose of protecting the feet of an elephant, O twice-born.

235.s:
rathasya cāśvāś catvāraḥ samāstasya ca carmiṇaḥ /
dhanvinaś carmibhistulyāḥ purastāccarmiṇo raṇe //
235.d:
रथस्य चाश्वाश् चत्वारः समास्तस्य च चर्मिणः /
धन्विनश् चर्मिभिस्तुल्याः पुरस्ताच्चर्मिणो रणे //
235.m:
And four horses are for a chariot, and as many shield-bearers;
archers equal to shield-bearers [are stationed], with the shield-bearers in front in battle.

235.s:
pṛṣṭhato dhanvinaḥ praścāddhanvinānturagā rathāḥ /
rathānāṃ kuñjarāḥ paścāddātavyāḥ pṛthivīkṣitā //
235.d:
पृष्ठतो धन्विनः प्रश्चाद्धन्विनान्तुरगा रथाः /
रथानां कुञ्जराः पश्चाद्दातव्याः पृथिवीक्षिता //
235.m:
Behind [them are] the archers; behind the archers, horses [and] chariots;
elephants are to be placed behind the chariots by the ruler of the earth.

235.s:
padātikuñjarāśvānāṃ dharmakāryaṃ prayatnataḥ /
śūrāḥ pramukhato deyāḥ skandhamātrapradarśanaṃ //
235.d:
पदातिकुञ्जराश्वानां धर्मकार्यं प्रयत्नतः /
शूराः प्रमुखतो देयाः स्कन्धमात्रप्रदर्शनं //
235.m:
The proper duty of infantry, elephants, and horses [should be carried out] with effort.
Heroes are to be placed at the very front; only the shoulder [of the ranks] should be displayed.

235.s:
kartavyaṃ bhīrusaṅghena śatruvidrāvakārakaṃ(1) /
dārayanti purastāttu na deyā bhīravaḥ puraḥ //
235.d:
कर्तव्यं भीरुसङ्घेन शत्रुविद्रावकारकं(1) /
दारयन्ति पुरस्तात्तु न देया भीरवः पुरः //
235.m:
That which puts the enemy to flight is to be done by the assembly of timid ones;
since they tear apart in front, the timid must not be placed in the front.

235.s:
protsāhantyeva raṇe bhīrūn śūrāḥ purasthitāḥ /
prāṃśavaḥ śakunāśāś ca ye cājihmekṣaṇā(2) narāḥ //
235.d:
प्रोत्साहन्त्येव रणे भीरून् शूराः पुरस्थिताः /
प्रांशवः शकुनाशाश् च ये चाजिह्मेक्षणा(2) नराः //
235.m:
Heroes stationed in the front indeed encourage the timid in battle.
Men who are tall, hawk-nosed, and straight-eyed,

235.s:
saṃhatabhrūyugāś caiva krodhanā kalahapriyāḥ /
nityahṛṣṭāḥ prahṛṣṭāś ca śūrā jñeyāś cakāminaḥ //
235.d:
संहतभ्रूयुगाश् चैव क्रोधना कलहप्रियाः /
नित्यहृष्टाः प्रहृष्टाश् च शूरा ज्ञेयाश् चकामिनः //
235.m:
with joined eyebrows, wrathful, fond of strife,
constantly cheerful, exhilarated, and passionate are to be known as heroes.

235.s:
saṃhatānāṃ hatānāṃ ca raṇāpanayanakriyā(3) /
pratiyuddhaṃ gajānāñca toyadānādikañca yat //
:n
1 śatrudrāvakāraṇamiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
2 ye ca jihmekṣaṇā iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
3 valāpanayanakriyeti ja..
:p 354
235.d:
संहतानां हतानां च रणापनयनक्रिया(3) /
प्रतियुद्धं गजानाञ्च तोयदानादिकञ्च यत् //
:न्
1 शत्रुद्रावकारणमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
2 ये च जिह्मेक्षणा इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
3 वलापनयनक्रियेति ज..
:प् 354
235.m:
The work of removing from the battlefield the compact and the slain,
counter-combat of elephants, and the giving of water and the like,
[Notes]
1. "Putting the enemy to flight" (śatrudrāvakāraṇam) in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, and ña.
2. "And those who are crooked-eyed" (ye ca jihmekṣaṇāḥ) in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, and ña.
3. "The work of removing the army" (valāpanayanakriyā) in manuscript ja.
[Page 354]

235.s:
āyudhānayanaṃ caiva pattikarma vidhīyate /
ripūṇāṃ bhettukāmānāṃ svasainyasya tu rakṣaṇaṃ //
235.d:
आयुधानयनं चैव पत्तिकर्म विधीयते /
रिपूणां भेत्तुकामानां स्वसैन्यस्य तु रक्षणं //
235.m:
and the bringing of weapons—this is prescribed as the infantry's duty.
Protecting one's own army against enemies who wish to break through,

235.s:
bhedanaṃ saṃhatānāñca carmiṇāṃ karma kīrtitaṃ /
vimukhīkaraṇaṃ yuddhe dhanvināṃ ca tathocyate //
235.d:
भेदनं संहतानाञ्च चर्मिणां कर्म कीर्तितं /
विमुखीकरणं युद्धे धन्विनां च तथोच्यते //
235.m:
and breaking through the compact [ranks] is proclaimed the duty of shield-bearers;
and turning the enemy's back in battle is likewise said [to be the duty] of archers.

235.s:
dūrāpasaraṇaṃ yānaṃ suhatasya tathocyate /
trāsanaṃ ripusainyānāṃ rathakarma tathocyate //
235.d:
दूरापसरणं यानं सुहतस्य तथोच्यते /
त्रासनं रिपुसैन्यानां रथकर्म तथोच्यते //
235.m:
Retreating far away and charging are likewise said [to be the duty] of the well-struck [cavalry];
terrifying the enemy armies is likewise said to be the duty of chariots.

235.s:
bhedanaṃ saṃhatānāñca bhedānāmapi saṃhatiḥ /
prākāratoraṇāṭṭāladrumabhaṅgaś ca saṅgate //
235.d:
भेदनं संहतानाञ्च भेदानामपि संहतिः /
प्राकारतोरणाट्टालद्रुमभङ्गश् च सङ्गते //
235.m:
Breaking through compact [forces], uniting divided [forces],
and breaking walls, gateways, watchtowers, and trees in the encounter [is the duty of elephants].

235.s:
pattibhūrviṣamā jñeyā rathāśvasya tathā samā /
sakardamā ca nāgānāṃ yuddhabhūmirudāhṛtā //
235.d:
पत्तिभूर्विषमा ज्ञेया रथाश्वस्य तथा समा /
सकर्दमा च नागानां युद्धभूमिरुदाहृता //
235.m:
Uneven ground is to be known as [suitable] for infantry; similarly, flat [ground] for chariot and horse;
and muddy ground is declared the battleground for elephants.

235.s:
evaṃ viracitavyūhaḥ kṛtapṛṣṭhadivākaraḥ /
tathānulomaśukrārkidikpālamṛdumārutāḥ //
235.d:
एवं विरचितव्यूहः कृतपृष्ठदिवाकरः /
तथानुलोमशुक्रार्किदिक्पालमृदुमारुताः //
235.m:
Having thus arranged the battle array, keeping the sun to the back,
and likewise having Venus, Saturn, the guardians of the directions, and a gentle wind favorable,

235.s:
yodhānuttejayetsarvānnāmagotrāvadānataḥ /
bhogaprāptyā ca vijaye svargaprāptyā mṛtasya ca //
235.d:
योधानुत्तेजयेत्सर्वान्नामगोत्रावदानतः /
भोगप्राप्त्या च विजये स्वर्गप्राप्त्या मृतस्य च //
235.m:
he should inspire all the warriors by [mentioning their] name, lineage, and heroic deeds,
and by [promising] the attainment of worldly enjoyment in victory, and attainment of heaven if killed:

235.s:
jitvārīn bhogasamprāptiḥ mṛtasya ca parā gatiḥ /
niṣkṛtiḥ svāmipiṇḍasya nāsti yuddhasamā gatiḥ //
235.d:
जित्वारीन् भोगसम्प्राप्तिः मृतस्य च परा गतिः /
निष्कृतिः स्वामिपिण्डस्य नास्ति युद्धसमा गतिः //
235.m:
"Having conquered enemies, there is the attainment of worldly enjoyment; and for the slain, the supreme destination.
[Battle is] discharge of debt to the master's food; there is no destination equal to battle!

235.s:
śūrāṇāṃ raktamāyāti tena pāpantyajanti te /
dhātādiduḥkhasahanaṃ raṇe tat paramantapaḥ //
235.d:
शूराणां रक्तमायाति तेन पापन्त्यजन्ति ते /
धातादिदुःखसहनं रणे तत् परमन्तपः //
235.m:
The blood of heroes flows, and by that they cast off sin;
enduring pain from blows and wounds in battle, that is supreme ascetic austerity.

235.s:
varāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi yānti śūraṃ raṇe mṛtaṃ /
svāmī sukṛtamādatte bhagnānāṃ vinivartināṃ //
235.d:
वराप्सरःसहस्राणि यान्ति शूरं रणे मृतं /
स्वामी सुकृतमादत्ते भग्नानां विनिवर्तिनां //
235.m:
Thousands of choice celestial nymphs go to the hero slain in battle;
the master takes the good deeds of those who are broken and flee.

235.s:
brahmahatyāphalaṃ teṣāṃ tathā proktaṃ pade pade /
tyaktvā sahāyān yo gaccheddevāstasya vinaṣṭaye //
235.d:
ब्रह्महत्याफलं तेषां तथा प्रोक्तं पदे पदे /
त्यक्त्वा सहायान् यो गच्छेद्देवास्तस्य विनष्टये //
235.m:
The fruit of killing a brāhmaṇa is likewise declared for them at every step.
He who flees abandoning his companions, the gods [work] for his destruction!

235.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ proktaṃ śūrāṇāmanirvartināṃ /
:p 355
dharmaniṣṭhe jayo rājñi(1) yoddhavyāś ca samāḥ samaiḥ //
235.d:
अश्वमेधफलं प्रोक्तं शूराणामनिर्वर्तिनां /
:प् 355
धर्मनिष्ठे जयो राज्ञि(1) योद्धव्याश् च समाः समैः //
235.m:
The fruit of a horse sacrifice is declared for heroes who do not retreat."
[Page 355]
Victory belongs to the king steadfast in righteousness; and equals must fight with equals.

235.s:
gajādyaiś ca gajādyāś ca na hantavyāḥ palāyinaḥ /
na prekṣakāḥ praviṣṭāś ca aśastrāḥ pratitādayaḥ //
235.d:
गजाद्यैश् च गजाद्याश् च न हन्तव्याः पलायिनः /
न प्रेक्षकाः प्रविष्टाश् च अशस्त्राः प्रतितादयः //
235.m:
Elephants and the like [should fight] with elephants and the like; fleeing men must not be slain,
nor spectators, nor those who have entered [the camp], nor the weaponless, nor those who have fallen.

235.s:
śānte nidrābhibhūte ca ardhottīrṇe nadīvane /
durdine kūṭayuddhāni śatrunāśārthamācaret //
235.d:
शान्ते निद्राभिभूते च अर्धोत्तीर्णे नदीवने /
दुर्दिने कूटयुद्धानि शत्रुनाशार्थमाचरेत् //
235.m:
When [the enemy is] exhausted, overcome by sleep, half-crossed over a river or a forest,
or on a stormy day, one should practice deceitful warfare for the destruction of the enemy.

235.s:
bāhū pragṛhya vikrośedbhagnā bhagnāḥ pare iti /
prāptaṃ mitraṃ balaṃ bhūri nāyako 'tra nipātitaḥ //
235.d:
बाहू प्रगृह्य विक्रोशेद्भग्ना भग्नाः परे इति /
प्राप्तं मित्रं बलं भूरि नायको ऽत्र निपातितः //
235.m:
Raising his arms, he should shout: "Broken, the enemies are broken!
An allied force, vast in size, has arrived; the leader here has been struck down!

235.s:
senānīrnihatāścāyaṃ bhūpatiścāpi viplutaḥ /
vidrutānāntu yodhānāṃ mukhaṃ ghāto vidhīyate //
235.d:
सेनानीर्निहताश्चायं भूपतिश्चापि विप्लुतः /
विद्रुतानान्तु योधानां मुखं घातो विधीयते //
235.m:
The commander of the army has been slain, and the king too has fled!"
And striking down the faces of fleeing warriors is prescribed.

235.s:
dhūpāś ca deyā dharmajña tathā ca paramohanāḥ /
patākāś caiva sambhāro vāditrāṇām bhayāvahaḥ //
235.d:
धूपाश् च देया धर्मज्ञ तथा च परमोहनाः /
पताकाश् चैव सम्भारो वादित्राणाम् भयावहः //
235.m:
Incenses, O knower of righteousness, highly deluding, should also be applied,
and banners, and a fearsome display of musical instruments.

235.s:
samprāpya vijayaṃ yuddhe devānviprāṃś ca saṃyajet(2) /
ratnāni rājagāmīni amātyena kṛte raṇe //
235.d:
सम्प्राप्य विजयं युद्धे देवान्विप्रांश् च संयजेत्(2) /
रत्नानि राजगामीनि अमात्येन कृते रणे //
235.m:
Having obtained victory in battle, he should worship the gods and brāhmaṇas.
When the battle has been fought by a minister, jewels belong to the king.

235.s:
tasya striyo na kasyāpi rakṣyāstāś ca parasya ca /
śatruṃ prāpya raṇe muktaṃ putravat paripālayet //
235.d:
तस्य स्त्रियो न कस्यापि रक्ष्यास्ताश् च परस्य च /
शत्रुं प्राप्य रणे मुक्तं पुत्रवत् परिपालयेत् //
235.m:
His women [must be protected; they belong] to no one else, and those of the enemy must be protected.
Capturing an enemy in battle and releasing him, he should protect him like a son.

235.s:
punastena na yoddhavyaṃ deśācārādi pālayet /
tataś ca svapuraṃ prāpya dhruve bhe praviśed gṛhaṃ //
235.d:
पुनस्तेन न योद्धव्यं देशाचारादि पालयेत् /
ततश् च स्वपुरं प्राप्य ध्रुवे भे प्रविशेद् गृहं //
235.m:
He should not fight with him again; he should preserve the customs of the country and the like.
And then, having reached his own city under a fixed asterism, he should enter his palace.

235.s:
devādipūjanaṃ kuryādrakṣedyodhakuṭumbakaṃ /
saṃvibhāgaṃ prāvāptaiḥ kuryād bhṛtyajanasya ca //
235.d:
देवादिपूजनं कुर्याद्रक्षेद्योधकुटुम्बकं /
संविभागं प्रावाप्तैः कुर्याद् भृत्यजनस्य च //
235.m:
He should perform worship of the gods and others, and protect the families of his warriors;
and he should distribute [wealth] among his servants from what was obtained.

235.s:
raṇādīkṣā mayoktā te jayāya nṛpaterdhruvā /
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe raṇadīkṣā nāma
pañcatriṃaśadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 dharmaniṣṭho jayo nitya iti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 devān viprān gurūn yajediti gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 356
:ś atha ṣaṭtriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śrīstotraṃ
235.d:
रणादीक्षा मयोक्ता ते जयाय नृपतेर्ध्रुवा /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे रणदीक्षा नाम
पञ्चत्रिंअशधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 धर्मनिष्ठो जयो नित्य इति ख.. , छ.. च
2 देवान् विप्रान् गुरून् यजेदिति घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 356
:श् अथ षट्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
श्रीस्तोत्रं
235.m:
The battle initiation has been declared by me to you, which ensures victory for the king.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred thirty-fifth chapter, entitled "Battle Initiation" [is concluded].
[Notes]
1. "Victory is always for one steadfast in righteousness" (dharmaniṣṭho jayo nityaḥ) in manuscripts kha and cha.
2. "He should worship the gods, brāhmaṇas, and gurus" (devān viprān gurūn yajet) in manuscripts gha, ja, and ña.
[Page 356]
Now the two hundred thirty-sixth chapter.
Hymn of Praise to Śrī

236.s:
puṣkara uvāca
rājyalakṣmīsthiratvāya yathendreṇa purā śriyaḥ /
stutiḥ kṛtā tathā rājā jayārthaṃ stutimācaret //
236.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
राज्यलक्ष्मीस्थिरत्वाय यथेन्द्रेण पुरा श्रियः /
स्तुतिः कृता तथा राजा जयार्थं स्तुतिमाचरेत् //
236.m:
Puṣkara said:
Just as a hymn of praise to Śrī was formerly made by Indra for the stability of royal fortune,
even so a king should utter a hymn of praise for the sake of victory.

236.s:
indra uvāca
namasye sarvalokānāṃ(1) jananīmabdhisambhavāṃ(2) /
śriyamunnindrapadmākṣīṃ viṣṇuvakṣaḥsthalasthitāṃ //
236.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
नमस्ये सर्वलोकानां(1) जननीमब्धिसम्भवां(2) /
श्रियमुन्निन्द्रपद्माक्षीं विष्णुवक्षःस्थलस्थितां //
236.m:
Indra said:
I bow to Śrī, the mother of all worlds, born of the ocean,
having eyes like fully blossomed lotuses, dwelling on the chest of Viṣṇu.

236.s:
tvaṃ siddhistvaṃ svadhā svāhā sudhā tvaṃ lokapāvani /
sandhayā rātriḥ prabhā bhūtirmedhā śraddhā sarasvatī //
236.d:
त्वं सिद्धिस्त्वं स्वधा स्वाहा सुधा त्वं लोकपावनि /
सन्धया रात्रिः प्रभा भूतिर्मेधा श्रद्धा सरस्वती //
236.m:
You are accomplishment, you are svadhā, svāhā, [and] nectar, O purifier of the worlds!
Twilight, night, radiance, prosperity, intelligence, faith, Sarasvatī,

236.s:
yajñavidyā mahāvidyā guhyavidyā ca śobhane /
ātmavidyā ca devi tvaṃ vimuktiphaladāyinī //
236.d:
यज्ञविद्या महाविद्या गुह्यविद्या च शोभने /
आत्मविद्या च देवि त्वं विमुक्तिफलदायिनी //
236.m:
the knowledge of sacrifice, the great knowledge, the secret knowledge, O beautiful one,
and the knowledge of the Self are you, O goddess, the granter of the fruit of complete liberation!

236.s:
ānvīkṣikī trayī vārtā daṇḍanītistvameva ca /
saumyā saumyair jagadrūpaistvayaitaddevi pūritaṃ //
236.d:
आन्वीक्षिकी त्रयी वार्ता दण्डनीतिस्त्वमेव च /
सौम्या सौम्यैर् जगद्रूपैस्त्वयैतद्देवि पूरितं //
236.m:
Logic, the triple Veda, commerce, and the science of politics are you alone;
by you, gentle with gentle forms of the world, this [universe] has been filled, O goddess!

236.s:
kā tvanyā tvāmṛte devi sarvayajñamayaṃ vapuḥ /
adhyāste deva devasya yogicintyaṃ gadābhṛtaḥ //
236.d:
का त्वन्या त्वामृते देवि सर्वयज्ञमयं वपुः /
अध्यास्ते देव देवस्य योगिचिन्त्यं गदाभृतः //
236.m:
Who else indeed but you, O goddess, abides upon the body
of the God of gods, the bearer of the mace, which is comprised of all sacrifices and contemplated by yogins?

236.s:
tvayā devi parityaktaṃ sakalaṃ bhuvanatrayaṃ /
vinaṣṭaprāyamabhavat tvayedānīṃ samedhitaṃ //
236.d:
त्वया देवि परित्यक्तं सकलं भुवनत्रयं /
विनष्टप्रायमभवत् त्वयेदानीं समेधितं //
236.m:
When abandoned by you, O goddess, the entire triple world
became almost perished; it has now been made to flourish by you.

236.s:
dārāḥ putrās tathāgāraṃ suhṛddhānyadhanādikaṃ /
bhavatyetanmahābhāge nityaṃ tvadvīkṣaṇān nṛṇāṃ //
:n
1 sarvabhūtānāmiti gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
2 javanīmambusambhavāmiti ja..
:p 357
236.d:
दाराः पुत्रास् तथागारं सुहृद्धान्यधनादिकं /
भवत्येतन्महाभागे नित्यं त्वद्वीक्षणान् नृणां //
:न्
1 सर्वभूतानामिति घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
2 जवनीमम्बुसम्भवामिति ज..
:प् 357
236.m:
Wives, sons, likewise home, friends, grain, and wealth—
all this comes to men, O highly fortunate one, constantly from your glance.
[Notes]
1. "Of all beings" (sarvabhūtānām) in manuscripts gha, ja, and ña.
2. "Swift, water-born" (javanīmambusambhavām) in manuscript ja.
[Page 357]

236.s:
śarīrārogyamaiśvaryamaripakṣakṣayaḥ sukhaṃ(1) /
devi tvaddṛṣṭidṛṣṭānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ na durlabhaṃ //
236.d:
शरीरारोग्यमैश्वर्यमरिपक्षक्षयः सुखं(1) /
देवि त्वद्दृष्टिदृष्टानां पुरुषाणां न दुर्लभं //
236.m:
Bodily health, sovereignty, the destruction of enemy factions, [and] happiness,
O goddess, are not difficult to obtain for men who are looked upon by your gaze.

236.s:
tvamambā sarvabhūtānāṃ devadevo hariḥ pitā /
tvayaitadvoiṣṇunā cāmba jagadvyāptaṃ carācaraṃ //
236.d:
त्वमम्बा सर्वभूतानां देवदेवो हरिः पिता /
त्वयैतद्वोइष्णुना चाम्ब जगद्व्याप्तं चराचरं //
236.m:
You are the mother of all beings; the God of gods, Hari, is the father.
By you and by this Viṣṇu, O mother, the world, moving and unmoving, is pervaded.

236.s:
mānaṃ koṣaṃ tathā koṣṭhaṃ mā gṛhaṃ mā paricchadaṃ /
mā śarīraṃ kalatrañca tyajethāḥ sarvapāvani //
236.d:
मानं कोषं तथा कोष्ठं मा गृहं मा परिच्छदं /
मा शरीरं कलत्रञ्च त्यजेथाः सर्वपावनि //
236.m:
Do not abandon [our] honor, treasury, nor granary, not [our] house, not retinue,
not [our] body and wife, O purifier of all!

236.s:
mā putrānmāsuhṛdvargānmā paśūnmā vibhūṣaṇaṃ /
tyajethā mama devasya(2) viṣṇorvakṣaḥsthalālaye(3) //
236.d:
मा पुत्रान्मासुहृद्वर्गान्मा पशून्मा विभूषणं /
त्यजेथा मम देवस्य(2) विष्णोर्वक्षःस्थलालये(3) //
236.m: Do not abandon sons, nor circle of friends, nor cattle, nor ornaments, / O you whose abode is the chest of my god Viṣṇu!

236.s:
sattvena satyaśaucābhyāṃ tathā śīlādibhirguṇaiḥ /
tyajante te narā sadyaḥ santyaktā ye tvayāmale //
236.d:
सत्त्वेन सत्यशौचाभ्यां तथा शीलादिभिर्गुणैः /
त्यजन्ते ते नरा सद्यः सन्त्यक्ता ये त्वयामले //
236.m: Those men whom you abandon, O spotless one, are immediately abandoned / by goodness, truth, and ritual purity, and likewise by virtues such as good conduct.

236.s:
tvayāvalokitāḥ sadyaḥ śīlādyair akhilair guṇaiḥ /
kulaiśvaryaiś ca yujyante puruṣā nirguṇā api //
236.d:
त्वयावलोकिताः सद्यः शीलाद्यैर् अखिलैर् गुणैः /
कुलैश्वर्यैश् च युज्यन्ते पुरुषा निर्गुणा अपि //
236.m: Looked upon by you, even men devoid of virtues / are instantly endowed with all virtues such as good conduct, and with noble birth and sovereignty.

236.s:
sa ślāghyaḥ sa guṇī dhanyaḥ sa kulīnaḥ sa buddhimān /
sa śūraḥ sa ca vikrānto yastvayā devi vīkṣitaḥ //
236.d:
स श्लाघ्यः स गुणी धन्यः स कुलीनः स बुद्धिमान् /
स शूरः स च विक्रान्तो यस्त्वया देवि वीक्षितः //
236.m: He is praiseworthy, he is virtuous, fortunate, of noble lineage, and wise; / he is brave and valiant, who is looked upon by you, O goddess.

236.s:
sadyo vaiguṇyamāyānti śīlādyāḥ sakalā guṇāḥ /
parāṅmukhī jagaddhātrī yasya tvaṃ viṣṇuvallabhe //
236.d:
सद्यो वैगुण्यमायान्ति शीलाद्याः सकला गुणाः /
पराङ्मुखी जगद्धात्री यस्य त्वं विष्णुवल्लभे //
236.m: All virtues, beginning with good conduct, immediately become deficiencies / for him from whom you turn your face away, O sustainer of the world, beloved of Viṣṇu!

236.s:
na te varṇayituṃ śaktā guṇān jihvāpi vedhasaḥ /
prasīda devi padmākṣi nāsmāṃstyākṣīḥ kadācana //
236.d:
न ते वर्णयितुं शक्ता गुणान् जिह्वापि वेधसः /
प्रसीद देवि पद्माक्षि नास्मांस्त्याक्षीः कदाचन //
236.m: Even the tongue of the Creator is unable to describe your virtues. / Be gracious, O lotus-eyed goddess! Never forsake us!

236.s:
puṣkara uvāca
evaṃ stutā dadau śrīś ca varamindrāya cepsitaṃ /
susthiratvaṃ ca rājyasya saṅgrāmavijayādikaṃ //
:n
1 kṣayaḥ svayamiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , jha.. ca / kṣayaḥ śubhamiti
cha..
2 devadevasyeti ṭa..
3 vakṣaḥsthalāśraye iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 358
236.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
एवं स्तुता ददौ श्रीश् च वरमिन्द्राय चेप्सितं /
सुस्थिरत्वं च राज्यस्य सङ्ग्रामविजयादिकं //
:न्
1 क्षयः स्वयमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , झ.. च / क्षयः शुभमिति
छ..
2 देवदेवस्येति ट..
3 वक्षःस्थलाश्रये इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 358
236.m:
Puṣkara said: / Praised in this manner, Śrī granted Indra his desired boon: / enduring stability of his realm, victory in battle, and the like.
[Footnote]
1 'kṣayaḥ svayam' in kha, ga, gha, and jha; 'kṣayaḥ śubham' in cha.
2 'devadevasya' in ṭa.
3 'vakṣaḥsthalāśraye' in kha, ga, gha, and ña. / [Page 358]

236.s:
svastotrapāṭhaśravaṇakartṝṇāṃ bhuktimuktidaṃ /
śrīstotraṃ satataṃ tasmāt paṭhecca śṛṇuyānnaraḥ //
:e ity agneye mahāpurāṇe śrīstotraṃ nāma
ṣaṭtriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rāmoktanītiḥ
236.d:
स्वस्तोत्रपाठश्रवणकर्तॄणां भुक्तिमुक्तिदं /
श्रीस्तोत्रं सततं तस्मात् पठेच्च शृणुयान्नरः //
:ए इत्य् अग्नेये महापुराणे श्रीस्तोत्रं नाम
षट्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
रामोक्तनीतिः
236.m:
The hymn to Śrī grants worldly enjoyment and liberation to those who recite or listen to it. / Therefore a man should constantly recite and listen to it.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and thirty-sixth chapter, named 'The Hymn to Śrī.'
Now, the two hundred and thirty-seventh chapter.
Polity spoken by Rāma.

237.s:
agnir uvāca
nītiste puṣkaroktā tu rāmoktā lakṣmaṇāya yā /
jayāya tāṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu dharmādivardhanīṃ //
237.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
नीतिस्ते पुष्करोक्ता तु रामोक्ता लक्ष्मणाय या /
जयाय तां प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु धर्मादिवर्धनीं //
237.m: Agni said: / The polity spoken by Puṣkara to you, which was spoken by Rāma to Lakṣmaṇa / for victory, that I shall declare; listen to it which increases righteousness and the rest.

237.s:
rāma uvāca
nyānenārjanamarthasya vardhanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ caret /
satpātrapratipattiś ca rājavṛttaṃ caturvidhaṃ //
237.d:
राम उवाच
न्यानेनार्जनमर्थस्य वर्धनं रक्षणं चरेत् /
सत्पात्रप्रतिपत्तिश् च राजवृत्तं चतुर्विधं //
237.m: Rāma said: / One should carry out the acquisition of wealth by just means, its increase, and its protection, / and its bestowal upon worthy recipients: fourfold is the conduct of a king.

237.s:
nayasya vinayo mūlaṃ vinayaḥ śāstraniś cayāt /
vinayo hīndriyajayastair yuktaḥ pālayenmahīṃ //
237.d:
नयस्य विनयो मूलं विनयः शास्त्रनिश् चयात् /
विनयो हीन्द्रियजयस्तैर् युक्तः पालयेन्महीं //
