237.m: Discipline is the root of policy; discipline arises from the certainty of the treatises; / discipline is indeed the conquest of the senses; endowed with these, he should protect the earth.

237.s:
śāstraṃ prajñā dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ prāgalbhyaṃ dhārayiṣṇutā /
utsāho vāgmitaudāryamāpatkālasahiṣṇutā(1) //
237.d:
शास्त्रं प्रज्ञा धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं प्रागल्भ्यं धारयिष्णुता /
उत्साहो वाग्मितौदार्यमापत्कालसहिष्णुता(1) //
237.m: Knowledge of the treatises, intellect, firmness, skill, bold confidence, retentiveness, / energy, eloquence, generosity, endurance in times of misfortune,

237.s:
prabhāvaḥ śucitā maitrī tyāgaḥ satyaṃ kṛtajñatā /
kulaṃ śīlaṃ samaśceti guṇāḥ sampattihetavaḥ //
237.d:
प्रभावः शुचिता मैत्री त्यागः सत्यं कृतज्ञता /
कुलं शीलं समश्चेति गुणाः सम्पत्तिहेतवः //
237.m: Majesty, purity, friendliness, liberality, truth, gratitude, / noble birth, good character, and equanimity: these are the qualities that cause prosperity.

237.s:
prakīrṇaviṣayāraṇye dhāvantaṃ vipramāthinaṃ /
:n
1 vāgimatā dārḍhyamāpatkālasahiṣṇuteti kha.. , gha.. , ja.. , jha.. ca
:p 359
jñānāṅkuśena kurvīta vaśyamindriyadantinaṃ //
237.d:
प्रकीर्णविषयारण्ये धावन्तं विप्रमाथिनं /
:न्
1 वागिमता दार्ढ्यमापत्कालसहिष्णुतेति ख.. , घ.. , ज.. , झ.. च
:प् 359
ज्ञानाङ्कुशेन कुर्वीत वश्यमिन्द्रियदन्तिनं //
237.m:
Running wild in the forest of scattered sense-objects, destructive,
[Footnote]
1 'vāgmatā dārḍhyam āpatkālasahiṣṇutā' in kha, gha, ja, and jha. / [Page 359]
one should make the elephant of the senses submissive with the goad of knowledge.

237.s:
kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobho harṣo māno madas tathā /
ṣaḍvargamutsṛjedenamasmiṃstyakte sukhī nṛpaḥ //
237.d:
कामः क्रोधस् तथा लोभो हर्षो मानो मदस् तथा /
षड्वर्गमुत्सृजेदेनमस्मिंस्त्यक्ते सुखी नृपः //
237.m: Desire, anger, greed, elation, pride, and arrogance: / he should cast off this group of six; when this is abandoned, the king is happy.

237.s:
ānvīkṣikīṃ trayīṃ vārtāṃ daṇḍanītiṃ ca pārthivaḥ /
tadvaidyaistatkriyopaitaiścintatayedvinayānvitaḥ //
237.d:
आन्वीक्षिकीं त्रयीं वार्तां दण्डनीतिं च पार्थिवः /
तद्वैद्यैस्तत्क्रियोपैतैश्चिन्ततयेद्विनयान्वितः //
237.m: Endowed with discipline, a king should deliberate on philosophy, the three Vedas, commerce, and statecraft, / in the company of those versed in them and engaged in their practice.

237.s:
ānvīkṣikyārthavijñānaṃ dharmādharmau trayīsthitau /
arthānarthau tu vārtāyāṃ daṇḍanītyāṃ nayānayau //
237.d:
आन्वीक्षिक्यार्थविज्ञानं धर्माधर्मौ त्रयीस्थितौ /
अर्थानर्थौ तु वार्तायां दण्डनीत्यां नयानयौ //
237.m: From philosophy comes knowledge of the true nature of things; righteousness and unrighteousness reside in the three Vedas; / profit and loss in commerce; and right policy and wrong policy in statecraft.

237.s:
ahiṃsā sūnṛtā vāṇī satyaṃ śaucaṃ dayā kṣamā /
varṇināṃ liṅgināṃ caiva sāmānyo dharma ucyate //
237.d:
अहिंसा सूनृता वाणी सत्यं शौचं दया क्षमा /
वर्णिनां लिङ्गिनां चैव सामान्यो धर्म उच्यते //
237.m: Non-violence, gentle speech, truth, ritual purity, compassion, and forbearance: / this is declared to be the common duty of members of the social orders and religious stages.

237.s:
prajāḥ samanugṛhṇīyāt kuryādācārasaṃsthitiṃ /
vāk sūnṛtā dayā dānaṃ hīnopagatarakṣaṇaṃ(1) //
237.d:
प्रजाः समनुगृह्णीयात् कुर्यादाचारसंस्थितिं /
वाक् सूनृता दया दानं हीनोपगतरक्षणं(1) //
237.m: He should favor his subjects and establish proper conduct: / gentle speech, compassion, gift-giving, and protection of the humble who have sought shelter.

237.s:
iti vṛttaṃ satāṃ sādhuhitaṃ satpuruṣavrataṃ /
ādhivyādhiparītāya adya śvo vā vināśine //
237.d:
इति वृत्तं सतां साधुहितं सत्पुरुषव्रतं /
आधिव्याधिपरीताय अद्य श्वो वा विनाशिने //
237.m: Such is the conduct of the virtuous, beneficial to good men, the vow of true men. / For a body beset by mental anguish and physical disease, perishing today or tomorrow,

237.s:
ko hi rājā śarīrāya dharmāpetaṃ samācaret /
na hi svamukhamanvicchan(2) pīḍayet kṛpaṇaṃ janaṃ //
237.d:
को हि राजा शरीराय धर्मापेतं समाचरेत् /
न हि स्वमुखमन्विच्छन्(2) पीडयेत् कृपणं जनं //
237.m: what king would commit what departs from righteousness? / Seeking his own happiness, he should never oppress wretched people.

237.s:
kṛpaṇaḥ pīḍyamāno hi manyunā hanti pārthivaṃ /
kriyate 'bhyarhaṇīyāya svajanāya yathāñjaliḥ //
237.d:
कृपणः पीड्यमानो हि मन्युना हन्ति पार्थिवं /
क्रियते ऽभ्यर्हणीयाय स्वजनाय यथाञ्जलिः //
237.m: For a wretched man, when oppressed, destroys the king with his grief. / Just as folded hands of reverence are made to one's own venerable kinsman,

237.s:
tataḥ sādhutaraḥ kāryo durjanāya śivarthinā /
priyamevābhidhātavyaṃ satsu nityaṃ dviṣatsu ca //
237.d:
ततः साधुतरः कार्यो दुर्जनाय शिवर्थिना /
प्रियमेवाभिधातव्यं सत्सु नित्यं द्विषत्सु च //
237.m: so an even greater courtesy should be shown to a wicked person by one who desires well-being. / One should always speak only pleasing words to the good and to enemies alike.

237.s:
devāste priyavaktāraḥ paśavaḥ krūravādinaḥ /
śucirāstikyapūtātmā pūjayeddevatāḥ sadā //
:n
1 dīnopagatarakṣaṇamiti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 svamukhamanvicchuriti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 360
237.d:
देवास्ते प्रियवक्तारः पशवः क्रूरवादिनः /
शुचिरास्तिक्यपूतात्मा पूजयेद्देवताः सदा //
:न्
1 दीनोपगतरक्षणमिति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
2 स्वमुखमन्विच्छुरिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 360
237.m:
Those who speak pleasing words are gods; those who speak harshly are beasts. / Pure, with a mind sanctified by faith, he should always worship the deities.
[Note]
1 "Protecting the miserable and helpless" in kha, gha, cha, ja, ña, and ṭa.
2 "Desiring one's own face [i.e., welfare]" in kha and cha. / [Page 360]

237.s:
devatāvat gurujanamātmavacca suhṛjjanaṃ /
praṇipātena hi guruṃ sato 'mṛṣānuceṣṭitaiḥ //
237.d:
देवतावत् गुरुजनमात्मवच्च सुहृज्जनं /
प्रणिपातेन हि गुरुं सतो ऽमृषानुचेष्टितैः //
237.m: [Treating] elders like gods and friends like oneself, / [one should win over] an elder by prostration, [and] the virtuous by sincere deeds.

237.s:
kurvītābhimukhān bhṛtyair devān sukṛtakarmaṇā /
sadbhāvena harenmitraṃ sambhrameṇa ca bāndhavān //
237.d:
कुर्वीताभिमुखान् भृत्यैर् देवान् सुकृतकर्मणा /
सद्भावेन हरेन्मित्रं सम्भ्रमेण च बान्धवान् //
237.m: Through servants one should propitiate the gods, [and] through meritorious action; / one should win a friend by genuine goodwill, and relatives by showing deference.

237.s:
strībhṛtyān premadānābhyāṃ dākṣiṇyetaraṃ janaṃ /
anindā parakṛtyeṣu svadharmaparipālanaṃ //
237.d:
स्त्रीभृत्यान् प्रेमदानाभ्यां दाक्षिण्येतरं जनं /
अनिन्दा परकृत्येषु स्वधर्मपरिपालनं //
237.m: Women and servants [should be won] with love and gifts, other people with courtesy; / non-criticism of the actions of others, adherence to one's own duty,

237.s:
kṛpaṇeṣu dayālutvaṃ sarvatra madhurā giraḥ /
prāṇair apyupakāritvaṃ mitrāyāvyabhicāriṇe //
237.d:
कृपणेषु दयालुत्वं सर्वत्र मधुरा गिरः /
प्राणैर् अप्युपकारित्वं मित्रायाव्यभिचारिणे //
237.m: compassion toward the wretched, sweet words on every occasion, / helping an unfailing friend even at the cost of one's life,

237.s:
gṛhāgate pariṣvaṅgaḥ śaktyā dānaṃ sahiṣṇutā /
svasamṛddhiṣvanutsekaḥ paravṛddhiṣvamatsaraḥ //
237.d:
गृहागते परिष्वङ्गः शक्त्या दानं सहिष्णुता /
स्वसमृद्धिष्वनुत्सेकः परवृद्धिष्वमत्सरः //
237.m: an embrace for one who comes to the house, giving according to one's means, forbearance, / absence of arrogance in one's own prosperity, absence of envy at the advancement of others,

237.s:
aparopatāpi vacanaṃ maunavratacariṣṇutā(1) /
bandhabhirbaddhasaṃyogaḥ svajane caturaśratā //
237.d:
अपरोपतापि वचनं मौनव्रतचरिष्णुता(1) /
बन्धभिर्बद्धसंयोगः स्वजने चतुरश्रता //
237.m: speech that does not afflict others, observing the vow of silence, / enduring connection with relatives, upright conduct toward one's own folk,

237.s:
ucitānuvidhāyitvamiti vṛttaṃ mahātmanāṃ //23//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rāmoktanītirnāma
saptatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājadharmāḥ
237.d:
उचितानुविधायित्वमिति वृत्तं महात्मनां //23//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे रामोक्तनीतिर्नाम
सप्तत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजधर्माः
237.m:
and doing what is proper: such is the conduct of noble souls. // 23
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and thirty-seventh chapter, entitled "Statecraft Taught by Rāma."
Now, the two hundred and thirty-eighth chapter.
The Duties of a King.

238.s:
rāma uvāca
svāmyamātyañca rāṣṭrañca durgaṃ koṣo balaṃ suhṛt /
parasparopakārīdaṃ saptāṅgaṃ rājyamucyate //
:n
1 svasamṛddhiṣvityādiḥ, mīnavratacariṣṇutetyantaḥ ja.. pustake
nāsti
:p 361
238.d:
राम उवाच
स्वाम्यमात्यञ्च राष्ट्रञ्च दुर्गं कोषो बलं सुहृत् /
परस्परोपकारीदं सप्ताङ्गं राज्यमुच्यते //
:न्
1 स्वसमृद्धिष्वित्यादिः, मीनव्रतचरिष्णुतेत्यन्तः ज.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
:प् 361
238.m:
Rāma said: / The sovereign, the minister, the realm, the fort, the treasury, the army, and the ally: / this kingdom is said to have seven limbs, mutually supportive.
[Note]
1 The passage beginning with "svasamṛddhiṣu..." up to "mīnavratacariṣṇutā" is missing in the ja manuscript. / [Page 361]

238.s:
rājyāṅgānāṃ varaṃ rāṣṭraṃ sādhanaṃ pālayet sadā(1) /
kulaṃ śīlaṃ vayaḥ sattvaṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ kṣiprakāritā //
238.d:
राज्याङ्गानां वरं राष्ट्रं साधनं पालयेत् सदा(1) /
कुलं शीलं वयः सत्त्वं दाक्षिण्यं क्षिप्रकारिता //
238.m: The realm is the best among the limbs of a kingdom; he should always protect this resource. / Noble lineage, good character, [prime] age, vigor, courtesy, swiftness of action,

238.s:
avisaṃvāditā satyaṃ vṛddhasevā kṛtajñatā /
daivasampannatā buddhirakṣudraparivāratā //
238.d:
अविसंवादिता सत्यं वृद्धसेवा कृतज्ञता /
दैवसम्पन्नता बुद्धिरक्षुद्रपरिवारता //
238.m: reliability, truthfulness, reverence for elders, gratitude, / fortune favored by destiny, intellect, having attendants who are not base,

238.s:
śakyasāmantatā caiva tathā ca dṛḍhabhaktitā(2) /
dīrghadarśitvamutsāhaḥ śucitā sthūlalakṣitā //
238.d:
शक्यसामन्तता चैव तथा च दृढभक्तिता(2) /
दीर्घदर्शित्वमुत्साहः शुचिता स्थूललक्षिता //
238.m: having feudatories who are manageable, firm devotion, / far-sightedness, enthusiasm, purity, generosity,

238.s:
vinītatvaṃ dhārmikatā sādhoś ca nṛpaterguṇāḥ /
prakhyātavaṃśamakrūraṃ lokasaṅgrāhiṇaṃ śuciṃ //
238.d:
विनीतत्वं धार्मिकता साधोश् च नृपतेर्गुणाः /
प्रख्यातवंशमक्रूरं लोकसङ्ग्राहिणं शुचिं //
238.m: modesty, and righteousness: these are the qualities of a good king. / From a renowned lineage, not cruel, winning the people, pure—

238.s:
kurvītātsahitāṅkṣī paricāraṃ mahīpatiḥ /
vāgmī pragalbhaḥ smṛtimānudagro balavān vaśī //
238.d:
कुर्वीतात्सहिताङ्क्षी परिचारं महीपतिः /
वाग्मी प्रगल्भः स्मृतिमानुदग्रो बलवान् वशी //
238.m: the lord of the earth, wishing for his own welfare, should assemble such an entourage. / Eloquent, bold, possessed of memory, exalted, strong, self-controlled,

238.s:
netā daṇḍasya nipuṇaḥ kṛtaśilpaparigrahaḥ(3) /
parābhiyogaprasahaḥ sarvaduṣṭapratikriyā(4) //
238.d:
नेता दण्डस्य निपुणः कृतशिल्पपरिग्रहः(3) /
पराभियोगप्रसहः सर्वदुष्टप्रतिक्रिया(4) //
238.m: a leader of the army, skilled, having patronized the arts, / capable of enduring enemy attack, a counteragent against all wicked persons,

238.s:
pravṛttānvavekṣī ca(5) sandhivigrahatattvavit /
gūḍhamantrapracārajño deśakālavibhāgavit //
238.d:
प्रवृत्तान्ववेक्षी च(5) सन्धिविग्रहतत्त्ववित् /
गूढमन्त्रप्रचारज्ञो देशकालविभागवित् //
238.m: mindful of ongoing affairs, knowing the essence of peace and war, / knowing the movements of secret counsel, knowing the divisions of place and time,

238.s:
ādātā samyagarthānāṃ viniyoktā ca pātravit /
krodhalobhabhayadrohadambhacāpalavarjitaḥ //
238.d:
आदाता सम्यगर्थानां विनियोक्ता च पात्रवित् /
क्रोधलोभभयद्रोहदम्भचापलवर्जितः //
238.m: a proper collector of revenues, a proper dispenser [of wealth] who knows worthy recipients, / free from anger, greed, fear, treason, deceit, and fickleness,

238.s:
paropatāpapaiśūnyamātsaryerṣānṛtātigaḥ /
vṛddhopadeśasampannaḥ śakto madhuradarśanaḥ //
238.d:
परोपतापपैशून्यमात्सर्येर्षानृतातिगः /
वृद्धोपदेशसम्पन्नः शक्तो मधुरदर्शनः //
238.m: transcending malice toward others, slander, envy, jealousy, and falsehood, / enriched by the counsel of the wise, capable, pleasant in appearance,

238.s:
guṇānurāgasthitimānātmasampadguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
kulīnāḥ śucayaḥ śūrāḥ śrutavanto 'nurāgiṇaḥ(6) //
:n
1 svāmyamātyetyādiḥ, pālayet sadetyantaḥ pāṭhaḥ ga.. pustake
nāsti
2 tadvacca dṛḍhabhaktiteti ga..
3 kṛtaśilpaḥ svavagraha iti gha.. , ña.. ca
4 sarvaduṣṭapratigraha iti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. ca
5 paracchidrānvavekṣī ceti gha.. , ña.. ca
6 guṇavanto 'nugāmina iti ga..
:p 362
238.d:
गुणानुरागस्थितिमानात्मसम्पद्गुणाः स्मृताः /
कुलीनाः शुचयः शूराः श्रुतवन्तो ऽनुरागिणः(6) //
:न्
1 स्वाम्यमात्येत्यादिः, पालयेत् सदेत्यन्तः पाठः ग.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
2 तद्वच्च दृढभक्तितेति ग..
3 कृतशिल्पः स्ववग्रह इति घ.. , ञ.. च
4 सर्वदुष्टप्रतिग्रह इति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. च
5 परच्छिद्रान्ववेक्षी चेति घ.. , ञ.. च
6 गुणवन्तो ऽनुगामिन इति ग..
:प् 362
238.m:
attached to virtue, and steady: these are recorded as the personal qualities [of a king]. / Well-born, pure, heroic, learned in scripture, loyal,
[Note]
1 The reading beginning with "svāmyamātya..." up to "pālayet sadā" is missing in the ga manuscript.
2 "tadvacca dṛḍhabhaktitā" in ga.
3 "kṛtaśilpaḥ svavagrahaḥ" in gha and ña.
4 "sarvaduṣṭapratigrahaḥ" in kha, gha, and cha.
5 "paracchidrānvavekṣī ca" in gha and ña.
6 "guṇavanto 'nugāminaḥ" in ga. / [Page 362]

238.s:
daṇḍanīteḥ prayoktāraḥ sacivāḥ syurmahīpateḥ /
suvigraho jānapadaḥ kulaśīkakalānvitaḥ //
238.d:
दण्डनीतेः प्रयोक्तारः सचिवाः स्युर्महीपतेः /
सुविग्रहो जानपदः कुलशीककलान्वितः //
238.m: and practitioners of statecraft should be the ministers of the lord of the earth. / Well-formed, native to the realm, endowed with noble birth, good character, and arts,

238.s:
vāgmī pragalbhaś cakṣuṣmānutsāhī pratipattimān /
stambhacāpalahīnaś ca maitraḥ kleśasahaḥ śuciḥ //
238.d:
वाग्मी प्रगल्भश् चक्षुष्मानुत्साही प्रतिपत्तिमान् /
स्तम्भचापलहीनश् च मैत्रः क्लेशसहः शुचिः //
238.m: eloquent, bold, perceptive, energetic, resourceful, / free from arrogance and fickleness, friendly, enduring hardships, pure,

238.s:
satyasattvadhṛtisthairyaprabhāvārogyasaṃyutaḥ /
kṛtaśilpaś ca(1) dakṣaś ca prajñāvān dhāraṇānvitaḥ //
238.d:
सत्यसत्त्वधृतिस्थैर्यप्रभावारोग्यसंयुतः /
कृतशिल्पश् च(1) दक्षश् च प्रज्ञावान् धारणान्वितः //
238.m: endowed with truth, courage, resolution, steadfastness, majesty, and health, / accomplished in skills, capable, wise, possessing retentive memory,

238.s:
dṛḍhabhaktirakartā ca vairāṇāṃ sacivo bhavet /
smṛtistatparatārtheṣu cittajño jñānaniś cayaḥ(2) //
238.d:
दृढभक्तिरकर्ता च वैराणां सचिवो भवेत् /
स्मृतिस्तत्परतार्थेषु चित्तज्ञो ज्ञाननिश् चयः(2) //
238.m: firmly devoted, and not one who creates enmities: such a person should be a minister. / Memory, intentness on goals, understanding others' minds, decisiveness of intellect,

238.s:
dṛḍhatā mantraguptiś ca mantrisampat prakīrtitā /
trayyāṃ ca daṇḍanītyāṃ ca kuśalaḥ syāt purohitaḥ //
238.d:
दृढता मन्त्रगुप्तिश् च मन्त्रिसम्पत् प्रकीर्तिता /
त्रय्यां च दण्डनीत्यां च कुशलः स्यात् पुरोहितः //
238.m: firmness, and secrecy of counsel: this is proclaimed as the perfection of a minister. / And in the threefold Veda and in statecraft, the royal priest should be skilled.

238.s:
atharvadevavihitaṃ kuryācchāntikapauṣṭikaṃ /
sādhutaiṣāmamātyānāṃ tadvidyaiḥ saha buddhimān //
238.d:
अथर्वदेवविहितं कुर्याच्छान्तिकपौष्टिकं /
साधुतैषाममात्यानां तद्विद्यैः सह बुद्धिमान् //
238.m: He should perform apotropaic and restorative rites prescribed by the Atharvaveda. / A wise king [should ascertain] the goodness of these ministers together with experts in their fields:

238.s:
cakṣuṣmattāṃ ca śilpañca parīkṣeta guṇadvayaṃ(3) /
svajanebhyo vijānīyāt kulaṃ sthānamavagrahaṃ //
238.d:
चक्षुष्मत्तां च शिल्पञ्च परीक्षेत गुणद्वयं(3) /
स्वजनेभ्यो विजानीयात् कुलं स्थानमवग्रहं //
238.m: he should examine the two qualities of perceptiveness and artistic skill; / from their relatives he should know their lineage, home region, and family background;

238.s:
parikarmasu dakṣañca vijñānaṃ dhārayiṣṇutāṃ /
guṇatrayaṃ parīkṣeta prāgalabhyaṃ prītitāṃ tathā(4) //
238.d:
परिकर्मसु दक्षञ्च विज्ञानं धारयिष्णुतां /
गुणत्रयं परीक्षेत प्रागलभ्यं प्रीतितां तथा(4) //
238.m: he should test three qualities: their skill in attendant duties, understanding, and capacity for retention; / likewise boldness and friendliness;

238.s:
kathāyogeṣu buddhyeta vāgmitvaṃ satyavāditāṃ /
utasāhaṃ ca prabhāvaṃ ca tathā kleśasahiṣṇutāṃ(5) //
238.d:
कथायोगेषु बुद्ध्येत वाग्मित्वं सत्यवादितां /
उतसाहं च प्रभावं च तथा क्लेशसहिष्णुतां(5) //
238.m: in conversational situations he should perceive eloquence and truthfulness, / as well as enthusiasm, majesty, and endurance of hardship;

238.s:
dhṛtiṃ caivānurāgaṃ ca sthairyañcāpadi lakṣayet /
bhaktiṃ maitrīṃ ca śaucaṃ ca jānīyādvyavahārataḥ //
:n
1 kṛtaśīlaśceti ja..
2 cintako jñānaniś caya iti ga..
3 parīkṣeta guṇatrayamiti ja..
4 pratibhāṃ tatheti ja..
5 svajanebhya ity ādiḥ, kleśasahiṣṇutāmityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ cha..
pustake nāsti
:p 363
238.d:
धृतिं चैवानुरागं च स्थैर्यञ्चापदि लक्षयेत् /
भक्तिं मैत्रीं च शौचं च जानीयाद्व्यवहारतः //
:न्
1 कृतशीलश्चेति ज..
2 चिन्तको ज्ञाननिश् चय इति ग..
3 परीक्षेत गुणत्रयमिति ज..
4 प्रतिभां तथेति ज..
5 स्वजनेभ्य इत्य् आदिः, क्लेशसहिष्णुतामित्यन्तः पाठः छ..
पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 363
238.m:
and in times of misfortune he should observe resolution, loyalty, and steadfastness; / he should know devotion, friendship, and integrity through practical dealings.
[Note]
1 "kṛtaśīlaśca" in ja.
2 "cintako jñānaniścayaḥ" in ga.
3 "parīkṣeta guṇatrayam" in ja.
4 "pratibhāṃ tathā" in ja.
5 The reading beginning with "svajanebhyaḥ..." up to "kleśasahiṣṇutām" is missing in the cha manuscript. / [Page 363]

238.s:
saṃvāsibhyo balaṃ sattvamārogyaṃ śīlameva ca(1) /
astabdhatāmacāpalyaṃ vairāṇāṃ cāpyakīrtanaṃ //
238.d:
संवासिभ्यो बलं सत्त्वमारोग्यं शीलमेव च(1) /
अस्तब्धतामचापल्यं वैराणां चाप्यकीर्तनं //
238.m: From fellow residents [he should learn of] strength, vigor, health, and moral character; / unpretentiousness, lack of fickleness, and not brooding over grievances

238.s:
pratyakṣato vijānīyād bhadratāṃ kṣudratāmapi /
phalānumeyāḥ sarvatra parokṣaguṇavṛttayaḥ //
238.d:
प्रत्यक्षतो विजानीयाद् भद्रतां क्षुद्रतामपि /
फलानुमेयाः सर्वत्र परोक्षगुणवृत्तयः //
238.m: he should know by direct observation, as well as goodness and baseness; / the functions of unseen qualities are everywhere to be inferred from their results.

238.s:
śasyākaravatī puṇyā khanidravyasamanvitā /
gohitā bhūrisalilā puṇyair janapadair yutā //
238.d:
शस्याकरवती पुण्या खनिद्रव्यसमन्विता /
गोहिता भूरिसलिला पुण्यैर् जनपदैर् युता //
238.m: Rich in crops and mines, holy, endowed with mineral treasures, / beneficial to cattle, having abundant water, populated by virtuous peoples,

238.s:
ramyā sakuñjarabalā vāristhalapathānvitā /
adevamātṛkā ceti śasyate bhūribhūtaye //
238.d:
रम्या सकुञ्जरबला वारिस्थलपथान्विता /
अदेवमातृका चेति शस्यते भूरिभूतये //
238.m: charming, possessing an elephant force, equipped with land and water routes, / and not dependent on rainfall: such [a realm] is praised for abundant prosperity.

238.s:
śūdrakāruvaṇikprāyo mahārambhaḥ kṛṣī balaḥ /
sānurāgo ripudveṣī pīḍāsahakaraḥ pṛthuḥ //
238.d:
शूद्रकारुवणिक्प्रायो महारम्भः कृषी बलः /
सानुरागो रिपुद्वेषी पीडासहकरः पृथुः //
238.m: Consisting mostly of Śūdras, artisans, and merchants, of great enterprise, agricultural, / loyal, hostile to enemies, bearing heavy taxes, expansive,

238.s:
nānādeśyaiḥ samākīrṇo dhārmikaḥ paśumān balī /
īdṛkjanapadaḥ śasto 'mūrkhavyasanināyakaḥ(2) //
238.d:
नानादेश्यैः समाकीर्णो धार्मिकः पशुमान् बली /
ईदृक्जनपदः शस्तो ऽमूर्खव्यसनिनायकः(2) //
238.m: thronged by people of various lands, righteous, possessing cattle, and strong: / such a realm is praised, whose leader is neither a fool nor addicted to vice.

238.s:
pṛthusīmaṃ mahākhātamuccaprākāratoraṇaṃ(3) /
puraṃ samāvasecchailasarinmaruvanāśrayaṃ //
238.d:
पृथुसीमं महाखातमुच्चप्राकारतोरणं(3) /
पुरं समावसेच्छैलसरिन्मरुवनाश्रयं //
238.m: With broad boundaries, a great moat, high ramparts and gate-towers, / he should inhabit a city supported by mountains, rivers, desert, or forest.

238.s:
jalavaddhānyadhanavaddurgaṃ kālasahaṃ mahat /
audakaṃ pārvataṃ vārkṣamairiṇaṃ dhanvinaṃ ca ṣaṭ //
238.d:
जलवद्धान्यधनवद्दुर्गं कालसहं महत् /
औदकं पार्वतं वार्क्षमैरिणं धन्विनं च षट् //
238.m: A fort should be endowed with water, grain, and wealth, large and able to endure time. / Forts are of six kinds: water-fort, mountain-fort, forest-fort, desert-fort, and wilderness-fort.

238.s:
īpsitadravyasampūrṇaḥ pitṛpaitāmahocitaḥ /
dharmārjito vyayasahaḥ koṣo dharmādivṛddhaye //
238.d:
ईप्सितद्रव्यसम्पूर्णः पितृपैतामहोचितः /
धर्मार्जितो व्ययसहः कोषो धर्मादिवृद्धये //
238.m: Filled with desired goods, inherited from father and grandfather, / acquired righteously, able to withstand expenditure, the treasury serves the growth of dharma and the rest.

238.s:
pitṛpaitāmaho vaśyaḥ saṃhato dattavetanaḥ /
vikhyātapauruṣo janyaḥ kuśulaḥ śakunair vṛtaḥ //
238.d:
पितृपैतामहो वश्यः संहतो दत्तवेतनः /
विख्यातपौरुषो जन्यः कुशुलः शकुनैर् वृतः //
238.m: Inherited from father and grandfather, compliant, unified, receiving regular pay, / of renowned valor, martial, skilled, and favored by portents—

238.s:
nānāprahaṇopeto nānāyuddhaviśāradaḥ /
:n
1 sattvamārogyaṃ kulameva ceti ja..
2 makhyavyasananāyaka iti ga..
3 uccaprakāragopuramiti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 364
nānāyodhasamākīrṇau nīrājitahayadvipaḥ //
238.d:
नानाप्रहणोपेतो नानायुद्धविशारदः /
:न्
1 सत्त्वमारोग्यं कुलमेव चेति ज..
2 मख्यव्यसननायक इति ग..
3 उच्चप्रकारगोपुरमिति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 364
नानायोधसमाकीर्णौ नीराजितहयद्विपः //
238.m:
Furnished with various weapons, skilled in various modes of warfare,
[Footnote]
1 'sattvam ārogyaṃ kulam eva ca' in ja.
2 'makhyavyasananāyakaḥ' in ga.
3 'uccaprākāragopuram' in gha and ña. / [Page 364]
thronged with diverse warriors, with horses and elephants purified by the lustration rite,

238.s:
pravāsāyāsaduḥkheṣu yuddheṣu ca kṛtaśramaḥ /
advaidhakṣatriyaprāyo daṇḍo daṇḍavatāṃ mataḥ //
238.d:
प्रवासायासदुःखेषु युद्धेषु च कृतश्रमः /
अद्वैधक्षत्रियप्रायो दण्डो दण्डवतां मतः //
238.m: hardened to toil in the hardships and fatigues of foreign campaigns and in battles, / composed mostly of loyal Kṣatriyas: such an army is approved by those who wield power.

238.s:
yogavijñānasattvārūḍhyaṃ mahāpakṣaṃ priyamvadaṃ /
āyātikṣamamadvaidhaṃ mitraṃ kurvīta satkulaṃ(1) //
238.d:
योगविज्ञानसत्त्वारूढ्यं महापक्षं प्रियम्वदं /
आयातिक्षममद्वैधं मित्रं कुर्वीत सत्कुलं(1) //
238.m: Endowed with skill, knowledge, and inner strength, having a large faction, speaking agreeably, / capable of endurance, unambiguous, of good family: such a one he should make an ally.

238.s:
dūrādevābhigamanaṃ spaṣṭārthahṛdayānugā /
vāk satkṛtya pradānañca trividho mitrasaṅgrahaḥ //
238.d:
दूरादेवाभिगमनं स्पष्टार्थहृदयानुगा /
वाक् सत्कृत्य प्रदानञ्च त्रिविधो मित्रसङ्ग्रहः //
238.m: Going forward to meet from afar, speech that is clear in meaning and conforms to the heart, / and giving with hospitality: threefold is the winning of allies.

238.s:
dharmakāmārthasaṃyogo mitrāttu trividhaṃ phalaṃ /
aurasaṃ tatra sannaddhaṃ(2) tathā vaṃśakramāgataṃ //
238.d:
धर्मकामार्थसंयोगो मित्रात्तु त्रिविधं फलं /
औरसं तत्र सन्नद्धं(2) तथा वंशक्रमागतं //
238.m: Union with righteousness, pleasure, and wealth is the threefold fruit from an ally. / In that regard, natural, one joined [by treaty], one inherited through lineage,

238.s:
rakṣitaṃ vyasanebhyaś ca mitraṃ jñeyaṃ caturvidhaṃ /
mitre guṇāḥ satyatādyāḥ samānasukhadukhatā //
238.d:
रक्षितं व्यसनेभ्यश् च मित्रं ज्ञेयं चतुर्विधं /
मित्रे गुणाः सत्यताद्याः समानसुखदुखता //
238.m: and one rescued from distress: an ally should be known as fourfold. / Virtues in an ally include truthfulness and the rest, and sharing equal joy and sorrow.

238.s:
vakṣye 'nujīvināṃ vṛtte sevī seveta bhūpatiṃ /
dakṣatā bhadratā dārḍhyaṃ kṣāntiḥ kleśasahiṣṇutā //
238.d:
वक्ष्ये ऽनुजीविनां वृत्ते सेवी सेवेत भूपतिं /
दक्षता भद्रता दार्ढ्यं क्षान्तिः क्लेशसहिष्णुता //
238.m: I shall state the conduct of dependents; a servant should serve the lord of the earth: / competence, goodness, firmness, patience, endurance of hardship,

238.s:
santoṣaḥ śīlamutsāho maṇḍayatyanujīvinaṃ /
yathākālamupāsīta rājānaṃ sevako nayāt //
238.d:
सन्तोषः शीलमुत्साहो मण्डयत्यनुजीविनं /
यथाकालमुपासीत राजानं सेवको नयात् //
238.m: contentment, good character, and zeal adorn a dependent. / A servant should attend upon the king at the proper time in accordance with policy.

238.s:
parasthānagamaṃ krauryamauddhatyaṃ matsarantyajet /
vigṛhya kathanaṃ bhṛtyo na kuryāj jyāyasā saha //
238.d:
परस्थानगमं क्रौर्यमौद्धत्यं मत्सरन्त्यजेत् /
विगृह्य कथनं भृत्यो न कुर्याज् ज्यायसा सह //
238.m: He should avoid entering another's place, cruelty, arrogance, and envy. / A servant should not enter into contentious talk with a superior.

238.s:
guhyaṃ marma ca mantrañca na ca bhartuḥ prakāśayet /
raktād vṛttiṃ samīheta viraktaṃ santyajennṛpaṃ //
238.d:
गुह्यं मर्म च मन्त्रञ्च न च भर्तुः प्रकाशयेत् /
रक्ताद् वृत्तिं समीहेत विरक्तं सन्त्यजेन्नृपं //
238.m: He should not disclose his master's secret, vulnerable point, or counsel. / He should seek his livelihood from one who is pleased, and abandon an alienated king.

238.s:
akārye pratiṣedhaś ca kārye cāpi pravartanaṃ /
saṅkṣepāditi sadvṛttaṃ bandhumitrānujīvināṃ //
:n
1 mitraṃ kurvīta satkriyamiti ja..
2 tatra sambaddhamiti ga..
:p 365
238.d:
अकार्ये प्रतिषेधश् च कार्ये चापि प्रवर्तनं /
सङ्क्षेपादिति सद्वृत्तं बन्धुमित्रानुजीविनां //
:न्
1 मित्रं कुर्वीत सत्क्रियमिति ज..
2 तत्र सम्बद्धमिति ग..
:प् 365
238.m:
Restraint from what should not be done, and engagement in what should be done: / in brief, this is the proper conduct of relatives, friends, and dependents.
[Footnote]
1 'mitraṃ kurvīta satkriyam' in ja.
2 'tatra sambandham' in ga. / [Page 365]

238.s:
ājīvyaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ rājā parjanyavadbhavet /
āyadvāreṣu cāptyarthaṃ dhanaṃ cādadatīti ca //
238.d:
आजीव्यः सर्वसत्त्वानां राजा पर्जन्यवद्भवेत् /
आयद्वारेषु चाप्त्यर्थं धनं चाददतीति च //
238.m: The king should be a source of sustenance for all living beings, like a rain-cloud; / and for securing revenue at the sources of income, they collect wealth:

238.s:
kuryādudyogasampannānadhyakṣān sarvakarmasu /
kṛṣirvaṇikpatho durgaṃ setuḥ kuñjarabandhanaṃ //
238.d:
कुर्यादुद्योगसम्पन्नानध्यक्षान् सर्वकर्मसु /
कृषिर्वणिक्पथो दुर्गं सेतुः कुञ्जरबन्धनं //
238.m: he should appoint energetic superintendents over all enterprises: / agriculture, trade-routes, fortifications, dikes and bridges, elephant capture,

238.s:
khanyākarabalādānaṃ śūnyānāṃ ca niveśanaṃ /
aṣṭavargamimaṃ rājā sādhuvṛtto 'nupālayet //
238.d:
खन्याकरबलादानं शून्यानां च निवेशनं /
अष्टवर्गमिमं राजा साधुवृत्तो ऽनुपालयेत् //
238.m: mines, collecting forces from forests, and the settlement of uninhabited lands: / a king of good conduct should foster this group of eight.

238.s:
āmuktikebhyaś caurebhyaḥ paurebhyo rājavallabhāt /
pṛthivīpatilobhācca prajānāṃ pañcadhā bhayaṃ //
238.d:
आमुक्तिकेभ्यश् चौरेभ्यः पौरेभ्यो राजवल्लभात् /
पृथिवीपतिलोभाच्च प्रजानां पञ्चधा भयं //
238.m: From newly arrived soldiers, from thieves, from townsmen, from the king's favorite, / and from the greed of the ruler of the earth: fivefold is the danger to subjects.

238.s:
avekṣyaitadbhayaṃ kāle ādadīta karaṃ nṛpaḥ /
abhyantaraṃ śarīraṃ svaṃ vāhyaṃ rāṣṭrañca(1) rakṣayet(2) //
238.d:
अवेक्ष्यैतद्भयं काले आददीत करं नृपः /
अभ्यन्तरं शरीरं स्वं वाह्यं राष्ट्रञ्च(1) रक्षयेत्(2) //
238.m: Taking note of this danger, the king should collect tax at the proper time. / He should protect his own internal body and his external kingdom.

238.s:
daṇḍāṃsta daṇḍayedrājā svaṃ rakṣecca viṣāditaḥ /
striyaḥ putrāṃś ca śatrubhyo viśvasenna kadācana //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rājadharmo nāma
aṣṭatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athonacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ
238.d:
दण्डांस्त दण्डयेद्राजा स्वं रक्षेच्च विषादितः /
स्त्रियः पुत्रांश् च शत्रुभ्यो विश्वसेन्न कदाचन //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे राजधर्मो नाम
अष्टत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथोनचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
षाड्गुण्यं
238.m:
The king should punish those deserving punishment, and should protect himself from poison and the like. / He should never trust women, sons, or enemies.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, entitled ‘The Duties of a King’, in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now begins the two hundred and thirty-ninth chapter:
The Six Methods of Foreign Policy

239.s:
rāma uvāca
maṇḍalaṃ cintayet mukhyaṃ rājā dvādaśarājakaṃ /
arirmitramarermitraṃ mitramitramataḥ paraṃ //
:n
1 rājyaṃ rāṣṭrañceti kha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
2 lakṣayediti ña..
:p 366
239.d:
राम उवाच
मण्डलं चिन्तयेत् मुख्यं राजा द्वादशराजकं /
अरिर्मित्रमरेर्मित्रं मित्रमित्रमतः परं //
:न्
1 राज्यं राष्ट्रञ्चेति ख.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
2 लक्षयेदिति ञ..
:प् 366
239.m:
Rāma said: / The king should consider the primary circle [of states] consisting of twelve kings: / the enemy, the friend, the enemy's friend, the friend's friend, and next,
[Apparatus]
1 kha, cha, and ña read 'rājyaṃ rāṣṭrañceti'.
2 ña reads 'lakṣayediti'.

239.s:
tathārimitramitrañca vijigīṣoḥ puraḥ smṛtāḥ(1) /
pārṣṇigrāhaḥ smṛtaḥ paścādākrandastadanantaraṃ //
239.d:
तथारिमित्रमित्रञ्च विजिगीषोः पुरः स्मृताः(1) /
पार्ष्णिग्राहः स्मृतः पश्चादाक्रन्दस्तदनन्तरं //
239.m: likewise the enemy's friend's friend—these are declared to be in front of the ambitious conqueror. / In the rear is declared the rearward enemy, and following him, the rearward ally.

239.s:
āsārāvanayoś caivaṃ vijagīṣāś ca maṇḍalaṃ /
areś ca vijigīṣoś ca madhyamo bhūmyanantaraḥ //
239.d:
आसारावनयोश् चैवं विजगीषाश् च मण्डलं /
अरेश् च विजिगीषोश् च मध्यमो भूम्यनन्तरः //
239.m: Likewise are the allies of these two in the rear; such is the circle of the ambitious conqueror. / Situated adjacent to the territories of both the enemy and the ambitious conqueror is the intermediate ruler.

239.s:
anugrahe saṃhatayor nigrahe vyastayoḥ prabhuḥ /
maṇḍalādvahireteṣāmudāsīno balādhikaḥ //
239.d:
अनुग्रहे संहतयोर् निग्रहे व्यस्तयोः प्रभुः /
मण्डलाद्वहिरेतेषामुदासीनो बलाधिकः //
239.m: He is capable of assisting them when united, and subduing them when divided. / Outside the circle of these is the neutral ruler, superior in strength.

239.s:
anugrahe saṃhatānāṃ vyastānāṃ ca budhe prabhuḥ /
sandhiñca vigrahaṃ yānamāsānadi vadāmi te //
239.d:
अनुग्रहे संहतानां व्यस्तानां च बुधे प्रभुः /
सन्धिञ्च विग्रहं यानमासानदि वदामि ते //
239.m: O wise one, he is capable of assisting them when united, and of subduing them when divided. / I shall tell you of alliance, war, marching, halting, and the rest.

239.s:
balavadvigrahītena sandhiṃ kuryācchivāya ca /
kapāla upahāraś ca santānaḥ saṅgatas tathā //
239.d:
बलवद्विग्रहीतेन सन्धिं कुर्याच्छिवाय च /
कपाल उपहारश् च सन्तानः सङ्गतस् तथा //
239.m: When attacked by a stronger foe, he should make peace for his own welfare. / Kapāla, upahāra, santāna, saṅgata,

239.s:
upanyāsaḥ pratīkāraḥ saṃyogaḥ puruṣāntaraḥ /
adṛṣṭanara ādiṣṭa ātmāpi sa upagrahaḥ //
239.d:
उपन्यासः प्रतीकारः संयोगः पुरुषान्तरः /
अदृष्टनर आदिष्ट आत्मापि स उपग्रहः //
239.m: upanyāsa, pratīkāra, saṃyoga, puruṣāntara, / adṛṣṭanara, ādiṣṭa, ātmāmiṣa, upagraha,

239.s:
parikramas tathā chinnas tathā ca paradūṣaṇaṃ /
skandhopayeyaḥ sandhiś ca sandhayaḥ ṣoḍaśeritāḥ //
239.d:
परिक्रमस् तथा छिन्नस् तथा च परदूषणं /
स्कन्धोपयेयः सन्धिश् च सन्धयः षोडशेरिताः //
239.m: parikrama, chinna, paradūṣaṇa, / and skandhopaneya—these sixteen alliances are spoken of.

239.s:
parasparopakāraś ca maitraḥ sambandhakas tathā(2) /
upahārāś ca catvārasteṣu mukhyāś ca sandhayaḥ //
239.d:
परस्परोपकारश् च मैत्रः सम्बन्धकस् तथा(2) /
उपहाराश् च चत्वारस्तेषु मुख्याश् च सन्धयः //
239.m: Mutual assistance, friendly, alliance through marriage, / and upahāra—these four are the principal among alliances.

239.s:
bālo vṛddho dīrgharogas tathā bandhuvahiṣkṛtaḥ /
mauruko bhīrukajano lubdho lubdhajanas tathā //
239.d:
बालो वृद्धो दीर्घरोगस् तथा बन्धुवहिष्कृतः /
मौरुको भीरुकजनो लुब्धो लुब्धजनस् तथा //
239.m: A child, an old man, a chronically ill person, an outcast from his kin, / a coward, one whose followers are cowards, a greedy person, one whose followers are greedy,

239.s:
viraktaprakṛtiś caiva viṣayeṣvatiśaktimān /
anekacittamantraś ca devabrāhmaṇanindakaḥ //
239.d:
विरक्तप्रकृतिश् चैव विषयेष्वतिशक्तिमान् /
अनेकचित्तमन्त्रश् च देवब्राह्मणनिन्दकः //
239.m: one whose subjects are disaffected, one overly attached to sensual pleasures, / one whose counsel wavers among many minds, a reviler of the gods and brāhmaṇas,

239.s:
daivopahatakaś caiva daivanindaka eva ca /
durbhikṣavyasanopeto balavyasanasaṅkulaḥ //
:n
1 puraḥsthitā iti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 maitraḥ sukhakarastatheti ga..
:p 367
239.d:
दैवोपहतकश् चैव दैवनिन्दक एव च /
दुर्भिक्षव्यसनोपेतो बलव्यसनसङ्कुलः //
:न्
1 पुरःस्थिता इति ख.. , छ.. च
2 मैत्रः सुखकरस्तथेति ग..
:प् 367
239.m:
one stricken by fate, a reviler of fate, / one beset by the distress of famine, one overcome by distress in his army,
[Apparatus]
1 kha and cha read 'puraḥsthitāḥ'.
2 ga reads 'maitraḥ sukhakarastathā'.

239.s:
svadeśastho bahuripurmuktaḥ kālena yaś ca ha /
satyadharmavyapetaś ca viṃśatiḥ puruṣā amī //
239.d:
स्वदेशस्थो बहुरिपुर्मुक्तः कालेन यश् च ह /
सत्यधर्मव्यपेतश् च विंशतिः पुरुषा अमी //
239.m: one stationed in his own territory who has many enemies, one abandoned by time, / and one devoid of truth and righteousness—these twenty persons,

239.s:
ertaiḥ sandhiṃ na kurvīta vigṛhṇīyāttu kebalaṃ /
parasparāpakāreṇa puṃsāṃ bhavati vigrahaḥ //
239.d:
एर्तैः सन्धिं न कुर्वीत विगृह्णीयात्तु केबलं /
परस्परापकारेण पुंसां भवति विग्रहः //
239.m: one should not make peace with these; rather, he should only wage war against them. / Hostility arises among men from mutual injury.

239.s:
ātmano 'bhyudayākāṅkṣī pīḍyamānaḥ pareṇa vā /
deśakālabalopetaḥ prārabheteha vigrahaṃ(1) //
239.d:
आत्मनो ऽभ्युदयाकाङ्क्षी पीड्यमानः परेण वा /
देशकालबलोपेतः प्रारभेतेह विग्रहं(1) //
239.m: Desiring his own prosperity, or when oppressed by another, / endowed with the advantage of place, time, and strength, one should undertake war in this world.

239.s:
rājyastrīsthānadeśānāṃ jñānasya ca balasya ca /
apahārī(2) mado mānaḥ pīḍā vaiṣayikī tathā //
239.d:
राज्यस्त्रीस्थानदेशानां ज्ञानस्य च बलस्य च /
अपहारी(2) मदो मानः पीडा वैषयिकी तथा //
239.m: Deprivation of kingdom, women, settlements, territory, / knowledge, or strength; arrogance; pride; injury caused by sensual pursuits;

239.s:
jñānātmaśaktidharmāṇāṃ(3) vighāto daivameva ca /
mitrārthañcāpamānaś ca tathā bandhuvināśanaṃ //
239.d:
ज्ञानात्मशक्तिधर्माणां(3) विघातो दैवमेव च /
मित्रार्थञ्चापमानश् च तथा बन्धुविनाशनं //
239.m: impediment to knowledge, personal power, or virtue; fate alone; / an ally's affair; insult; destruction of kin;

239.s:
bhūtānugrahavicchedas tathā maṇḍaladūṣaṇaṃ /
ekārthābhiniveśatvamiti vigrahayonayaḥ //
239.d:
भूतानुग्रहविच्छेदस् तथा मण्डलदूषणं /
एकार्थाभिनिवेशत्वमिति विग्रहयोनयः //
239.m: alienation of loyal subjects; corrupting the circle [of kings]; / and competing desire for a single object—these are the sources of war.

239.s:
sāpatnyaṃ vāstujaṃ strījaṃ vāgjātamaparādhajaṃ /
vairaṃ pañcavidhaṃ proktaṃ sādhanaiḥ praśamannayet //
239.d:
सापत्न्यं वास्तुजं स्त्रीजं वाग्जातमपराधजं /
वैरं पञ्चविधं प्रोक्तं साधनैः प्रशमन्नयेत् //
239.m: Arising from rivalry, arising from land, arising from women, arising from words, and arising from an offense— / enmity is declared to be of five kinds; he should bring it to pacification by proper means.

239.s:
kiñcitphalaṃ niṣphalaṃ vā sandigdhaphalameva ca /
tadātve doṣajananamāyatyāñcaiva niṣphalaṃ //
239.d:
किञ्चित्फलं निष्फलं वा सन्दिग्धफलमेव च /
तदात्वे दोषजननमायत्याञ्चैव निष्फलं //
239.m: [A war that brings] meager fruit, or no fruit, or doubtful fruit, / causing harm in the present and bearing no fruit in the future,

239.s:
āyatyāñca tadātve ca doṣasañjananaṃ tathā /
aparijñātavīryeṇa pareṇa stobhito 'pi vā //
239.d:
आयत्याञ्च तदात्वे च दोषसञ्जननं तथा /
अपरिज्ञातवीर्येण परेण स्तोभितो ऽपि वा //
239.m: or producing harm both in the future and in the present, / or incited by an enemy whose strength is unknown,

239.s:
parārthaṃ strīnimittañca dīrghakālaṃ dvijaiḥ saha /
akāladaivayuktena baloddhatasakhena ca //
:n
1 ātmana ity adiḥ, vigrahamityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ ga..pustake nāsti
2 avahāra iti gha..
3 jñānārthaśaktidharmāṇāmiti ña..
:p 368
239.d:
परार्थं स्त्रीनिमित्तञ्च दीर्घकालं द्विजैः सह /
अकालदैवयुक्तेन बलोद्धतसखेन च //
:न्
1 आत्मन इत्य् अदिः, विग्रहमित्यन्तः पाठः ग..पुस्तके नास्ति
2 अवहार इति घ..
3 ज्ञानार्थशक्तिधर्माणामिति ञ..
:प् 368
239.m:
[or fought] for another's sake, or caused by a woman, or of long duration, or with brāhmaṇas, / or with one aided by ill-timed fate, or with one whose ally is haughty with power—
[Apparatus]
1 The passage beginning with 'ātmano' and ending with 'vigraham' is missing in manuscript ga.
2 gha reads 'avahāraḥ'.
3 ña reads 'jñānārthaśaktidharmāṇām'.

239.s:
tadātve phalasaṃyuktamāyatyāṃ phalavarjitaṃ /
āyatyāṃ phalasaṃyuktaṃ tadātve niṣphalaṃ tathā //
239.d:
तदात्वे फलसंयुक्तमायत्यां फलवर्जितं /
आयत्यां फलसंयुक्तं तदात्वे निष्फलं तथा //
239.m:
[A war] that bears fruit in the present but is devoid of fruit in the future,
likewise one that bears fruit in the future but is fruitless in the present,

239.s:
itīmaṃ ṣoḍaśavidhannakuryādeva vigrahaṃ /
tadātvāyatisaṃśuddhaṃ karma rājā sadācaret //
239.d:
इतीमं षोडशविधन्नकुर्यादेव विग्रहं /
तदात्वायतिसंशुद्धं कर्म राजा सदाचरेत् //
239.m:
a king should never wage such a sixteenfold war.
A king should always undertake an action that is sound both in the present and in the future.

239.s:
hṛṣṭaṃ puṣṭaṃ balaṃ matvā gṛhṇīyādviparītakaṃ /
mitramākranda āsāro yadā syurdṛḍhabhaktayaḥ //
239.d:
हृष्टं पुष्टं बलं मत्वा गृह्णीयाद्विपरीतकं /
मित्रमाक्रन्द आसारो यदा स्युर्दृढभक्तयः //
239.m:
Considering his own army pleased and well-nourished, and that of the enemy to be the opposite,
when his ally, rear ally, and supporting ally are firmly devoted,

239.s:
parasya viparītañca tadā vigrahamācaret /
vigṛhya sandhāya tathā sambhūyātha prasaṅgataḥ //
239.d:
परस्य विपरीतञ्च तदा विग्रहमाचरेत् /
विगृह्य सन्धाय तथा सम्भूयाथ प्रसङ्गतः //
239.m:
and those of the enemy are the opposite, then he should wage war.
Marching after having declared war, after making peace, together [with an ally], or through a contingent cause,

239.s:
upekṣayā ca nipuṇair yānaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtaṃ /
parasparasya sāmarthyavighātādāsanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
239.d:
उपेक्षया च निपुणैर् यानं पञ्चविधं स्मृतं /
परस्परस्य सामर्थ्यविघातादासनं स्मृतं //
239.m:
and through indifference—marching is considered fivefold by the skilled.
Halting is taught [to arise] from the neutralization of each other's strength.

239.s:
areś ca vijagīṣoś ca yānavat pañcadhā smṛtam /
balinīrdviṣatormadhye vācātmānaṃ samarpayan //
239.d:
अरेश् च विजगीषोश् च यानवत् पञ्चधा स्मृतम् /
बलिनीर्द्विषतोर्मध्ये वाचात्मानं समर्पयन् //
239.m:
Like marching, it is taught to be fivefold for both the enemy and the one desirous of conquest.
Between two powerful enemies, offering oneself through words,

239.s:
dvaidhībhāvena tiṣṭheta kākākṣivadalakṣitaḥ /
ubhayorapi sampāte seveta balavattaraṃ //
239.d:
द्वैधीभावेन तिष्ठेत काकाक्षिवदलक्षितः /
उभयोरपि सम्पाते सेवेत बलवत्तरं //
239.m:
one should remain in a state of double-dealing, unnoticed like a crow's eye.
When both encounter each other, he should serve the more powerful.

239.s:
yadā dvāvapi necchetāṃ saṃśleṣaṃ jātasaṃvidau /
tadopasarpettacchatrumadhikaṃ vā svayaṃ vrajet(1) //
239.d:
यदा द्वावपि नेच्छेतां संश्लेषं जातसंविदौ /
तदोपसर्पेत्तच्छत्रुमधिकं वा स्वयं व्रजेत्(1) //
239.m:
When both, having formed a secret pact, do not desire union [with him],
then he should approach their enemy or go over to a stronger one himself.

239.s:
ucchidyamāno balinā nirupāyapratikriyaḥ /
kuloddhataṃ satyamāryamāseveta balotkaṭaṃ(2) //
239.d:
उच्छिद्यमानो बलिना निरुपायप्रतिक्रियः /
कुलोद्धतं सत्यमार्यमासेवेत बलोत्कटं(2) //
239.m:
Being uprooted by a powerful [foe], devoid of any means of counteraction,
he should resort to one of noble family, truthful, noble, and preeminent in strength.

239.s:
taddarśanopāstikatā nityantadbhāvabhāvitā /
tatkāritapraśriyatā vṛttaṃ saṃśrayiṇaḥ śrutaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe ṣāḍguṇyaṃ nāma
ekonacatvārtiṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 ubhayorityādiḥ, svayaṃ vrajedityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake
nāsti
2 balotkaramiti ga.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 369
:ś atha catvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
samādiḥ
239.d:
तद्दर्शनोपास्तिकता नित्यन्तद्भावभाविता /
तत्कारितप्रश्रियता वृत्तं संश्रयिणः श्रुतं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे षाड्गुण्यं नाम
एकोनचत्वार्तिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 उभयोरित्यादिः, स्वयं व्रजेदित्यन्तः पाठः ज.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
2 बलोत्करमिति ग.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 369
:श् अथ चत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
समादिः
239.m:
Constantly seeking his sight, serving him, always meditating on devotion to him,
and displaying humility produced by him—such is the conduct heard of one seeking refuge.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-ninth chapter, entitled 'The Six Methods of Foreign Policy,' in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Notes]
1 The passage beginning with 'ubhayor' and ending with 'svayaṃ vrajet' is absent in manuscript ja.
2 ga, gha, ja, and ña read 'balotkaram'.
Now follows the two hundred and fortieth chapter:
[The expedients such as conciliation, etc.]

240.s:
rāma uvāca
prabhavotsāhaśaktibhyāṃ mantraśaktiḥ praśasyate /
prabhāvotsāhavān kāvyo jito devapurodhasā //
240.d:
राम उवाच
प्रभवोत्साहशक्तिभ्यां मन्त्रशक्तिः प्रशस्यते /
प्रभावोत्साहवान् काव्यो जितो देवपुरोधसा //

240.s:
mantrayeteha kāryāṇi nānāptair nāvipaścitā /
aśakyārambhavṛttīnāṃ kutaḥ kleśādṛte phalaṃ //
240.d:
मन्त्रयेतेह कार्याणि नानाप्तैर् नाविपश्चिता /
अशक्यारम्भवृत्तीनां कुतः क्लेशादृते फलं //
240.m:
One should deliberate on affairs here neither with untrustworthy persons nor with the unwise.
For those whose conduct consists of attempting the impossible, whence can fruit come except distress?

240.s:
avijñātasya vijñānaṃ vijñātasya ca niś cayaḥ /
arthadvaidhasya sandehacchedanaṃ śeṣadarśanaṃ //
240.d:
अविज्ञातस्य विज्ञानं विज्ञातस्य च निश् चयः /
अर्थद्वैधस्य सन्देहच्छेदनं शेषदर्शनं //
240.m:
Ascertaining the unknown, determining the known,
resolving doubt in two conflicting alternatives, and discerning the rest;

240.s:
sahāyāḥ sādhanopāyā vibhāgo deśakālayoḥ /
vipatteś ca pratīkāraḥ pañcāṅgo mantra iṣyate(1) //
240.d:
सहायाः साधनोपाया विभागो देशकालयोः /
विपत्तेश् च प्रतीकारः पञ्चाङ्गो मन्त्र इष्यते(1) //
240.m:
allies, means of accomplishment, allocation of place and time,
and counteraction against disaster—counsel is held to have five limbs.

240.s:
manaḥprasādaḥ śraddhā ca tathā karaṇapāṭavaṃ /
sahāyotthānasampacca karmaṇāṃ siddhilakṣaṇaṃ //
240.d:
मनःप्रसादः श्रद्धा च तथा करणपाटवं /
सहायोत्थानसम्पच्च कर्मणां सिद्धिलक्षणं //
240.m:
Clarity of mind, faith, skill in execution,
and excellence in mobilizing assistants—these are the signs of success in actions.

240.s:
madaḥ pramādaḥ kāmaś ca suptapralapitāni ca /
bhindanti mantraṃ pracchannāḥ kāminyo ramatāntathā //
240.d:
मदः प्रमादः कामश् च सुप्तप्रलपितानि च /
भिन्दन्ति मन्त्रं प्रच्छन्नाः कामिन्यो रमतान्तथा //
240.m:
Intoxication, heedlessness, passion, talking in sleep,
and concealed passionate women while dallying disclose counsel.

240.s:
pragalbhaḥ smṛtimānvāgmīśastre śāstre ca niṣṭhitaḥ /
abhyastakarmā nṛpaterdūto bhaviturmarhati //
240.d:
प्रगल्भः स्मृतिमान्वाग्मीशस्त्रे शास्त्रे च निष्ठितः /
अभ्यस्तकर्मा नृपतेर्दूतो भवितुर्मर्हति //
240.m:
Bold, possessing memory, eloquent, proficient in weapons and treatises,
and practiced in administration—such a man is fit to be an envoy for a king.

240.s:
nisṛṣṭārtho mitārthaś ca tathā śāsanahārakaḥ(2) /
sāmarthyāt pādato hīno dūtastu trividhaḥ smṛtaḥ //
240.d:
निसृष्टार्थो मितार्थश् च तथा शासनहारकः(2) /
सामर्थ्यात् पादतो हीनो दूतस्तु त्रिविधः स्मृतः //
240.m:
With plenipotentiary power, with limited instructions, and a bearer of a decree—
an envoy is considered threefold, each inferior by a quarter in capacity.

240.s:
nāvijñātaṃ puraṃ śatroḥ praviśecca na śaṃsadaṃ /
:n
1 naya iṣyate iti kha.. , gha.. ca
2 śāsanaśāsaka iti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 370
kālamīkṣeta kāryārthamanujñātaś ca niṣpatet //
240.d:
नाविज्ञातं पुरं शत्रोः प्रविशेच्च न शंसदं /
:न्
1 नय इष्यते इति ख.. , घ.. च
2 शासनशासक इति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 370
कालमीक्षेत कार्यार्थमनुज्ञातश् च निष्पतेत् //
240.m:
He should not enter an unknown city of an enemy, nor an assembly;
[Notes]
1 'naya iṣyate' in manuscripts kha and gha.
2 kha and cha read 'śāsanaśāsakaḥ'.
he should watch for the proper time to accomplish his task, and depart when permitted.

240.s:
chidrañca śatrorjānīyāt koṣamitrabalāni ca /
rāgāparāgau jānīyād dṛṣṭigātraviceṣṭitaiḥ(1) //
240.d:
छिद्रञ्च शत्रोर्जानीयात् कोषमित्रबलानि च /
रागापरागौ जानीयाद् दृष्टिगात्रविचेष्टितैः(1) //
240.m:
He should learn the vulnerable points of the enemy, and his treasury, allies, and armed forces;
he should ascertain affection and disaffection through glances and bodily gestures.

240.s:
kuryāccaturvidhaṃ stortraṃ pakṣayorubhayorapi /
tapasvivyañjanopetaiḥ sucaraiḥ(2) saha saṃvaset //
240.d:
कुर्याच्चतुर्विधं स्तोर्त्रं पक्षयोरुभयोरपि /
तपस्विव्यञ्जनोपेतैः सुचरैः(2) सह संवसेत् //
240.m:
He should offer fourfold praise to both factions;
he should associate with good spies disguised as ascetics.

240.s:
caraḥ prakāśo dūtaḥ syādaprakāśaś caro dvidhā /
baṇik kṛṣībalo liṅgī bhikṣukādyātmakāś carāḥ //
240.d:
चरः प्रकाशो दूतः स्यादप्रकाशश् चरो द्विधा /
बणिक् कृषीबलो लिङ्गी भिक्षुकाद्यात्मकाश् चराः //
240.m:
A spy is twofold: an open spy is an envoy, and a concealed spy;
merchants, farmers, religious mendicants, monks, and the like are spies.

240.s:
yāyādariṃ vyasaninaṃ niṣphale(3) dūtaceṣṭite /
prakṛtavyasanaṃ yatsyāttat samīkṣya samutpatet //
240.d:
यायादरिं व्यसनिनं निष्फले(3) दूतचेष्टिते /
प्रकृतव्यसनं यत्स्यात्तत् समीक्ष्य समुत्पतेत् //
240.m:
He should march against an enemy beset by calamity when the work of the envoy proves fruitless;
observing whatever calamity affects the elements of sovereignty, he should spring into action.

240.s:
anayādvyasyati śreyastasmāttadvyasanaṃ smṛtaṃ /
hutāśano jalaṃ vyādhirdurbhikṣaṃ marakaṃ tathā //
240.d:
अनयाद्व्यस्यति श्रेयस्तस्मात्तद्व्यसनं स्मृतं /
हुताशनो जलं व्याधिर्दुर्भिक्षं मरकं तथा //
240.m:
Because through mismanagement good fortune deteriorates, it is therefore called a calamity.
Fire, water, disease, famine, and pestilence—

240.s:
iti pañcavidhaṃ daivaṃ vyasanaṃ mānuṣaṃ paraṃ /
daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa śāntyā ca praśamannayet //
240.d:
इति पञ्चविधं दैवं व्यसनं मानुषं परं /
दैवं पुरुषकारेण शान्त्या च प्रशमन्नयेत् //
240.m:
thus calamity from fate is fivefold; that caused by humans is another.
One should pacify [calamity] from fate through human effort and pacifying rites;

240.s:
utthāpitena nītyā ca mānuṣaṃ vyasanaṃ haret /
mantro mantraphalāvāptiḥ kāryānuṣṭhānamāyatiḥ //
240.d:
उत्थापितेन नीत्या च मानुषं व्यसनं हरेत् /
मन्त्रो मन्त्रफलावाप्तिः कार्यानुष्ठानमायतिः //
240.m:
and he should avert human calamity through initiative and policy.
Counsel, securing the fruit of counsel, execution of tasks, future prosperity,

240.s:
āyavyayau daṇḍanītiramitrapratiṣedhanaṃ /
vyasanasya pratīkāro rājyarājābhirakṣaṇaṃ //
240.d:
आयव्ययौ दण्डनीतिरमित्रप्रतिषेधनं /
व्यसनस्य प्रतीकारो राज्यराजाभिरक्षणं //
240.m:
revenue and expenditure, the science of politics, restraining enemies,
remedying calamity, and protecting the kingdom and the king—

240.s:
ityamātyasya karmedaṃ hanti savyasanānvitaḥ /
hiraṇyadhānyavastrāṇi vāhanaṃ prajayā bhavet //
240.d:
इत्यमात्यस्य कर्मेदं हन्ति सव्यसनान्वितः /
हिरण्यधान्यवस्त्राणि वाहनं प्रजया भवेत् //
240.m:
such is the duty of the minister; if afflicted with calamity, he ruins this.
Gold, grain, garments, and mounts come from the subjects;

240.s:
tathānye dravyanicayā danti savyasanā prajā /
prajānāmāpadisthānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ koṣadaṇḍayoḥ //
:n
1 dṛṣṭivaktraviceṣṭitair iti ga.. , gha.. , cha.. , jha.. , ña.. ca
2 svacarair iti ja..
3 viphale iti gha.. , jha.. , ña.. ca
:p 371
240.d:
तथान्ये द्रव्यनिचया दन्ति सव्यसना प्रजा /
प्रजानामापदिस्थानां रक्षणं कोषदण्डयोः //
:न्
1 दृष्टिवक्त्रविचेष्टितैर् इति ग.. , घ.. , छ.. , झ.. , ञ.. च
2 स्वचरैर् इति ज..
3 विफले इति घ.. , झ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 371
240.m:
likewise other collections of goods; subjects afflicted with calamity ruin them.
The protection of subjects placed in misfortune, and of treasury and army,
[Notes]
1 'dṛṣṭivaktraviceṣṭitaiḥ' in manuscripts ga, gha, cha, jha, and ña.
2 'svacaraiḥ' in manuscript ja.
3 gha, jha, and ña read 'viphale'.

240.s:
paurādyāścopakurvanti saṃśrayādiha durdinaṃ /
tūṣṇīṃ yuddhaṃ janatrāṇaṃ mitrāmitraparigrahaḥ //
240.d:
पौराद्याश्चोपकुर्वन्ति संश्रयादिह दुर्दिनं /
तूष्णीं युद्धं जनत्राणं मित्रामित्रपरिग्रहः //
240.m:
and citizens and others assist here when refuge [is sought] in bad times;
silent warfare, protecting the people, winning over allies and enemies,

240.s:
sāmantādi kṛte doṣe naśyettadvyasanācca tat /
bhṛtyānāṃ bharaṇaṃ dānaṃ prajāmitraparigrahaḥ //
240.d:
सामन्तादि कृते दोषे नश्येत्तद्व्यसनाच्च तत् /
भृत्यानां भरणं दानं प्रजामित्रपरिग्रहः //
240.m:
when harm is done by vassal kings and others, that perishes through their calamity.
Supporting servants, giving gifts, embracing subjects and allies,

240.s:
dharmakāmādibhedaś ca durgasaṃskārabhūṣaṇaṃ /
koṣāttadvyasanāddhanti koṣamūlo hi bhūpatiḥ //
240.d:
धर्मकामादिभेदश् च दुर्गसंस्कारभूषणं /
कोषात्तद्व्यसनाद्धन्ति कोषमूलो हि भूपतिः //
240.m:
pursuing dharma, kāma, and the like, and repairing and adorning the fortress—
[all this comes] from the treasury; calamity thereof destroys it, for a king is rooted in his treasury.

240.s:
mitrāmitrāvanīhemasādhanaṃ ripumardanaṃ /
dūrakāryāśukāritvaṃ daṇḍāttadvyasanāddharet //
240.d:
मित्रामित्रावनीहेमसाधनं रिपुमर्दनं /
दूरकार्याशुकारित्वं दण्डात्तद्व्यसनाद्धरेत् //
240.m:
Gaining allies, enemies, territory, and gold, crushing foes,
and swift execution of distant tasks [come] from the army; calamity thereof destroys that.

240.s:
sastambhayati mitrāṇi amitraṃ nāśayatyapi /
dhanādyair upakāritvaṃ mitrāttadvyasanāddharet(1) //
240.d:
सस्तम्भयति मित्राणि अमित्रं नाशयत्यपि /
धनाद्यैर् उपकारित्वं मित्रात्तद्व्यसनाद्धरेत्(1) //
240.m:
It supports allies and even destroys the enemy;
assistance through wealth and the like comes from the ally; calamity thereof removes that.

240.s:
rājā savyasanī hanyādrājakāryāṇi yāni ca /
vāgdaṇḍayoś ca pāruṣyamarthadūṣaṇameva ca //
240.d:
राजा सव्यसनी हन्याद्राजकार्याणि यानि च /
वाग्दण्डयोश् च पारुष्यमर्थदूषणमेव च //
240.m:
A king afflicted with calamity destroys royal affairs whatever they may be:
harshness of speech and of punishment, and misuse of wealth;

240.s:
pānaṃ strī mṛgayā dyūtaṃ vyasanāni mahīpateḥ /
ālasyaṃ stabdhatā darpaḥ pramādo dvaidhakāritā //
240.d:
पानं स्त्री मृगया द्यूतं व्यसनानि महीपतेः /
आलस्यं स्तब्धता दर्पः प्रमादो द्वैधकारिता //
240.m:
drinking, women, hunting, and gambling are the calamities of the king;
indolence, stubbornness, arrogance, heedlessness, and duplicity—

240.s:
iti pūrvopadiṣṭañca sacivavyasanaṃ smṛtaṃ /
anāvṛṣṭiś ca pīḍādau rāṣṭravyasanamucyate //
240.d:
इति पूर्वोपदिष्टञ्च सचिवव्यसनं स्मृतं /
अनावृष्टिश् च पीडादौ राष्ट्रव्यसनमुच्यते //
240.m:
these, taught previously, are considered the calamities of the minister.
Drought and oppression [by thieves], etc., are called the calamities of the realm.

240.s:
viśīrṇayantraprākāraparikhātvamaśastratā /
kṣīṇayā senayā naddhaṃ durgavyasanamucyate //
240.d:
विशीर्णयन्त्रप्राकारपरिखात्वमशस्त्रता /
क्षीणया सेनया नद्धं दुर्गव्यसनमुच्यते //
240.m:
Broken war-machines, ruined ramparts and moats, lack of weapons,
and being besieged by an exhausted army are called the calamities of the fortress.

240.s:
vyayīkṛtaḥ parikṣipto 'prajito 'sañcitas tathā /
daṣito darasaṃsthaś ca koṣavyasanamucyate //
240.d:
व्ययीकृतः परिक्षिप्तो ऽप्रजितो ऽसञ्चितस् तथा /
दषितो दरसंस्थश् च कोषव्यसनमुच्यते //
240.m:
Squandered, dispersed, non-productive, uncollected,
defiled, and kept in caves is called the calamity of the treasury.

240.s:
uparuddhaṃ parikṣiptamamānitavimānitaṃ /
:n
1 saṃstambhayatītyādiḥ, mitrāttadvyasanāddharedityantaḥ
pāṭhaḥ cha.puatake nāsti
:p 372
abhūtaṃ vyādhitaṃ śrāntaṃ dūrāyātannavāgataṃ //
240.d:
उपरुद्धं परिक्षिप्तममानितविमानितं /
:न्
1 संस्तम्भयतीत्यादिः, मित्रात्तद्व्यसनाद्धरेदित्यन्तः
पाठः छ.पुअतके नास्ति
:प् 372
अभूतं व्याधितं श्रान्तं दूरायातन्नवागतं //
240.m:
Besieged, dispersed, unhonored, dishonored,
[Notes]
1 The passage beginning with 'saṃstambhayati' and ending with 'mitrāttadvyasanāddharet' is missing in manuscript cha.
unpaid, diseased, exhausted, arrived from afar, newly arrived,

240.s:
parikṣīṇaṃ pratihataṃ prahatāgratarantathā /
āśānirvedabhūyiṣṭhamanṛtaprāptameva ca //
240.d:
परिक्षीणं प्रतिहतं प्रहताग्रतरन्तथा /
आशानिर्वेदभूयिष्ठमनृतप्राप्तमेव च //
240.m:
depleted, repulsed, whose frontline is struck down,
abounding in despair and dejection, and deceived by lies—

240.s:
kalatragarbhannikṣiptamantaḥśalpaṃ tathaiva ca /
vicchinnavīvadhāsāraṃ śūnyamūlaṃ tathaiva ca //
240.d:
कलत्रगर्भन्निक्षिप्तमन्तःशल्पं तथैव च /
विच्छिन्नवीवधासारं शून्यमूलं तथैव च //
240.m: Where wives and children are placed in the center, where there is an internal thorn, / where supplies and reinforcements are cut off, where the base is left empty,

240.s:
asvāmyasaṃhataṃ vāpi bhinnakūṭaṃ tathaiva ca /
duṣpārṣṇigrāhamarthañca balavyasanamucyate //
240.d:
अस्वाम्यसंहतं वापि भिन्नकूटं तथैव च /
दुष्पार्ष्णिग्राहमर्थञ्च बलव्यसनमुच्यते //
240.m: where there is no lord or unity, where the front rank is broken, / where the rear is difficult to protect, and [lacking] wealth—this is said to be distress of the army.

240.s:
daivopapīḍitaṃ mitraṃ grastaṃ śatrubalena ca /
kāmakrodhādisaṃyuktamutsāhādaribhirbhavet //
240.d:
दैवोपपीडितं मित्रं ग्रस्तं शत्रुबलेन च /
कामक्रोधादिसंयुक्तमुत्साहादरिभिर्भवेत् //
240.m: When an ally is oppressed by fate, seized by an enemy army, / or associated with lust, anger, and the like, [distress] may arise from energetic enemies.

240.s:
arthasya dūṣaṇaṃ krodhāt pāruṣyaṃ vākyadaṇḍayoḥ /
kāmajaṃ mṛgayā dyūtaṃ vyasanaṃ pānakaṃ striyaḥ //
240.d:
अर्थस्य दूषणं क्रोधात् पारुष्यं वाक्यदण्डयोः /
कामजं मृगया द्यूतं व्यसनं पानकं स्त्रियः //
240.m: Abuse of wealth arises from anger, as does harshness of speech and of punishment; / the vices born of desire are hunting, gambling, drinking, and women.

240.s:
vākpāruṣyaṃ paraṃ loke udvejanamanarthakaṃ /
asiddhasādhanaṃ daṇḍastaṃ yuktyānayennṛpaḥ //
240.d:
वाक्पारुष्यं परं लोके उद्वेजनमनर्थकं /
असिद्धसाधनं दण्डस्तं युक्त्यानयेन्नृपः //
240.m: Harshness of speech in this world causes extreme agitation and is profitless; / punishment should accomplish what has not been accomplished; the king should apply it prudently.

240.s:
udvejayati bhūtāni daṇḍapāruṣyavān nṛpaḥ /
bhūtānyudvejyamānāni dviṣatāṃ yānti saṃśrayaṃ //
240.d:
उद्वेजयति भूतानि दण्डपारुष्यवान् नृपः /
भूतान्युद्वेज्यमानानि द्विषतां यान्ति संश्रयं //
240.m: A king given to harsh punishment terrifies living beings; / and terrified beings seek the protection of his enemies.

240.s:
vivṛddhāḥ śatravaś caiva vināśāya bhavanti te /
dūṣyasya dūṣaṇārthañca parityāgo mahīyasaḥ //
240.d:
विवृद्धाः शत्रवश् चैव विनाशाय भवन्ति ते /
दूष्यस्य दूषणार्थञ्च परित्यागो महीयसः //
240.m: Those enemies, grown powerful, lead to his destruction. / The abandonment of a worthy person in order to corrupt a corruptible one,

240.s:
arthasya nītitattvajñair arthadūṣaṇamucyate /
pānāt kāryādino jñānaṃ mṛgayāto 'ritaḥ kṣayaḥ //
240.d:
अर्थस्य नीतितत्त्वज्ञैर् अर्थदूषणमुच्यते /
पानात् कार्यादिनो ज्ञानं मृगयातो ऽरितः क्षयः //
240.m: is called abuse of wealth by those who know the principles of polity. / From drinking arises lack of judgment in duty and the like; from hunting comes destruction by an enemy.

240.s:
jitaśramārthaṃ mṛgayāṃ vicaredrakṣite vane /
dharmārthaprāṇamāśādi dyūte syāt kalahādikaṃ //
240.d:
जितश्रमार्थं मृगयां विचरेद्रक्षिते वने /
धर्मार्थप्राणमाशादि द्यूते स्यात् कलहादिकं //
240.m: To overcome fatigue, one should practice hunting in a protected forest. / In gambling, there is loss of righteousness, wealth, life, and the like, as well as quarrels and such.

240.s:
kālātipāto dharmārthapī.rā strīvyasanādbhavet /
pānadoṣāt prāṇanāśaḥ kāryākāryāviniś cayaḥ //
:p 373
240.d:
कालातिपातो धर्मार्थपी.रा स्त्रीव्यसनाद्भवेत् /
पानदोषात् प्राणनाशः कार्याकार्याविनिश् चयः //
:प् 373
240.m:
Loss of time and obstruction of righteousness and wealth arise from attachment to women; / from the vice of drinking comes loss of life and inability to discern what should and should not be done.
[Page 373]

240.s:
skandhāvāraniveśajño nimittajño ripuṃ jayet /
skandhāvārasya madhye tu sakoṣaṃ nṛpatergṛhaṃ //
240.d:
स्कन्धावारनिवेशज्ञो निमित्तज्ञो रिपुं जयेत् /
स्कन्धावारस्य मध्ये तु सकोषं नृपतेर्गृहं //
240.m: One who knows how to lay out an encampment and knows omens will conquer the enemy. / In the center of the encampment should be the king's dwelling, together with the treasury.

240.s:
maulībhūtaṃ śreṇisuhṛddviṣadāṭavikaṃ balaṃ /
rājaharmyaṃ samāvṛtya krameṇa viniveśayet(1) //
240.d:
मौलीभूतं श्रेणिसुहृद्द्विषदाटविकं बलं /
राजहर्म्यं समावृत्य क्रमेण विनिवेशयेत्(1) //
240.m: The hereditary forces, guild troops, friendly troops, enemy [auxiliaries], and forest-dwelling troops / should be stationed in sequence, surrounding the royal residence.

240.s:
sainyaikadeśaḥ sannaddhaḥ senāpatipuraḥsaraḥ /
paribhrameccatvarāṃś ca maṇḍalena vahir niśi //
240.d:
सैन्यैकदेशः सन्नद्धः सेनापतिपुरःसरः /
परिभ्रमेच्चत्वरांश् च मण्डलेन वहिर् निशि //
240.m: A section of the army, fully equipped and preceded by the commander-in-chief, / should patrol the squares outside the perimeter at night.

240.s:
vārtāḥ svakā vijānīyāddarasīmāntacāriṇaḥ /
nirgacchet praviśeccaiva sarva evopalakṣitaḥ //
240.d:
वार्ताः स्वका विजानीयाद्दरसीमान्तचारिणः /
निर्गच्छेत् प्रविशेच्चैव सर्व एवोपलक्षितः //
240.m: He should gather his own intelligence regarding those roaming the distant frontiers; / everyone who goes out and comes in must be carefully observed.

240.s:
sāmadānaṃ ca bhedaś ca daṇḍopekṣendrajālakaṃ /
māyopāyāḥ sapta pare nikṣipetsādhanāya tān //
240.d:
सामदानं च भेदश् च दण्डोपेक्षेन्द्रजालकं /
मायोपायाः सप्त परे निक्षिपेत्साधनाय तान् //
240.m: Conciliation, bribery, causing division, punishment, overlooking, and trickery, / along with deception—these seven are the expedients; he should employ them against others to achieve success.

240.s:
caturvidhaṃ smṛtaṃ sāma upakārānukīrtanāt /
mithaḥsambanhdakathanaṃ mṛdupūrvaṃ ca bhāṣaṇaṃ //
240.d:
चतुर्विधं स्मृतं साम उपकारानुकीर्तनात् /
मिथःसम्बन्ह्दकथनं मृदुपूर्वं च भाषणं //
240.m: Conciliation is declared to be of four kinds: proclaiming past benefits, / recounting mutual ties, speaking gently,

240.s:
āyāte darśanaṃ vācā tavāhamiti cārpaṇaṃ /
yaḥ samprāptadhanotsarga uttamādhamamadhyamaḥ //
240.d:
आयाते दर्शनं वाचा तवाहमिति चार्पणं /
यः सम्प्राप्तधनोत्सर्ग उत्तमाधममध्यमः //
240.m: granting an audience when one arrives, and surrendering oneself in speech, saying, 'I am yours.' / The gift of wealth received is considered highest, lowest, or middling:

240.s:
pratidānaṃ tadā tasya gṛhītasyānumodanaṃ /
dravyadānamapūrvaṃ ca svayaṅgrāhapravartanaṃ(2) //
240.d:
प्रतिदानं तदा तस्य गृहीतस्यानुमोदनं /
द्रव्यदानमपूर्वं च स्वयङ्ग्राहप्रवर्तनं(2) //
240.m: returning a gift, approving what has been received, / giving unprecedented wealth, and allowing self-seizure [of booty].

240.s:
deyaś ca pratimokṣaś ca dānaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtaṃ /
sneharāgāpanayanasaṃharṣotpādanaṃ tathā //
240.d:
देयश् च प्रतिमोक्षश् च दानं पञ्चविधं स्मृतं /
स्नेहरागापनयनसंहर्षोत्पादनं तथा //
240.m: Things to be given, and release [of what has been seized], dāna is remembered as being of five kinds. / Likewise, the removal of affection and love, and the generation of rivalry,

240.s:
mitho bhedaś ca bhedajñair bhedaś ca trividhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
badho 'rthaharaṇaṃ caiva parikleśastridhā damaḥ //
240.d:
मिथो भेदश् च भेदज्ञैर् भेदश् च त्रिविधः स्मृतः /
बधो ऽर्थहरणं चैव परिक्लेशस्त्रिधा दमः //
240.m: and discord among one another: [thus] dissension is remembered as three-fold by those skilled in dissension. / Killing, seizure of property, and harassment—[thus] punishment is three-fold.

240.s:
prakāśaścāprakāśaś ca lokadviṣṭān prakāśataḥ /
udvijeta hatair lokasteṣu piṇḍaḥ praśasyate //
:n
1 pariveśayediti kha..
2 tathaiva supravartanamiti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 374
240.d:
प्रकाशश्चाप्रकाशश् च लोकद्विष्टान् प्रकाशतः /
उद्विजेत हतैर् लोकस्तेषु पिण्डः प्रशस्यते //
:न्
1 परिवेशयेदिति ख..
2 तथैव सुप्रवर्तनमिति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 374
240.m:
It is open and secret. Those hated by the people [should be dealt with] openly. / The people tremble at those who have been slain, so a [direct] blow is commended against them.
[...]
1. "pariveśayet" in manuscript kha.
2. "tathaiva supravartanam" in manuscripts ja. and ṭa. / [p. 376]

240.s:
viśeṣeṇopaniṣidyogair hanyācchastrādinā dviṣaḥ /
jātimātraṃ dvijaṃ naiva hanyāt sāmottaraṃ vaśe //
240.d:
विशेषेणोपनिषिद्योगैर् हन्याच्छस्त्रादिना द्विषः /
जातिमात्रं द्विजं नैव हन्यात् सामोत्तरं वशे //
240.m: Especially through esoteric devices he should strike enemies with weapons and the like; / he should never strike a twice-born merely by caste;conciliation should be the foremost means in bringing [him] under control.

240.s:
pralimpanniva cetāṃsi dṛṣṭvāsādhu pibanniva /
grasannivāmṛtaṃ sāma prayuñjīta priyaṃ vacaḥ //
240.d:
प्रलिम्पन्निव चेतांसि दृष्ट्वासाधु पिबन्निव /
ग्रसन्निवामृतं साम प्रयुञ्जीत प्रियं वचः //
240.m: As if anointing minds, drinking it in, looking gently, / as if swallowing nectar, one should employ conciliation, [namely] sweet speech.

240.s:
mithyābhiśastaḥ śrīkāma āhūyāpratimānitaḥ /
rājadveṣī cātikara ātmasambhāvitas tathā //
240.d:
मिथ्याभिशस्तः श्रीकाम आहूयाप्रतिमानितः /
राजद्वेषी चातिकर आत्मसम्भावितस् तथा //
240.m: One falsely accused, one seeking wealth, one summoned and not respected, / one who hates the king, an extortionist of taxes, and one who thinks too highly of himself,

240.s:
vicchinnadharmakāmārthaḥ kruddho mānī vimānitaḥ /
akāraṇāt parityaktaḥ kṛtavairo 'pi sāntvitaḥ //
240.d:
विच्छिन्नधर्मकामार्थः क्रुद्धो मानी विमानितः /
अकारणात् परित्यक्तः कृतवैरो ऽपि सान्त्वितः //
240.m: one deprived of virtue, pleasure, and wealth, one enraged, proud, insulted, / one abandoned without cause, and even one reconciled after enmity has been made,

240.s:
hṛtadravyakalatraś ca pūjārho 'pratipūjitaḥ /
etāṃstu bhedayecchatrau sthitānnityān suśaṅkitān //
240.d:
हृतद्रव्यकलत्रश् च पूजार्हो ऽप्रतिपूजितः /
एतांस्तु भेदयेच्छत्रौ स्थितान्नित्यान् सुशङ्कितान् //
240.m: one whose property and wife have been seized, and one worthy of honor who was not honored— / he should cause dissension among these when they reside with the enemy, being constantly suspicious of them.

240.s:
āgatān pūjayet kāmair nijāṃś ca praśamannayet /
sāmadṛṣṭānusandhānamatyugrabhayadarśanaṃ //
240.d:
आगतान् पूजयेत् कामैर् निजांश् च प्रशमन्नयेत् /
सामदृष्टानुसन्धानमत्युग्रभयदर्शनं //
240.m: When they arrive, he should honor them with desires and pacify his own men. / Reconciliation, scrutiny of aims, presentation of severe terrors,

240.s:
pradhānadānamānaṃ ca bhedopāyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
mitraṃ hataṃ kāṣṭhamiva ghuṇajagdhaṃ viśīryate //
240.d:
प्रधानदानमानं च भेदोपायाः प्रकीर्तिताः /
मित्रं हतं काष्ठमिव घुणजग्धं विशीर्यते //
240.m: and gifts and honors to chiefs are proclaimed as the expedients of dissension. / An ally who is struck falls apart like wood eaten away by woodworms.

240.s:
triśaktirdeśakālajño daṇḍenāstaṃ nayedarīn /
maitrīpradhānaṃ kalyāṇabuddhiṃ sāntvena sādhayet //
240.d:
त्रिशक्तिर्देशकालज्ञो दण्डेनास्तं नयेदरीन् /
मैत्रीप्रधानं कल्याणबुद्धिं सान्त्वेन साधयेत् //
240.m: Endowed with the three powers and knowing time and place, he should bring foes to ruin with force; / one whose chief aim is friendship and whose mind is benevolent he should manage through conciliation.

240.s:
lubdhaṃ kṣīṇañca dānena mitrānanyonyaśaṅkayā /
daṇḍasya darśanādduṣṭān putrabhrātādi sāmataḥ //
240.d:
लुब्धं क्षीणञ्च दानेन मित्रानन्योन्यशङ्कया /
दण्डस्य दर्शनाद्दुष्टान् पुत्रभ्रातादि सामतः //
240.m: The greedy and the weakened [he should manage] with gifts; allies, by [instilling] mutual suspicion; / the wicked, through the display of punishment; sons, brothers, and the like, through conciliation;

240.s:
dānabhedaiś camūmukhyān yodhān(1) janapadadikān /
sāmāntāṭavikān bhedadaṇḍābhyāmaparāddhakān //
240.d:
दानभेदैश् चमूमुख्यान् योधान्(1) जनपददिकान् /
सामान्ताटविकान् भेददण्डाभ्यामपराद्धकान् //
240.m: generals, by gifts and dissension; warriors and regional inhabitants [by the same]; / neighboring forest dwellers through dissension and punishment, and wrongdoers likewise.

240.s:
devatāpratimānantu pūjayāntargatair naraiḥ /
pumān strīvastrasaṃvīto niśi cādbhutadarśanaḥ //
:n
1 dānabhedaiś caiva mukhyān paurāniti ja..
:p 375
240.d:
देवताप्रतिमानन्तु पूजयान्तर्गतैर् नरैः /
पुमान् स्त्रीवस्त्रसंवीतो निशि चाद्भुतदर्शनः //
:न्
1 दानभेदैश् चैव मुख्यान् पौरानिति ज..
:प् 375
240.m:
By means of men placed inside images of deities during worship, / or a man clothed in women's garments, looking wondrous at night,
[...]
1. "dānabhedaiś caiva mukhyān paurān" in manuscript ja. / [p. 375]

240.s:
vetālolkāpiśācānāṃ śivānāṃ ca svarūpakī /
kāmato rūpadhāritvaṃ śastrāgnyaśmāmbuvarṣaṇaṃ //
240.d:
वेतालोल्कापिशाचानां शिवानां च स्वरूपकी /
कामतो रूपधारित्वं शस्त्राग्न्यश्माम्बुवर्षणं //
240.m: taking on the forms of vetālas, meteors, piśācas, and jackals, / assuming shapes at will, raining weapons, fire, stones, and water,

240.s:
tamo 'nilo 'nalo megha iti māyā hy amānuṣī /
jaghāna kīcakaṃ bhīma āsthitaḥ strīrūpatāṃ //
240.d:
तमो ऽनिलो ऽनलो मेघ इति माया ह्य् अमानुषी /
जघान कीचकं भीम आस्थितः स्त्रीरूपतां //
240.m: darkness, wind, fire, and clouds—this is superhuman illusion. / Bhīma slew Kīcaka by assuming the form of a woman.

240.s:
anyāye vyasane yuddhe pravṛttasyānivāraṇaṃ /
upekṣeyaṃ smṛtā bhrātopekṣitaś ca hiḍimbayā //
240.d:
अन्याये व्यसने युद्धे प्रवृत्तस्यानिवारणं /
उपेक्षेयं स्मृता भ्रातोपेक्षितश् च हिडिम्बया //
240.m: Not restraining one engaged in injustice, vice, or battle— / this is known as indifference; and [her own] brother was disregarded by Hiḍimbā.

240.s:
meghāndhakāravṛṣṭyagniparvatādbhutadarśanaṃ /
darasthānaṃ ca sainyānāṃ darśanaṃ dhvajaśālināṃ //
240.d:
मेघान्धकारवृष्ट्यग्निपर्वताद्भुतदर्शनं /
दरस्थानं च सैन्यानां दर्शनं ध्वजशालिनां //
240.m: Showing the marvels of clouds, darkness, rain, fire, and mountains, / and displaying a frightening station of troops possessed of banners,

240.s:
chinnapāṭitabhinnānāṃ saṃsṛtānāṃ ca darśanaṃ /
itīndrajālaṃ dviṣatāmbhotyarthamupakalpayet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sāmādirnāma
catvāriṃśadadhkadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ekacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājanītiḥ
240.d:
छिन्नपाटितभिन्नानां संसृतानां च दर्शनं /
इतीन्द्रजालं द्विषताम्भोत्यर्थमुपकल्पयेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सामादिर्नाम
चत्वारिंशदध्कद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ एकचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजनीतिः
240.m:
and displaying [warriors] cut down, torn apart, broken, and moving about— / thus one should employ sorcery for the terror of enemies.
Thus ends the two hundred and fortieth chapter, named "Conciliation and the Other Expedients," in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the two hundred and forty-first chapter:
Statecraft.

241.s:
rāma uvāca
ṣaḍvidhantu balaṃ vyūhya devān prārcya ripuṃ vrajet /
maulaṃ bhūtaṃ śroṇisuhṛddviṣadāṭavikaṃ balaṃ //
241.d:
राम उवाच
षड्विधन्तु बलं व्यूह्य देवान् प्रार्च्य रिपुं व्रजेत् /
मौलं भूतं श्रोणिसुहृद्द्विषदाटविकं बलं //
241.m: Rāma said: / Having arrayed the six-fold army and having worshipped the gods, he should march against the enemy: / the hereditary army, the hired army, the guild-army, the allied army, the enemy troops, and the forest army.

241.s:
pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ garīyastu balānāṃ vyasanaṃ tathā /
ṣaḍaṅgaṃ mantrakoṣābhyāṃ padātyaśvarathadvipaiḥ //
241.d:
पूर्वं पूर्वं गरीयस्तु बलानां व्यसनं तथा /
षडङ्गं मन्त्रकोषाभ्यां पदात्यश्वरथद्विपैः //
241.m: Each preceding one is more important, and likewise is the calamity of the armies. / [The army is] six-limbed through counsel and the treasury, and with infantry, horses, chariots, and elephants.

241.s:
nadyadravanadurgeṣu yatra yatra bhayaṃ bhavet /
:p 376
senāpatistatra tatra gacchedvyūhīkṛtair balaiḥ //
241.d:
नद्यद्रवनदुर्गेषु यत्र यत्र भयं भवेत् /
:प् 376
सेनापतिस्तत्र तत्र गच्छेद्व्यूहीकृतैर् बलैः //
241.m:
At rivers, mountains, and forest fortresses, wherever there may be danger,
[p. 376]
the commander-in-chief should advance there with troops arrayed in battle formations.

241.s:
nāyakaḥ purato yāyāt pravīrapuruṣāvṛtaḥ /
madhye kalatraṃ svāmī ca koṣaḥ phalgu ca yadbalaṃ //
241.d:
नायकः पुरतो यायात् प्रवीरपुरुषावृतः /
मध्ये कलत्रं स्वामी च कोषः फल्गु च यद्बलं //
241.m: The leader should go in front surrounded by champion men; / in the center should be the wife, the master, the treasury, and whatever troop is weak.

241.s:
pārśvayorubhayoraśvā vājināṃ pārśvayo rathāḥ /
rathānāṃ pārśvayornāgā nāgānāṃ cāṭavībalaṃ //
241.d:
पार्श्वयोरुभयोरश्वा वाजिनां पार्श्वयो रथाः /
रथानां पार्श्वयोर्नागा नागानां चाटवीबलं //
241.m: On both sides should be horses; on the sides of the horses, chariots; / on the sides of the chariots, elephants; and on the sides of the elephants, the forest force.

241.s:
paścāt senāpatiḥ sarvaṃ puraskṛtya kṛtī svayaṃ /
yāyātsannaddhasainyaughaḥ khinnānāśvāsayañcchanaiḥ //
241.d:
पश्चात् सेनापतिः सर्वं पुरस्कृत्य कृती स्वयं /
यायात्सन्नद्धसैन्यौघः खिन्नानाश्वासयञ्च्छनैः //
241.m: The commander-in-chief, capable himself, placing everyone in front, / should advance behind with a prepared mass of troops, gently encouraging the weary.

241.s:
yāyādvyūhena mahatā makareṇa purobhaye /
śyenenoddhṛtapakṣeṇa sūcyā vā vīravaktrayā //
241.d:
यायाद्व्यूहेन महता मकरेण पुरोभये /
श्येनेनोद्धृतपक्षेण सूच्या वा वीरवक्त्रया //
241.m: When danger is in front, he should advance in a great makara array, / or with a hawk array with raised wings, or with a needle array having heroes at its point.

241.s:
paścādbhaye tu śakaṭaṃ pārśvayorvajrasañjñitaṃ(1) /
sarvataḥ sarvatobhadraṃ bhaye vyūhaṃ prakalpayet //
241.d:
पश्चाद्भये तु शकटं पार्श्वयोर्वज्रसञ्ज्ञितं(1) /
सर्वतः सर्वतोभद्रं भये व्यूहं प्रकल्पयेत् //
241.m: When danger is behind, [he should arrange] a cart array; on both flanks, the one named thunderbolt; / when danger is on all sides, he should form the sarvatobhadra array.

241.s:
kandare śailagahane nimnagāvanasaṅkaṭe /
dīrghādhvani pariśrāntaṃ kṣutpipāsāhitaklamaṃ //
241.d:
कन्दरे शैलगहने निम्नगावनसङ्कटे /
दीर्घाध्वनि परिश्रान्तं क्षुत्पिपासाहितक्लमं //
241.m: In a cave, a mountain fastness, a river or forest defile, / fatigued from a long march, distressed by hunger and thirst,

241.s:
vyādhidurbhikṣamarakapīḍitaṃ dasyuvidrutaṃ /
paṅkāṃśujalaskandhaṃ vyastaṃ puñjīkṛtaṃ pathi //
241.d:
व्याधिदुर्भिक्षमरकपीडितं दस्युविद्रुतं /
पङ्कांशुजलस्कन्धं व्यस्तं पुञ्जीकृतं पथि //
241.m: afflicted by disease, famine, and pestilence, routed by bandits, / sunk in mud, dust, or floods of water, scattered or huddled together on the road,

241.s:
prasuptaṃ bhojanavyagramabhūmiṣṭhamasusthitaṃ /
caurāgnibhayavitrastaṃ vṛṣṭivātasamāhataṃ //
241.d:
प्रसुप्तं भोजनव्यग्रमभूमिष्ठमसुस्थितं /
चौराग्निभयवित्रस्तं वृष्टिवातसमाहतं //
241.m: fast asleep, busy with eating, situated on disadvantageous ground, ill-stationed, / terrified by danger of thieves and fire, battered by rain and wind—

241.s:
ityādau svacamūṃ rakṣet prasainyaṃ ca ghatayet /
viśiṣṭo deśakālābhyāṃ bhinnaviprakṛtirbalī //
241.d:
इत्यादौ स्वचमूं रक्षेत् प्रसैन्यं च घतयेत् /
विशिष्टो देशकालाभ्यां भिन्नविप्रकृतिर्बली //
241.m: in these and other conditions he should protect his own army and destroy the hostile army. / Strong and superior in place and time, when the other's disposition is broken,

241.s:
kuryāt prakāśayuddhaṃ hi kūṭayuddhaṃ viparyaye /
teṣvavaskandakāleṣu paraṃ hanyātsamākulaṃ //
:n
1 vajrasaṅkaṭamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 377
241.d:
कुर्यात् प्रकाशयुद्धं हि कूटयुद्धं विपर्यये /
तेष्ववस्कन्दकालेषु परं हन्यात्समाकुलं //
:न्
1 वज्रसङ्कटमिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 377
241.m:
he should indeed wage open warfare; in the reverse case, deceptive warfare. / At those times of surprise attack, he should strike down the enemy when he is threw into confusion.
[...]
1. "vajrasaṅkaṭam" in manuscripts kha. and cha. / [p. 377]

241.s:
abhūmiṣṭhaṃ svabhūmiṣṭhaṃ svabhūmau copajāyataḥ /
prakṛtipragrahākṛṣṭaṃ pāśair vanacarādibhiḥ //
241.d:
अभूमिष्ठं स्वभूमिष्ठं स्वभूमौ चोपजायतः /
प्रकृतिप्रग्रहाकृष्टं पाशैर् वनचरादिभिः //
241.m: When he is on disadvantageous ground while oneself is on advantageous ground, or by subverting him on his own ground, / drawn out through subverting his subjects or with nooses by forest dwellers and the like,

241.s:
hanyāt pravīrapuruṣair bhaṅgadānāpakarṣaṇaiḥ /
purastāddarśanaṃ datvā tallakṣakṛtaniś cayāt //
241.d:
हन्यात् प्रवीरपुरुषैर् भङ्गदानापकर्षणैः /
पुरस्ताद्दर्शनं दत्वा तल्लक्षकृतनिश् चयात् //
241.m: he should strike down with champion men, by feigning flight and drawing him away. / Having shown an appearance in front, since his resolve is fixed on that target,

241.s:
hanyātpaścāt pravīreṇa balenopetya veginā /
paścādvā saṅkulīkṛtya hanyācchūreṇa pūrvataḥ //
241.d:
हन्यात्पश्चात् प्रवीरेण बलेनोपेत्य वेगिना /
पश्चाद्वा सङ्कुलीकृत्य हन्याच्छूरेण पूर्वतः //
241.m: he should strike from behind, approaching swiftly with an elite force; / or having thrown them into confusion from behind, he should strike from the front with a hero.

241.s:
ābhyāṃ pārśvābhighātau tu vyākhyātau kūṭayodhane /
purastādviṣame deśe paścāddhanyāttu vegavān //
241.d:
आभ्यां पार्श्वाभिघातौ तु व्याख्यातौ कूटयोधने /
पुरस्ताद्विषमे देशे पश्चाद्धन्यात्तु वेगवान् //
241.m: Flank attacks in deceptive warfare are explained by these two [methods]. / When the ground in front is uneven, the swift one should strike from behind;

241.s:
puraḥ paścāttu viṣame evameva tu pārśvayoḥ /
prathamaṃ yodhayitvā tu dūṣyāmitrāṭavībalau //
241.d:
पुरः पश्चात्तु विषमे एवमेव तु पार्श्वयोः /
प्रथमं योधयित्वा तु दूष्यामित्राटवीबलौ //
241.m: when it is uneven in front and behind, [he should strike] just so on the flanks. / Having first engaged in battle with seducible, enemy, and forest troops,

241.s:
śrāntaṃ mandannirākrandaṃ hanyādaśrāntavāhanaṃ /
dūṣyāmitrabalair vāpi bhaṅgandatvā prayatnavān //
241.d:
श्रान्तं मन्दन्निराक्रन्दं हन्यादश्रान्तवाहनं /
दूष्यामित्रबलैर् वापि भङ्गन्दत्वा प्रयत्नवान् //
241.m: he should strike down the enemy when he is tired, slow, and without aid, using unwearied mounts; / or indeed, having feigned flight with seducible and enemy troops, exerting himself,

241.s:
jitamityeva viśvastaṃ hanyānmantravyapāśrayaḥ /
skandhāvārapuragrāmaśasyasvāmiprajādiṣu //
241.d:
जितमित्येव विश्वस्तं हन्यान्मन्त्रव्यपाश्रयः /
स्कन्धावारपुरग्रामशस्यस्वामिप्रजादिषु //
241.m: relying on secret plans, he should strike the enemy who is confident that he has won. / In military camps, towns, villages, crops, rulers, and subjects,

241.s:
viśrabhyantaṃ parānīkamapramatto vināśayet /
athavā gograhākṛṣṭaṃ tallakṣyaṃ mārgabandhanāt //
241.d:
विश्रभ्यन्तं परानीकमप्रमत्तो विनाशयेत् /
अथवा गोग्रहाकृष्टं तल्लक्ष्यं मार्गबन्धनात् //
241.m: he should remain alert and destroy the hostile army as it rests in confidence; / or drawn out by a raid on cattle, targeting that by blocking the paths.

241.s:
avaskandabhayādrātripūjāgarakṛtaśramaḥ /
divāsuptaṃ samāhanyānnidrāvyākulasainikaṃ //
241.d:
अवस्कन्दभयाद्रात्रिपूजागरकृतश्रमः /
दिवासुप्तं समाहन्यान्निद्राव्याकुलसैनिकं //
241.m: Exhausted by staying awake at night for fear of an assault, / he should strike down the soldiers asleep by day and bewildered by slumber,

241.s:
niśi viśrabdhasaṃsuptaṃ nāgair vā khaḍgapāṇibhiḥ /
prayāne pūrvayāyitvaṃ vanadurgapraveśanaṃ //
241.d:
निशि विश्रब्धसंसुप्तं नागैर् वा खड्गपाणिभिः /
प्रयाने पूर्वयायित्वं वनदुर्गप्रवेशनं //
241.m: or sound asleep in confidence at night, by means of elephants or sword-bearing men. / In marching, going ahead, entering forest strongholds,

241.s:
abhinnānāmanīkānāṃ bhedanaṃ bhinnasaṅgrahaḥ /
vibhīṣakādvāraghātaṃ koṣarakṣebhakarma ca //
241.d:
अभिन्नानामनीकानां भेदनं भिन्नसङ्ग्रहः /
विभीषकाद्वारघातं कोषरक्षेभकर्म च //
241.m: breaking unbroken battle ranks, rallying broken ones, / intimidating, smashing gates, and protecting the treasury are the work of elephants.

241.s:
abhinnabhedanaṃ mitrasandhānaṃ rathakarma ca /
:p 378
vanadiṅmārgavicaye vīvadhāsāralakṣaṇaṃ //
241.d:
अभिन्नभेदनं मित्रसन्धानं रथकर्म च /
:प् 378
वनदिङ्मार्गविचये वीवधासारलक्षणं //
241.m:
Breaking the unbroken, bringing together allies are the work of chariots,
[p. 378]
and, in surveying the paths and quarters of the forest, observing transport routes and reinforcement.

241.s:
anuyānāpasaraṇe śīghrakāryopapādanaṃ /
dīnānusaraṇaṃ ghātaḥ koṭīnāṃ jaghanasya ca //
241.d:
अनुयानापसरणे शीघ्रकार्योपपादनं /
दीनानुसरणं घातः कोटीनां जघनस्य च //
241.m: Pursuit and retreat, the swift execution of actions, / chasing the distressed, and striking the flanks and the rear;

241.s:
aśvakarmātha patteś ca sarvadā śastradhāraṇaṃ /
śivirasya ca mārgādeḥ śodhanaṃ vastikarma ca //
241.d:
अश्वकर्माथ पत्तेश् च सर्वदा शस्त्रधारणं /
शिविरस्य च मार्गादेः शोधनं वस्तिकर्म च //
241.m: these are the duties of the cavalry. And for the infantry, it is constantly bearing weapons, / clearing the camp and the roads, and guard duty.

241.s:
saṃsthūlasthāṇuvalmīkavṛkṣagulmāpakaṇṭakaṃ /
sāpasārā padātīnāṃ bhūrnātiviṣamā matā //
241.d:
संस्थूलस्थाणुवल्मीकवृक्षगुल्मापकण्टकं /
सापसारा पदातीनां भूर्नातिविषमा मता //
241.m: Ground that has solid, thick tree stumps, anthills, trees, and shrubs, but is free of thorns, / possessing an escape route, and not overly uneven, is considered suitable for infantry.

241.s:
svalpavṛkṣopalā kṣipralaṅghanīyanagā sthirā /
niḥśarkarā vipaṅkā ca sāpasārā ca vājibhūḥ //
241.d:
स्वल्पवृक्षोपला क्षिप्रलङ्घनीयनगा स्थिरा /
निःशर्करा विपङ्का च सापसारा च वाजिभूः //
241.m: Having few trees and stones, with hills quickly passable, firm, / devoid of gravel, free of mud, and providing an escape route—such is ground suitable for cavalry.

241.s:
nisthāṇuvṛkṣakedārā rathabhūmirakardamā /
mardanīyatarucchedyavratatīpaṅkavarjitā //
241.d:
निस्थाणुवृक्षकेदारा रथभूमिरकर्दमा /
मर्दनीयतरुच्छेद्यव्रततीपङ्कवर्जिता //
241.m: Free of tree stumps, trees, and marshy fields, free of mire, / lacking crushable trees, clippable creepers, and mud, is the ground for chariots.

241.s:
nirjharāgamyaśailā(1) ca viṣamā gajamedinī /
urasyādīni bhinnāni pratigṛhṇan balāni hi //
241.d:
निर्झरागम्यशैला(1) च विषमा गजमेदिनी /
उरस्यादीनि भिन्नानि प्रतिगृह्णन् बलानि हि //
241.m: Ground with waterfalls, accessible rocks, and uneven terrain is suitable for elephants. / Collecting the forces such as the center when broken,

241.s:
pratigraha iti khyāto rājakāryāntarakṣamaḥ /
tena śūnyastu yo vyūhaḥ sa bhinna iva lakṣyate //
241.d:
प्रतिग्रह इति ख्यातो राजकार्यान्तरक्षमः /
तेन शून्यस्तु यो व्यूहः स भिन्न इव लक्ष्यते //
241.m: is known as the reserve (*pratigraha*), which is capable of managing other royal enterprises. / An array devoid of it appears as if already broken.

241.s:
jayārthī na ca yuddhyeta matimānapratigrahaḥ /
yatra rājā tatra koṣaḥ koṣādhīnā hi rājatā //
241.d:
जयार्थी न च युद्ध्येत मतिमानप्रतिग्रहः /
यत्र राजा तत्र कोषः कोषाधीना हि राजता //
241.m: One desiring victory and wise should not fight without a reserve. / Where the king is, there is the treasury, and kingship depends on the treasury.

241.s:
yodhebhyastu tato dadyāt kiñciddātuṃ(2) na yujyate /
dravyalakṣaṃ rājaghāte tadardhaṃ tatsutārdane //
241.d:
योधेभ्यस्तु ततो दद्यात् किञ्चिद्दातुं(2) न युज्यते /
द्रव्यलक्षं राजघाते तदर्धं तत्सुतार्दने //
241.m: Therefore, he should give [rewards] to the warriors; it is not proper to give nothing: / a hundred thousand in wealth for killing the [enemy] king, half of that for slaying his son,

241.s:
senāpatibadhe tadvaddadyāddhastyādimardane /
athavā khalu yudhyeran pratyaśvarathadantinaḥ //
:n
1 niḥśarkarā gamyaśaileti ja..
2 kiṃ hi dātumiti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 379
241.d:
सेनापतिबधे तद्वद्दद्याद्धस्त्यादिमर्दने /
अथवा खलु युध्येरन् प्रत्यश्वरथदन्तिनः //
:न्
1 निःशर्करा गम्यशैलेति ज..
2 किं हि दातुमिति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 379
241.m:
