पुरुषलक्षणं

242.s:
agnir uvāca
rāmoktoktā mayā nītiḥ strīṇāṃ rājan nṛṇāṃ vade /
lakṣaṇaṃ yadsamudreṇa gargāyoktaṃ yathā purā //
242.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
रामोक्तोक्ता मया नीतिः स्त्रीणां राजन् नृणां वदे /
लक्षणं यद्समुद्रेण गर्गायोक्तं यथा पुरा //
242.m: Agni said: / The statecraft spoken by Rāma has been told by me. O king, I shall speak of the characteristics / of women and men, as was formerly told by Samudra to Garga.

242.s:
samudra uvāca
puṃsāñca lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye strīṇāñcaiva śubhāśubhaṃ /
ekādhiko dviśukraś ca triganbhīrastathaiva ca //
242.d:
समुद्र उवाच
पुंसाञ्च लक्षणं वक्ष्ये स्त्रीणाञ्चैव शुभाशुभं /
एकाधिको द्विशुक्रश् च त्रिगन्भीरस्तथैव च //
242.m: Samudra said: / I shall describe the auspicious and inauspicious characteristics of men and women: / one having one predominant [quality], two whites, and likewise three deep [parts],

242.s:
tritrikastripralambaś ca tribhirvyāpnoti yas tathā /
tribalīmāṃstrivinatastrikālajñaś ca suvrata //
242.d:
त्रित्रिकस्त्रिप्रलम्बश् च त्रिभिर्व्याप्नोति यस् तथा /
त्रिबलीमांस्त्रिविनतस्त्रिकालज्ञश् च सुव्रत //
242.m: having three triads, three hanging down, and he who pervades by three; / possessing three folds, bent in three, and knowing the three times, O you of noble vows;

242.s:
puruṣaḥ syātsulakṣaṇyo vipulaś ca tathā triṣu /
caturlekhas tathā yaś ca tathaiva ca catuḥsamaḥ //
242.d:
पुरुषः स्यात्सुलक्षण्यो विपुलश् च तथा त्रिषु /
चतुर्लेखस् तथा यश् च तथैव च चतुःसमः //
242.m: a man having auspicious characteristics is broad in three [places], / one who has four lines, and likewise one who is even in four [parts],

242.s:
catuṣkiṣkuś caturdaṃṣṭraḥ śuklakṛṣṇastathaiva ca /
caturgandhaś caturhrasvaḥ sūkṣmadīrghaś ca pañcasu //
242.d:
चतुष्किष्कुश् चतुर्दंष्ट्रः शुक्लकृष्णस्तथैव च /
चतुर्गन्धश् चतुर्ह्रस्वः सूक्ष्मदीर्घश् च पञ्चसु //
242.m: measuring four cubits, having four canine teeth, white and dark, / possessing four fragrances, short in four, and subtle and long in five [places],

242.s:
ṣaḍunnato 'ṣṭavaṃśaś ca saptasneho navāmalaḥ /
daśapadmo daśavyūho nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalaḥ //
242.d:
षडुन्नतो ऽष्टवंशश् च सप्तस्नेहो नवामलः /
दशपद्मो दशव्यूहो न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलः //
242.m: elevated in six, possessing eight lineages, seven glosses, nine purities, / ten lotuses, ten arrays, circular like a banyan tree,

242.s:
caturdaśasamadvandvaḥ ṣoḍaśākṣayaś ca śasyate /
dharmārthakāmasaṃyukto dharmo hy ekādhiko mataḥ //
242.d:
चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्वः षोडशाक्षयश् च शस्यते /
धर्मार्थकामसंयुक्तो धर्मो ह्य् एकाधिको मतः //
242.m: having fourteen equal pairs, and sixteen imperishables is praised. / Endowed with virtue, wealth, and pleasure, virtue is considered the one predominant [quality].

242.s:
tārakābhyāṃ vinā netre śukradanto dviśuklakaḥ /
gambhīrastriśravo nābhiḥ sattvañcaikaṃ trikaṃ smṛtaṃ //
242.d:
तारकाभ्यां विना नेत्रे शुक्रदन्तो द्विशुक्लकः /
गम्भीरस्त्रिश्रवो नाभिः सत्त्वञ्चैकं त्रिकं स्मृतं //
242.m: He who has eyes, apart from the pupils, and teeth white, is 'two-white'. / Three are deep: the voice, the navel, and sattva—this is considered one triad.

242.s:
anasūyā dayā kṣāntirmaṅgalācārayuktatā /
śaucaṃ spṛhā tvakārpaṇyamanāyāsaś ca śauryatā //
:p 384
242.d:
अनसूया दया क्षान्तिर्मङ्गलाचारयुक्तता /
शौचं स्पृहा त्वकार्पण्यमनायासश् च शौर्यता //
:प् 384
242.m:
Absence of malice, compassion, forbearance, devotion to auspicious conduct, / ritual purity, zeal, lack of miserliness, lack of fatigue, and valor—
[Page 384]

242.s:
citrikastripralambaḥ syādvṛṣaṇe bhujayornaraḥ /
digdeśajātivargāṃś ca tejasā yaśasā śriyā //
242.d:
चित्रिकस्त्रिप्रलम्बः स्याद्वृषणे भुजयोर्नरः /
दिग्देशजातिवर्गांश् च तेजसा यशसा श्रिया //
242.m: this is the triad. A man having three hanging down would be [so] in the testicles and the two arms. / And one who pervades directions, countries, and groups of men by his splendor, fame, and fortune,

242.s:
vyāpnoti yastrikavyāpī tribalīmānnarastvasau /
udare balayastisro narantrivinataṃ śṛṇu //
242.d:
व्याप्नोति यस्त्रिकव्यापी त्रिबलीमान्नरस्त्वसौ /
उदरे बलयस्तिस्रो नरन्त्रिविनतं शृणु //
242.m: pervading through three, is 'three-pervading'. That man who has three folds / has three folds on his belly. Hear of the man bent in three:

242.s:
devatānāṃ dvijānāñca gurūṇāṃ praṇatastu yaḥ /
dharmārthakāmakālajñastrikālajño 'bhidhīyate //
242.d:
देवतानां द्विजानाञ्च गुरूणां प्रणतस्तु यः /
धर्मार्थकामकालज्ञस्त्रिकालज्ञो ऽभिधीयते //
242.m: he who bows to deities, twice-born men, and gurus; / one who knows the proper times for virtue, wealth, and pleasure is called 'knower of the three times'.

242.s:
uro lalāṭaṃ vaktrañca trivistīrṇo vilekhavān /
dvau pāṇī dvau tathā pādau dhvajacchatrādibhiryutau //
242.d:
उरो ललाटं वक्त्रञ्च त्रिविस्तीर्णो विलेखवान् /
द्वौ पाणी द्वौ तथा पादौ ध्वजच्छत्रादिभिर्युतौ //
242.m: The chest, forehead, and face [make him] 'broad in three'. Marked with lines: / the two hands and likewise the two feet endowed with [marks of] a banner, parasol, and the like.

242.s:
aṅgulyo hṛdayaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ kaṭiḥ śastaṃ catuḥsamaṃ /
ṣaṇṇavatyaṅgulotsedhaś catuṣkiṣkupramāṇataḥ //
242.d:
अङ्गुल्यो हृदयं पृष्ठं कटिः शस्तं चतुःसमं /
षण्णवत्यङ्गुलोत्सेधश् चतुष्किष्कुप्रमाणतः //
242.m: The fingers, chest, back, and waist are praised as 'even in four'. / The height of ninety-six finger-breadths is by measure 'four cubits'.

242.s:
draṃṣṭrāś catasraś candrābhāś catuḥkṛṣṇaṃ vadāmi te /
netratārau bhruvau śmaśruḥ kṛṣṇāḥ keśāstathaiva ca //
242.d:
द्रंष्ट्राश् चतस्रश् चन्द्राभाश् चतुःकृष्णं वदामि ते /
नेत्रतारौ भ्रुवौ श्मश्रुः कृष्णाः केशास्तथैव च //
242.m: The four canine teeth resemble the moon. I shall tell you the 'four-dark': / the pupils of the eyes, the eyebrows, the beard, and likewise the hair are black.

242.s:
nāsāyāṃ vadane svede kakṣayorviḍagandhakaḥ /
hrasvaṃ liṅgaṃ tathā grīvā jaṅghe syādvedahrasvakaṃ //
242.d:
नासायां वदने स्वेदे कक्षयोर्विडगन्धकः /
ह्रस्वं लिङ्गं तथा ग्रीवा जङ्घे स्याद्वेदह्रस्वकं //
242.m: Fragrant like bdellium in the nose, mouth, sweat, and armpits. / The penis, neck, and two shanks are short—that would be 'four-short'.

242.s:
sūkṣmāṇyaṅguliparvāṇi nakhakeśadvijatvacaḥ /
hanū netre lalāṭe ca nāsā dīrghā stanāntaraṃ //
242.d:
सूक्ष्माण्यङ्गुलिपर्वाणि नखकेशद्विजत्वचः /
हनू नेत्रे ललाटे च नासा दीर्घा स्तनान्तरं //
242.m: Slender are the joints of the fingers, the nails, hair, teeth, and skin. / The jaws, eyes, forehead, nose, and the space between the breasts are long.

242.s:
vakṣaḥ kakṣau nakhā nāsonnataṃ vaktraṃ kṛkāṭikā /
snigdhāstvakkeśadantāś ca loma dṛṣṭirnakhāś ca vāk //
242.d:
वक्षः कक्षौ नखा नासोन्नतं वक्त्रं कृकाटिका /
स्निग्धास्त्वक्केशदन्ताश् च लोम दृष्टिर्नखाश् च वाक् //
242.m: The chest, armpits, nails, nose, face, and nape of the neck are elevated. / Glossy are the skin, hair, teeth, body hair, gaze, nails, and speech.

242.s:
jānvorurvoś ca pṛṣṭhastha vaṃśau dvau karanāsayoḥ /
netre nāsāpuṭau karṇau meḍhraṃ pāyumukhe 'malaṃ //
242.d:
जान्वोरुर्वोश् च पृष्ठस्थ वंशौ द्वौ करनासयोः /
नेत्रे नासापुटौ कर्णौ मेढ्रं पायुमुखे ऽमलं //
242.m: The two knee-joints and thighs, the two lineages on the back, and those of the hands and nose. / The eyes, nostrils, ears, penis, anus, and mouth are pure.

242.s:
jihvoṣṭhe tālunetre tu hastapādau nakhās tathā /
śiśnāgravaktraṃ śasyante padmābhā daśa dehināṃ //
242.d:
जिह्वोष्ठे तालुनेत्रे तु हस्तपादौ नखास् तथा /
शिश्नाग्रवक्त्रं शस्यन्ते पद्माभा दश देहिनां //
242.m: The tongue, lips, palate, eyes, hands, feet, nails, / tip of the penis, and mouth: these ten resembling a lotus are praised in embodied beings.

242.s:
pāṇipādaṃ mukhaṃ grīvā śravaṇe hṛdayaṃ śiraḥ /
:p 385
lalāṭamudaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ vṛhantaḥ pūjitā daśa //
242.d:
पाणिपादं मुखं ग्रीवा श्रवणे हृदयं शिरः /
:प् 385
ललाटमुदरं पृष्ठं वृहन्तः पूजिता दश //
242.m:
The hands, feet, mouth, neck, ears, heart, head,
[Page 385]
forehead, belly, and back: these ten, being large, are honored.

242.s:
prasāritabhujasyeha madhyamāgradvayāntaraṃ /
ucchrāyeṇa samaṃ yasya nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalaḥ //
242.d:
प्रसारितभुजस्येह मध्यमाग्रद्वयान्तरं /
उच्छ्रायेण समं यस्य न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलः //
242.m: He whose distance between the tips of the middle fingers when his arms are outstretched / is equal to his height is 'circular like a banyan tree' (nyagrodhaparimaṇḍala).

242.s:
pādau gulphau sphicau pārśvau vaṅkṣaṇau vṛṣaṇau kucau /
karṇauṣṭhe sakthinī jaṅghe hastau bāhū tathākṣiṇī //
242.d:
पादौ गुल्फौ स्फिचौ पार्श्वौ वङ्क्षणौ वृषणौ कुचौ /
कर्णौष्ठे सक्थिनी जङ्घे हस्तौ बाहू तथाक्षिणी //
242.m: The feet, ankles, buttocks, flanks, groins, testicles, breasts, / ears, lips, thighs, shanks, hands, arms, and eyes:

242.s:
caturdaśasamadvandva etatsāmānyato naraḥ /
vidyāś caturdaśa dvyakṣaiḥ paśyedyaḥ ṣoḍaśākṣakaḥ //
242.d:
चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्व एतत्सामान्यतो नरः /
विद्याश् चतुर्दश द्व्यक्षैः पश्येद्यः षोडशाक्षकः //
242.m: a man generally has these fourteen equal pairs. / He who sees the fourteen branches of learning with both eyes is 'sixteen-eyed'.

242.s:
rūkṣaṃ śirātataṃ gātramaśubhaṃ māṃsavarjitaṃ /
durgandhiviparītaṃ yacchastandṛṣṭyā prasannayā //
242.d:
रूक्षं शिराततं गात्रमशुभं मांसवर्जितं /
दुर्गन्धिविपरीतं यच्छस्तन्दृष्ट्या प्रसन्नया //
242.m: A rough body, covered with veins, devoid of flesh, is inauspicious. / That which is foul-smelling is the opposite [of auspicious]; what is praised is [accompanied] by a clear gaze.

242.s:
dhanyasya madhurā vāṇī gatirmattebhasannibhā /
ekakūpabhavaṃ roma bhaye rakṣā sakṛt sakṛt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe puruṣalakṣaṇaṃ nāma
dvicatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha tricatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
strīlakṣaṇaṃ
242.d:
धन्यस्य मधुरा वाणी गतिर्मत्तेभसन्निभा /
एककूपभवं रोम भये रक्षा सकृत् सकृत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पुरुषलक्षणं नाम
द्विचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
स्त्रीलक्षणं
242.m:
A fortunate man's voice is sweet, and his gait resembles an intoxicated elephant. / Hair growing singly from a follicle brings protection in times of danger again and again.
Thus ends the two hundred and forty-second chapter, entitled 'Characteristics of Men', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and forty-third chapter.
Characteristics of Women

243.s:
samudra uvāca
śastā strī(1) cārusarvāṅgī mattamātaṅgagāminī /
gurūrujaghanā yā ca mattapārāvatekṣaṇā //
243.d:
समुद्र उवाच
शस्ता स्त्री(1) चारुसर्वाङ्गी मत्तमातङ्गगामिनी /
गुरूरुजघना या च मत्तपारावतेक्षणा //
243.m: Samudra said: / Praised is a woman whose limbs are entirely beautiful, who walks like an elephant in rut, / who has heavy thighs and hips, and whose eyes are like an impassioned pigeon;

243.s:
sunīlakeśī tanvaṅgī vilomāṅgī manoharā /
:n
1 śubhā strī iti ja..
:p 386
samabhūmispṛśau pādau saṃhatau ca tathā stanau //
243.d:
सुनीलकेशी तन्वङ्गी विलोमाङ्गी मनोहरा /
:न्
1 शुभा स्त्री इति ज..
:प् 386
समभूमिस्पृशौ पादौ संहतौ च तथा स्तनौ //

243.s:
nābhiḥ pradakṣiṇāvartā guhyamaśvatthapatravat /
gulphau nigūḍhau madhyena nābhiraṅguṣṭhamānikā //
243.d:
नाभिः प्रदक्षिणावर्ता गुह्यमश्वत्थपत्रवत् /
गुल्फौ निगूढौ मध्येन नाभिरङ्गुष्ठमानिका //
243.m: whose navel curls clockwise, whose pudendum is shaped like an aśvattha leaf, / whose ankles are hidden by the middle [flesh], whose navel measures a thumb's width;

243.s:
jaṭharanna pralambañca romarūkṣā na śobhanā /
narkṣavṛkṣanadīnāmnī na sadā(1) kalahapriyā //
243.d:
जठरन्न प्रलम्बञ्च रोमरूक्षा न शोभना /
नर्क्षवृक्षनदीनाम्नी न सदा(1) कलहप्रिया //
243.m: whose belly does not hang down; she who is rough with body hair is not auspicious; / she who is not named after a constellation, tree, or river, nor constantly fond of quarreling;

243.s:
na lolupā na durbhāṣā śubhā devādipūjitā /
gaṇḍair madhūkapuṣpābhair na śirālā na lomaśā //
243.d:
न लोलुपा न दुर्भाषा शुभा देवादिपूजिता /
गण्डैर् मधूकपुष्पाभैर् न शिराला न लोमशा //
243.m: not greedy, not foul-mouthed; an auspicious woman is honored by gods and others; / with cheeks resembling madhūka flowers, neither veined nor hairy;

243.s:
na saṃhatabhrūkuṭilā patiprāṇā patipriyā /
alakṣaṇāpi lakṣaṇyā yatrākārāstato guṇāḥ(2) //
243.d:
न संहतभ्रूकुटिला पतिप्राणा पतिप्रिया /
अलक्षणापि लक्षण्या यत्राकारास्ततो गुणाः(2) //
243.m: not with joined and crooked eyebrows, holding her husband as her life, beloved of her husband. / Even one without marks has good marks; where there are good forms, there are good qualities.

243.s:
bhuvaṅkaniṣṭhikā yasyā na spṛśenmṛtyureva sā //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe strīlakṣaṇaṃ nāma
tricatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catuś catvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
cāmarādilakṣaṇam
243.d:
भुवङ्कनिष्ठिका यस्या न स्पृशेन्मृत्युरेव सा //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे स्त्रीलक्षणं नाम
त्रिचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुश् चत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
चामरादिलक्षणम्
243.m:
She whose little toe does not touch the ground brings death itself.
Thus ends the two hundred and forty-third chapter, entitled 'Characteristics of Women', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and forty-fourth chapter.
Characteristics of Fly-whisks and Other Regalia

244.s:
agnir uvāca
cāmaro rukmādaṇḍo 'gryaḥ chatraṃ rājñaḥ praśasyate /
haṃsapakṣair viracitaṃ mayūrasya śukasya ca //
244.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
चामरो रुक्मादण्डो ऽग्र्यः छत्रं राज्ञः प्रशस्यते /
हंसपक्षैर् विरचितं मयूरस्य शुकस्य च //
244.m: Agni said: / A fly-whisk with a golden staff is foremost; the parasol of a king is commended / when made with the feathers of a swan, a peacock, or a parrot.

244.s:
pakṣair vātha balākāyā na kāryaṃ miśrapakṣakaiḥ /
:n
1 na śatheti cha..
2 jaṭharamityādiḥ, tato guṇā ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ gha.. , ña.. ,
pustakadvaye nāsti
:p 387
caturasyaṃ brāhmaṇasya vṛttaṃ rājñaś ca śuklakaṃ //
244.d:
पक्षैर् वाथ बलाकाया न कार्यं मिश्रपक्षकैः /
:न्
1 न शथेति छ..
2 जठरमित्यादिः, ततो गुणा इत्य् अन्तः पाठः घ.. , ञ.. ,
पुस्तकद्वये नास्ति
:प् 387
चतुरस्यं ब्राह्मणस्य वृत्तं राज्ञश् च शुक्लकं //
244.m:
or with crane feathers; it should not be made with mixed feathers.
[Footnote 1: ‘na śathā’ in manuscript cha.]
[Footnote 2: The passage beginning with ‘jaṭharam’ up to ‘tato guṇāḥ’ is absent in two manuscripts, gha and ña.]
[Page 387]
A square [parasol] is for a brāhmaṇa, and a round, white one is for a king.

244.s:
tricatuḥpañcaṣaṭsaptāṣṭaparvaś ca daṇḍakaḥ /
bhadrāsanaṃ kṣīravṛkṣaiḥ pañcāśadaṅgulocchrayaiḥ(1) //
244.d:
त्रिचतुःपञ्चषट्सप्ताष्टपर्वश् च दण्डकः /
भद्रासनं क्षीरवृक्षैः पञ्चाशदङ्गुलोच्छ्रयैः(1) //
244.m:
The shaft may have three, four, five, six, seven, or eight joints.
A throne of state should be made from milk-bearing trees, fifty aṅgulas high,

244.s:
vistāreṇa trihastaṃ(2) syāt suvarṇādyaiś ca citritaṃ /
dhanurdravyatrayaṃ lohaṃ śṛṅgaṃ dāru dvijottama //
244.d:
विस्तारेण त्रिहस्तं(2) स्यात् सुवर्णाद्यैश् च चित्रितं /
धनुर्द्रव्यत्रयं लोहं शृङ्गं दारु द्विजोत्तम //
244.m:
and three cubits in width, ornamented with gold and other [metals].
There are three materials for a bow: metal, horn, and wood, O best of the twice-born.

244.s:
jyādravyatritayañcaiva vaṃśabhaṅgatvacas tathā /
dārucāpapramāṇantu śreṣṭhaṃ hastacatuṣṭayaṃ //
244.d:
ज्याद्रव्यत्रितयञ्चैव वंशभङ्गत्वचस् तथा /
दारुचापप्रमाणन्तु श्रेष्ठं हस्तचतुष्टयं //
244.m:
And the three bowstring materials are bamboo, bhangā, and bark.
The best measure for a wooden bow is four cubits;

244.s:
tadeva samahīnantu proktaṃ madhyakanīyasi /
muṣṭigrāhanimittāni madhye dravyāṇi kārayet //
244.d:
तदेव समहीनन्तु प्रोक्तं मध्यकनीयसि /
मुष्टिग्राहनिमित्तानि मध्ये द्रव्याणि कारयेत् //
244.m:
that same [bow] reduced equally [by half-cubits] is declared moderate and inferior.
In the middle, one should make materials suitable for grasping with the fist.

244.s:
svalpakoṭistvacā śṛṅgaṃ śārṅgalohamaye dvija /
kāminībhrūlatākārā koṭiḥ kāryā susaṃyutā //
244.d:
स्वल्पकोटिस्त्वचा शृङ्गं शार्ङ्गलोहमये द्विज /
कामिनीभ्रूलताकारा कोटिः कार्या सुसंयुता //
244.m:
With small notches, bark, or horn, in one made of horn and metal, O twice-born:
the notch should be fashioned well-joined, shaped like the creeping brow of a lovely woman.

244.s:
pṛthagvā vipra miśraṃ vā lauhaṃ śārṅgantu kārayet /
śārṅgaṃ samucitaṃ kāryaṃ rukmavinduvibhūṣitaṃ //
244.d:
पृथग्वा विप्र मिश्रं वा लौहं शार्ङ्गन्तु कारयेत् /
शार्ङ्गं समुचितं कार्यं रुक्मविन्दुविभूषितं //
244.m:
A metal or horn [bow] should be made separately or mixed, O vipra;
a horn bow should be made appropriately adorned with golden spots.

244.s:
kuṭilaṃ sphuṭitañcāpaṃ sacchidrañca na śasyate /
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ kṛṣṇāyo dhanuṣi smṛtaṃ //
244.d:
कुटिलं स्फुटितञ्चापं सच्छिद्रञ्च न शस्यते /
सुवर्णं रजतं ताम्रं कृष्णायो धनुषि स्मृतं //
244.m:
A crooked, cracked, or perforated bow is not commended.
Gold, silver, copper, and iron are prescribed for a bow.

244.s:
māhiṣaṃ śārabhaṃ śārṅgaṃ rauhiṣaṃ vā dhanuḥśubhaṃ /
candanaṃ vetasaṃ sālaṃ dhāvalaṅkakubhantaruḥ //
244.d:
माहिषं शारभं शार्ङ्गं रौहिषं वा धनुःशुभं /
चन्दनं वेतसं सालं धावलङ्ककुभन्तरुः //
244.m:
A horn bow made of buffalo, śarabha, or ruru deer [horn] is auspicious.
Sandalwood, cane, sāl, dhāva, kakubha trees:

244.s:
sarvaśreṣṭhaṃ dhanurvaṃśair gṛhītaiḥ śaradi śritaiḥ /
pūjayettu dhanuḥ(3) khaḍgamantraistrailokyamohanaiḥ //
244.d:
सर्वश्रेष्ठं धनुर्वंशैर् गृहीतैः शरदि श्रितैः /
पूजयेत्तु धनुः(3) खड्गमन्त्रैस्त्रैलोक्यमोहनैः //
244.m:
the bow made from bamboo harvested in autumn is best of all.
One should worship the bow and the sword with mantras that enchant the three worlds.

244.s:
ayasaścātha vaṃśasya śarasyāpyaśarasya ca /
ṛtvijo hemavārṇābhāḥ snāyuśliṣṭāḥ supatrakāḥ //
:n
1 caturasramityādiḥ, pañcāśadaṅgulocchrayair ityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ
ja..pustake nāsti
2 dvihastamiti ṭa..
3 pūjayettaddhanuriti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 388
244.d:
अयसश्चाथ वंशस्य शरस्याप्यशरस्य च /
ऋत्विजो हेमवार्णाभाः स्नायुश्लिष्टाः सुपत्रकाः //
:न्
1 चतुरस्रमित्यादिः, पञ्चाशदङ्गुलोच्छ्रयैर् इत्यन्तः पाठः
ज..पुस्तके नास्ति
2 द्विहस्तमिति ट..
3 पूजयेत्तद्धनुरिति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 388
244.m:
Arrows of iron, bamboo, or with reed and without reed,
acting as priests, golden-hued, bound with sinew, well-feathered,
[...]
[Footnote 1: The passage beginning with ‘caturasram’ up to ‘pañcāśadaṅgulocchrayaiḥ’ is absent in manuscript ja.]
[Footnote 2: ‘dvihastam’ in manuscript ṭa.]
[Footnote 3: ‘pūjayettaddhanuḥ’ in manuscripts ga, gha, and ña.]
[Page 388]

244.s:
rukmapuṅkhāḥ supaṅkāste tailadhautāḥ suvarṇakāḥ /
yātrāyāmabhiṣekādau yajedvāṇadhanurmukhān //
244.d:
रुक्मपुङ्खाः सुपङ्कास्ते तैलधौताः सुवर्णकाः /
यात्रायामभिषेकादौ यजेद्वाणधनुर्मुखान् //
244.m:
with golden nocks, well-pointed, washed in oil, and of fine appearance.
On an expedition, during a consecration, and other occasions, one should worship those headed by arrows and bows,

244.s:
sapatākāstrasaṅgrāhasāṃvatsarakarānnṛpaḥ /
brahmā vai meruśikhare svargagaṅgātaṭe 'yajat //
244.d:
सपताकास्त्रसङ्ग्राहसांवत्सरकरान्नृपः /
ब्रह्मा वै मेरुशिखरे स्वर्गगङ्गातटे ऽयजत् //
244.m:
along with banners, armouries, and astrologers, O king.
Brahmā indeed sacrificed on the summit of Meru, on the bank of the heavenly Gaṅgā.

244.s:
lauhadaityaṃ sa dadṛśe vidhnaṃ yajñe tu cintayan /
tasya cintayato vahneḥ puruṣo 'bhūdvalī mahān //
244.d:
लौहदैत्यं स ददृशे विध्नं यज्ञे तु चिन्तयन् /
तस्य चिन्तयतो वह्नेः पुरुषो ऽभूद्वली महान् //
244.m:
As he contemplated an obstacle to the sacrifice, he saw an iron-bodied demon.
While he was contemplating, a great, mighty man arose from the fire.

244.s:
vavande 'jañca tandevā abhyanandanta harṣitāḥ(1) /
tasmātsa nandakaḥ(2) kaḍgo devokto hariragrahīt //
244.d:
ववन्दे ऽजञ्च तन्देवा अभ्यनन्दन्त हर्षिताः(1) /
तस्मात्स नन्दकः(2) कड्गो देवोक्तो हरिरग्रहीत् //
244.m:
He paid homage to the Unborn [Brahmā], and the delighted gods welcomed him.
Therefore he was called Nandaka; Hari took the sword named by the gods.

244.s:
taṃ jagrāha śanair devo(3) vikoṣaḥ so 'bhyapadyata /
khaḍgo nīlo ratnamuṣṭistato 'bhūcchatabāhukaḥ //
244.d:
तं जग्राह शनैर् देवो(3) विकोषः सो ऽभ्यपद्यत /
खड्गो नीलो रत्नमुष्टिस्ततो ऽभूच्छतबाहुकः //
244.m:
The god gently took it, and it came forth from its scabbard.
The sword was dark blue with a hilt of jewels, and then became hundred-armed.

244.s:
daityaḥ sa gadayā devān drāvayāmāsa vai raṇe /
viṣṇunā khaḍgacchinnāni daityagātrāṇi bhūtale //
244.d:
दैत्यः स गदया देवान् द्रावयामास वै रणे /
विष्णुना खड्गच्छिन्नानि दैत्यगात्राणि भूतले //
244.m:
That demon routed the gods in battle with a mace.
The demon’s limbs, cut by Viṣṇu with the sword, fell on the earth;

244.s:
patitāni tu saṃsparśānnandakasya ca tāni hi /
lohabhūtāni sarvāṇi hatvā tasmai harirvaraṃ //
244.d:
पतितानि तु संस्पर्शान्नन्दकस्य च तानि हि /
लोहभूतानि सर्वाणि हत्वा तस्मै हरिर्वरं //
244.m:
by the touch of Nandaka, all of them became iron.
Having slain him, Hari granted him a boon:

244.s:
dadau pavitramaṅgante āyudhāya bhavedbhuvi /
hariprasādād brahmāpi vinā vighnaṃ hariṃ prabhuṃ //
244.d:
ददौ पवित्रमङ्गन्ते आयुधाय भवेद्भुवि /
हरिप्रसादाद् ब्रह्मापि विना विघ्नं हरिं प्रभुं //
244.m:
‘Your limb shall become holy on earth for the sake of weapons.’
By Hari’s grace, even Brahmā worshipped the lord Hari with the sacrifice without obstacle.

244.s:
pūjayāmāsa yajñena vakṣye 'tho khaḍgalakṣaṇaṃ /
khaṭīkhaṭṭarajātā ye daśanīyāstute smṛtāḥ //
244.d:
पूजयामास यज्ञेन वक्ष्ये ऽथो खड्गलक्षणं /
खटीखट्टरजाता ये दशनीयास्तुते स्मृताः //
244.m:
I shall now describe the characteristics of a sword:
Those produced in Khaṭīkhaṭṭara are known as fit to be displayed;

244.s:
kāyacchidastvāṣikāḥ syurdṛḍhāḥ sūrpārakodbhavāḥ /
tīkṣṇāśchedasahā vaṅgāstīkṣṇāḥsyuścāṅgadeśajāḥ //
244.d:
कायच्छिदस्त्वाषिकाः स्युर्दृढाः सूर्पारकोद्भवाः /
तीक्ष्णाश्छेदसहा वङ्गास्तीक्ष्णाःस्युश्चाङ्गदेशजाः //
244.m:
those of Ṛṣika cut the body; those produced in Śūrpāraka are strong;
those of Vaṅga are sharp and withstand cutting; and those produced in the Aṅga country are sharp.

244.s:
śatārdhamaṅgulānāñca śreṣṭhaṃ khadgaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
:n
1 lohadaityamityādiḥ, harṣitā ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ ja.. pustake
nāsti
2 tasmāttu nandaka iti gha.. , ña.. ca
3 mahādeva iti ja..
:p 389
tadardhaṃ madhyamaṃ jñeyaṃ tato hīnaṃ na dhārayet //
244.d:
शतार्धमङ्गुलानाञ्च श्रेष्ठं खद्गं प्रकीर्तितं /
:न्
1 लोहदैत्यमित्यादिः, हर्षिता इत्य् अन्तः पाठः ज.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
2 तस्मात्तु नन्दक इति घ.. , ञ.. च
3 महादेव इति ज..
:प् 389
तदर्धं मध्यमं ज्ञेयं ततो हीनं न धारयेत् //
244.m:
A sword of fifty aṅgulas is declared the best;
[...]
[Footnote 1: The passage beginning with ‘lohadaityam’ up to ‘harṣitāḥ’ is absent in manuscript ja.]
[Footnote 2: ‘tasmāttu nandakaḥ’ in manuscripts gha and ña.]
[Footnote 3: ‘mahādevaḥ’ in manuscript ja.]
[Page 389]
half of that is known as middling; one should not wear one smaller than that.

244.s:
dīrghaṃ sumadhuraṃ śabdaṃ yusya khaḍgasya sattama /
kiṅkiṇīsadṛśantasya dhāraṇaṃ śreṣṭhamucyate //
244.d:
दीर्घं सुमधुरं शब्दं युस्य खड्गस्य सत्तम /
किङ्किणीसदृशन्तस्य धारणं श्रेष्ठमुच्यते //
244.m:
The sword whose sound is long and very sweet,
like a small bell, O best of men, its wearing is said to be best.

244.s:
khaḍgaḥ padmapalāśāgro maṇḍalāgraś ca śasyate /
karavīradalāgrābho ghṛtagandho viyatprabhaḥ //
244.d:
खड्गः पद्मपलाशाग्रो मण्डलाग्रश् च शस्यते /
करवीरदलाग्राभो घृतगन्धो वियत्प्रभः //
244.m:
A sword with a point like a lotus petal, or rounded at the point, is commended,
or having the luster of an oleander petal, smelling of ghee, and shining like the sky.

244.s:
samāṅgulasthāḥ śasyante vraṇāḥ khadgeṣu liṅgavat /
kākolūkasavarṇābhā viṣamāste na śobhanāḥ //
244.d:
समाङ्गुलस्थाः शस्यन्ते व्रणाः खद्गेषु लिङ्गवत् /
काकोलूकसवर्णाभा विषमास्ते न शोभनाः //
244.m:
Flaws situated at equal aṅgulas on swords are commended like marks;
those having the color of a crow or an owl, and irregular ones, are not auspicious.

244.s:
khaḍge na paśyedvadanamucchiṣṭo na spṛśedasiṃ /
mūlyaṃ jātiṃ na kathayenniśi kuryānna śīrṣake //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe āyudhalakṣaṇādirnāma catuś
catvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ratnaparīkṣā
244.d:
खड्गे न पश्येद्वदनमुच्छिष्टो न स्पृशेदसिं /
मूल्यं जातिं न कथयेन्निशि कुर्यान्न शीर्षके //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे आयुधलक्षणादिर्नाम चतुश्
चत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
रत्नपरीक्षा
244.m:
One should not look at one's face in a sword; one should not touch a sword while impure from food;
one should not state its price or origin, nor place it at one's head at night.
Thus ends the two hundred and forty-fourth chapter, entitled ‘Characteristics of Weapons and the Like,’ in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the two hundred and forty-fifth chapter:
Examination of Gems

245.s:
agnir uvāca
ratnānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye ratnaṃ dhāryamidaṃ nṛpaiḥ /
vajraṃ marakataṃ ratnaṃ padmarāgañca mauktikaṃ //
245.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
रत्नानां लक्षणं वक्ष्ये रत्नं धार्यमिदं नृपैः /
वज्रं मरकतं रत्नं पद्मरागञ्च मौक्तिकं //
245.m:
Agni said:
I shall describe the characteristics of gems; this gem should be worn by kings:
diamond, emerald, ruby, and pearl,

245.s:
indranīlaṃ mahānīlaṃ vaidūryaṃ gandhaśasyakaṃ /
candrakāntaṃ sūryakāntaṃ sphaṭikaṃ pulakaṃ tathā //
:p 390
245.d:
इन्द्रनीलं महानीलं वैदूर्यं गन्धशस्यकं /
चन्द्रकान्तं सूर्यकान्तं स्फटिकं पुलकं तथा //
:प् 390
245.m:
sapphire, mahānīla, cat's eye, gandhaśasyaka,
moonstone, sunstone, crystal, and pulaka,
[Page 390]

245.s:
karketanaṃ puṣparāgaṃ tathā jyotīrasaṃ dvija /
spaṭikaṃ rājapaṭṭañca tathā rājamayaṃ śubhaṃ //
245.d:
कर्केतनं पुष्परागं तथा ज्योतीरसं द्विज /
स्पटिकं राजपट्टञ्च तथा राजमयं शुभं //
245.m:
chrysoberyl, topaz, and jyotīrasa, O twice-born,
quartz, rājapaṭṭa, and the auspicious rājamaya,

245.s:
saugandhikaṃ tathā gañjaṃ śaṅkhabrahmamayaṃ tathā /
gomedaṃ rudhirākṣañca tathā bhallātakaṃ dvija //
245.d:
सौगन्धिकं तथा गञ्जं शङ्खब्रह्ममयं तथा /
गोमेदं रुधिराक्षञ्च तथा भल्लातकं द्विज //
245.m:
saugandhika, also gañja, conch, and brahmamaya,
gomeda, rudhirākṣa, and bhallātaka, O twice-born,

245.s:
dhūlīṃ marakatañcaiva tuthakaṃ sīsameva ca /
pīluṃ pravālakañcaiva girivajraṃ dvijottama //
245.d:
धूलीं मरकतञ्चैव तुथकं सीसमेव च /
पीलुं प्रवालकञ्चैव गिरिवज्रं द्विजोत्तम //
245.m:
dhūlīmarakata, tuttha, and lead,
pīlu, coral, and mountain diamond, O best of the twice-born,

245.s:
bhujaṅgamamaṇiñcaiva tathā vajramaṇiṃ śubhaṃ /
ṭiṭṭibhañca tathā piṇḍaṃ bhrāmarañca tathotpalaṃ //
245.d:
भुजङ्गममणिञ्चैव तथा वज्रमणिं शुभं /
टिट्टिभञ्च तथा पिण्डं भ्रामरञ्च तथोत्पलं //
245.m:
serpent gem, and the auspicious vajramaṇi,
ṭiṭṭibha, piṇḍa, bhrāmara, and utpala.

245.s:
suvarṇapratibaddhāni ratnāni śrījayādike /
antaḥprabhatvaṃ vaimalyaṃ susaṃsthānatvameva ca //
245.d:
सुवर्णप्रतिबद्धानि रत्नानि श्रीजयादिके /
अन्तःप्रभत्वं वैमल्यं सुसंस्थानत्वमेव च //
245.m:
Gems set in gold [are worn] for fortune, victory, and the like.
Internal brilliance, spotless purity, and fine symmetry:

245.s:
sudhāryā naiva dhāryāstu niṣprabhā malinās tathā /
khaṇḍāḥ saśarkarā ye ca praśastaṃ vajradharaṇam //
245.d:
सुधार्या नैव धार्यास्तु निष्प्रभा मलिनास् तथा /
खण्डाः सशर्करा ये च प्रशस्तं वज्रधरणम् //
245.m:
these are well suited to be worn; but those lusterless, dirty,
broken, or full of grit must never be worn. The wearing of diamond is praised.

245.s:
ambhastarati yadvajramabhedyaṃ vimalaṃ ca yat /
ṣaṭkoṇaṃ śakracāpābhaṃ laghu cārkanibhaṃ śubham //
245.d:
अम्भस्तरति यद्वज्रमभेद्यं विमलं च यत् /
षट्कोणं शक्रचापाभं लघु चार्कनिभं शुभम् //
245.m:
A diamond that floats on water, is unbreakable, spotless,
six-angled, resembling a rainbow, light, and shining like the sun, is auspicious.

245.s:
śukapakṣanibhaḥ snigdhaḥ kāntimānvimalas tathā /
svarṇacūrṇanibhaiḥ sūkṣmair marakataś ca vindubhiḥ //
245.d:
शुकपक्षनिभः स्निग्धः कान्तिमान्विमलस् तथा /
स्वर्णचूर्णनिभैः सूक्ष्मैर् मरकतश् च विन्दुभिः //
245.m:
An emerald resembling a parrot's wing, glossy, brilliant, spotless,
and with fine specks resembling gold dust [is auspicious].

245.s:
sphaṭikajāḥ padmarāgāḥ syū rāgavanto 'tinirmalāḥ /
jātavaṅgā bhavantīha kuruvindasamudbhavāḥ //
245.d:
स्फटिकजाः पद्मरागाः स्यू रागवन्तो ऽतिनिर्मलाः /
जातवङ्गा भवन्तीह कुरुविन्दसमुद्भवाः //
245.m:
Rubies born of crystal are richly colored and exceedingly pure;
here they are of noble origin when produced from kuruvinda.

245.s:
saugandhikotthā kāṣāyā muktāphalāstu śuktijāḥ /
vimalāstebhya utkṛṣṭā ye ca śaṅkhodbhavā mune //
245.d:
सौगन्धिकोत्था काषाया मुक्ताफलास्तु शुक्तिजाः /
विमलास्तेभ्य उत्कृष्टा ये च शङ्खोद्भवा मुने //
245.m:
Those originating from saugandhika are reddish-brown. Pearls originate from oysters;
those born of conches, O sage, are spotless and superior to them.

245.s:
nāgadantabhavāścāgryāḥ kumbhaśūkaramatsyajāḥ /
veṇunāgabhavāḥ śreṣṭhā mauktikaṃ meghajaṃ varaṃ //
245.d:
नागदन्तभवाश्चाग्र्याः कुम्भशूकरमत्स्यजाः /
वेणुनागभवाः श्रेष्ठा मौक्तिकं मेघजं वरं //
245.m:
Those born from elephant tusks are foremost, as are those born from the brow of an elephant, a boar, or a fish;
those born from bamboo and serpents are excellent, and a pearl born of a cloud is supreme.

245.s:
vṛttatvaṃ śukratā svācchyaṃmahattvaṃ mauktike guṇāḥ /
:p 391
indranīlaṃ śubhaṃ kṣīre rājate bhrājate 'dhikaṃ(1) //
245.d:
वृत्तत्वं शुक्रता स्वाच्छ्यंमहत्त्वं मौक्तिके गुणाः /
:प् 391
इन्द्रनीलं शुभं क्षीरे राजते भ्राजते ऽधिकं(1) //
245.m:
Roundness, whiteness, clarity, and large size are the virtues in a pearl.
[Page 391]
An auspicious sapphire shines and radiates exceedingly in milk.

245.s:
rañjayet svaprabhāveṇa tamamūlyaṃ vinirdiśet /
nīlaraktantu vaidūryaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ hārādikaṃ bhajet(2) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe ratnaparīkṣā nāma
pañcacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vāstulakṣaṇaṃ
245.d:
रञ्जयेत् स्वप्रभावेण तममूल्यं विनिर्दिशेत् /
नीलरक्तन्तु वैदूर्यं श्रेष्ठं हारादिकं भजेत्(2) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे रत्नपरीक्षा नाम
पञ्चचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ षट्चत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
वास्तुलक्षणं
245.m:
[If] it tinges [the milk] by its own brilliance, one should pronounce it priceless.
Cat's-eye that is blue and red is superior; it should be used for necklaces and the like.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and forty-fifth chapter, named 'Examination of Gems'.
Now the two hundred and forty-sixth chapter.
Characteristics of Site Architecture

246.s:
agnir uvāca
vāstulakṣma pravakṣyāmi viprādīnāṃ ca bhūriha /
śvetā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā caiva yathākramam //
246.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वास्तुलक्ष्म प्रवक्ष्यामि विप्रादीनां च भूरिह /
श्वेता रक्ता तथा पीता कृष्णा चैव यथाक्रमम् //
246.m:
Agni said:
I shall declare the characteristics of the site architecture, and the ground here for Brahmins and the others:
white, red, yellow, and black respectively,

246.s:
ghṛtaraktānnamadyānāṃ gandhāḍhyā vasataś ca bhūḥ /
madhurā ca kaṣāyā ca amlādyuparasā kramāt //
246.d:
घृतरक्तान्नमद्यानां गन्धाढ्या वसतश् च भूः /
मधुरा च कषाया च अम्लाद्युपरसा क्रमात् //
246.m:
abounding in the scents of clarified butter, blood, food, and liquor [respectively] for living [upon];
and sweet, astringent, sour, and pungent respectively in secondary tastes;

246.s:
kuśaiḥ śarais tathākāśair dūrvābhiryā ca saṃśritā /
prārcya viprāṃś ca śiḥśalpāṃ khātapūrvantu kalpayet //
246.d:
कुशैः शरैस् तथाकाशैर् दूर्वाभिर्या च संश्रिता /
प्रार्च्य विप्रांश् च शिःशल्पां खातपूर्वन्तु कल्पयेत् //
246.m:
and covered with kuśa grass, reeds, kāśa grass, and dūrvā grass [respectively].
Having first worshipped the Brahmins and the artisans, one should arrange [the ground], having first excavated it.

246.s:
catuḥṣaṣṭipadaṃ kṛtvā madhye brahmā catuṣpadaḥ /
prāk teṣāṃ vai gṛhasvāmī kathitastu tathāryamā //
246.d:
चतुःषष्टिपदं कृत्वा मध्ये ब्रह्मा चतुष्पदः /
प्राक् तेषां वै गृहस्वामी कथितस्तु तथार्यमा //
246.m:
Making a grid of sixty-four squares, Brahmā occupies four squares in the centre.
To the east of them, the master of the house is declared, and likewise Aryaman.

246.s:
dakṣiṇena vivasvāṃś ca mitraḥ paścimatas tathā /
udaṅmahīdharaś caiva āpavatsau ca vahnige //
246.d:
दक्षिणेन विवस्वांश् च मित्रः पश्चिमतस् तथा /
उदङ्महीधरश् चैव आपवत्सौ च वह्निगे //
246.m:
To the south is Vivasvan, and Mitra is to the west;
Mahīdhara is to the north, and Āpa and Vatsa are in the corner of Fire.

246.s:
sāvitraś caiva savitā jayendrau nairṛte 'mbudhau /
:n
1 bhrājate sthitamiti cha.. , ja.. ca
2 bhavediti ga.. , gha.. ca
:p 392
rudravyādhī ca vāyavye pūrvādau koṇagādvahiḥ //
246.d:
सावित्रश् चैव सविता जयेन्द्रौ नैरृते ऽम्बुधौ /
:न्
1 भ्राजते स्थितमिति छ.. , ज.. च
2 भवेदिति ग.. , घ.. च
:प् 392
रुद्रव्याधी च वायव्ये पूर्वादौ कोणगाद्वहिः //
246.m:
Sāvitra, Savitṛ, Jaya, and Indra are in the south-west, [and others] in the ocean [direction, west].
[...]
1. 'bhrājate sthitam' in cha and ja.
2. 'bhavet' in ga and gha.
Rudra and Rājayakṣmā are in the north-west; outside the corner deities beginning from the east:

246.s:
mahendraś ca raviḥ satyo bhṛśaḥ(1) pūrve 'tha dakṣiṇe /
gṛhakṣato 'ryamadhṛtī gandharvāścātha vāruṇe //
246.d:
महेन्द्रश् च रविः सत्यो भृशः(1) पूर्वे ऽथ दक्षिणे /
गृहक्षतो ऽर्यमधृती गन्धर्वाश्चाथ वारुणे //
246.m:
Mahendra, Ravi, Satya, and Bhṛśa are in the east; then in the south:
Gṛhakṣata, Aryaman, Dhṛti, and the Gandharvas; and then in the western [direction]:

246.s:
puṣpadanto 'surāś caiva varuṇo yakṣa eva ca /
saumye bhallāṭasomau ca aditirdhanadas tathā //
246.d:
पुष्पदन्तो ऽसुराश् चैव वरुणो यक्ष एव च /
सौम्ये भल्लाटसोमौ च अदितिर्धनदस् तथा //
246.m:
Puṣpadanta, the Asuras, Varuṇa, and the Yakṣa;
in the northern [direction] are Bhallāṭa and Soma, Aditi, and the Giver of Wealth [Kubera];

246.s:
nāgaḥ karagrahaś caiśe aṣṭau diśi diśi smṛtāḥ /
ādyantau tu tayordevau proktāvatra gṛheśvarau //
246.d:
नागः करग्रहश् चैशे अष्टौ दिशि दिशि स्मृताः /
आद्यन्तौ तु तयोर्देवौ प्रोक्तावत्र गृहेश्वरौ //
246.m:
Nāga and Karagraha are in the north-east: eight are remembered in each direction.
The first and last of these two deities are declared here as the lords of the house:

246.s:
parjanyaḥ prathamo devo dvitīyaś ca karagrahaḥ /
mahendraravisatyāś ca bhṛśo 'tha gaganantathā //
246.d:
पर्जन्यः प्रथमो देवो द्वितीयश् च करग्रहः /
महेन्द्ररविसत्याश् च भृशो ऽथ गगनन्तथा //
246.m:
Parjanya is the first deity, and the second is Karagraha,
[then] Mahendra, Ravi, Satya, Bhṛśa, and Gagana;

246.s:
pavanaḥ pūrvataś caiva antarīkṣadhaneśvarau /
āgneye cātha nairṛtye mṛgasugrīvakau surau //
246.d:
पवनः पूर्वतश् चैव अन्तरीक्षधनेश्वरौ /
आग्नेये चाथ नैरृत्ये मृगसुग्रीवकौ सुरौ //
246.m:
and Pavana in the east, and Antarīkṣa and Dhaneśvara;
and in the south-east and south-west are the deities Mṛga and Sugrīva;

246.s:
rogo mukhyaś ca vāyavye dakṣiṇe puṣpavittadau /
gṛhakṣato yamabhṛśau gandharvo nāgapaitṛkaḥ //
246.d:
रोगो मुख्यश् च वायव्ये दक्षिणे पुष्पवित्तदौ /
गृहक्षतो यमभृशौ गन्धर्वो नागपैतृकः //
246.m:
Roga and Mukhya are in the north-west; in the south are Puṣpa and the Giver of Wealth,
Gṛhakṣata, Yama, Bhṛśa, Gandharva, Nāga, and Pitṛpati;

246.s:
āpye dauvārikasugrīvau puṣpadanto 'suro jalaṃ /
yakṣmā rogaś ca śoṣaś ca uttare nāgarājakaḥ //
246.d:
आप्ये दौवारिकसुग्रीवौ पुष्पदन्तो ऽसुरो जलं /
यक्ष्मा रोगश् च शोषश् च उत्तरे नागराजकः //
246.m:
in the western [quarter] are Dauvārika, Sugrīva, Puṣpadanta, Asura, and Jala;
Yakṣmā, Roga, and Śoṣa [follow]; in the north is the Serpent King,

246.s:
mukhyo bhallāṭaśaśinau aditiś ca kuverakaḥ /
nāgo hutāśaḥ śreṣṭho vai(2) śakrasūryau ca pūrvataḥ //
246.d:
मुख्यो भल्लाटशशिनौ अदितिश् च कुवेरकः /
नागो हुताशः श्रेष्ठो वै(2) शक्रसूर्यौ च पूर्वतः //
246.m:
Mukhya, Bhallāṭa, Śaśin, Aditi, and Kuvera.
Nāga and Hutāśa are excellent, and Śakra and Sūrya in the east;

246.s:
dakṣe gṛhakṣataḥ puṣpa āpye sugrīva uttamaḥ /
puṣpadanto hy udagdvāri bhallāṭaḥ puṣpadantakaḥ //
246.d:
दक्षे गृहक्षतः पुष्प आप्ये सुग्रीव उत्तमः /
पुष्पदन्तो ह्य् उदग्द्वारि भल्लाटः पुष्पदन्तकः //
246.m:
in the south, Gṛhakṣata and Puṣpa; in the west, Sugrīva is best;
Puṣpadanta [is also there]; at the north door, Bhallāṭa and Puṣpadantaka.

246.s:
śileṣṭakādivinyāsaṃ mantraiḥ prārcya surāṃś caret /
nande nandaya vāsiṣṭhe vasubhiḥ prajayā saha //
:n
1 bhṛguriti ja..
2 nāgo hutāśanaḥ śreṣṭha iti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 393
246.d:
शिलेष्टकादिविन्यासं मन्त्रैः प्रार्च्य सुरांश् चरेत् /
नन्दे नन्दय वासिष्ठे वसुभिः प्रजया सह //
:न्
1 भृगुरिति ज..
2 नागो हुताशनः श्रेष्ठ इति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 393
246.m:
Having first worshipped the gods with mantras, one should perform the laying of the foundation stone, brick, and the like:
'O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, bring joy along with the Vasus and with progeny!
[...]
1. 'bhṛguḥ' in ja.
2. 'nāgo hutāśanaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ' in kha and cha.

246.s:
jaye bhārgavavadāyāde prajānāñjayamāhave(1) /
pūrṇe 'ṅgirasadāyāde pūrṇakāmaṃ kurudhva māṃ //
246.d:
जये भार्गववदायादे प्रजानाञ्जयमाहवे(1) /
पूर्णे ऽङ्गिरसदायादे पूर्णकामं कुरुध्व मां //
246.m:
O Jayā, female heir of Bhṛgu, bring victory to the people in battle!
O Pūrṇā, female heir of Aṅgiras, make my desire fulfilled!

246.s:
bhadre kāśyapadāyāde kuru bhadrāṃ matiṃ mama /
sarvavījasamāyukte sarvaratnauṣadhair vṛte //
246.d:
भद्रे काश्यपदायादे कुरु भद्रां मतिं मम /
सर्ववीजसमायुक्ते सर्वरत्नौषधैर् वृते //
246.m:
O Bhadrā, female heir of Kaśyapa, make my mind auspicious!
Endowed with all seeds, surrounded by all gems and herbs,

246.s:
rucire nandane nande vāsiṣṭhe ramyatāmiha /
prajāpatisute devi caturasre mahīmaye //
246.d:
रुचिरे नन्दने नन्दे वासिष्ठे रम्यतामिह /
प्रजापतिसुते देवि चतुरस्रे महीमये //
246.m:
delightful, gladdening, O Nandā, daughter of Vasiṣṭha, take delight here!
O goddess, daughter of Prajāpati, four-cornered, made of earth,

246.s:
subhage suvrate bhadre gṛhe kaśyapi ramyatāṃ /
pūjite paramācāryair gandhamālyair alaṅkṛte(2) //
246.d:
सुभगे सुव्रते भद्रे गृहे कश्यपि रम्यतां /
पूजिते परमाचार्यैर् गन्धमाल्यैर् अलङ्कृते(2) //
246.m:
fortunate, keeper of good vows, auspicious, daughter of Kaśyapa, take delight in the house!
Worshipped by supreme teachers, adorned with fragrant garlands,

246.s:
bhavabhūtikare devi gṛhe bhārgavi ramyatāṃ /
avyaṅgye cākṣate pūrṇe muneraṅgirasaḥ sute //
246.d:
भवभूतिकरे देवि गृहे भार्गवि रम्यतां /
अव्यङ्ग्ये चाक्षते पूर्णे मुनेरङ्गिरसः सुते //
246.m:
bringing welfare and prosperity, O goddess, daughter of Bhṛgu, take delight in the house!
Flawless, uninjured, whole, daughter of the sage Aṅgiras,

246.s:
iṣṭake tvaṃ prayaccheṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭāṅkārayamyahaṃ /
deśasvāmipurasvāmigṛhasvāmiparigrahe //
246.d:
इष्टके त्वं प्रयच्छेष्टं प्रतिष्टाङ्कारयम्यहं /
देशस्वामिपुरस्वामिगृहस्वामिपरिग्रहे //
246.m:
O brick, grant what is desired; I perform the consecration!
In the acquisition by the lord of the country, the lord of the city, and the master of the house,

246.s:
manuṣyadhanahastyaśvapaśuvṛddhikarī bhava /
gṛhapraveśe 'pi tathā śilānyāsaṃ samācaret //
246.d:
मनुष्यधनहस्त्यश्वपशुवृद्धिकरी भव /
गृहप्रवेशे ऽपि तथा शिलान्यासं समाचरेत् //
246.m:
be the increaser of humans, wealth, elephants, horses, and cattle!'
Likewise, at the time of house-entering, one should perform the laying of the foundation stone.

246.s:
uttareṇa śubhaḥ plakṣo vaṭaḥ prāk syād gṛhāditaḥ /
udumvaraś ca yāmyena paścime 'śvattha uttamaḥ //
246.d:
उत्तरेण शुभः प्लक्षो वटः प्राक् स्याद् गृहादितः /
उदुम्वरश् च याम्येन पश्चिमे ऽश्वत्थ उत्तमः //
246.m:
A plakṣa tree is auspicious to the north; a banyan should be to the east of the house and the like;
an udumbara to the south; and in the west, a sacred fig tree is best.

246.s:
vāmabhāge tathodyānaṃ kuryādvāsaṃ gṛhe śubhaṃ /
sāyaṃ prātastu gharmāptau śītakāle dināntare //
246.d:
वामभागे तथोद्यानं कुर्याद्वासं गृहे शुभं /
सायं प्रातस्तु घर्माप्तौ शीतकाले दिनान्तरे //
246.m:
One should also make a garden on the left side; dwelling in the house will be auspicious.
In the evening and in the morning, during the hot season, and on alternate days in the cold season,

246.s:
varṣārātre bhuyaḥ śoṣe sektavyā ropitadrumāḥ /
viḍaṅgaghṛṭasaṃyuktān secayecchītavāriṇā //
246.d:
वर्षारात्रे भुयः शोषे सेक्तव्या रोपितद्रुमाः /
विडङ्गघृटसंयुक्तान् सेचयेच्छीतवारिणा //
246.m:
and during the rainy season when the ground dries out, planted trees must be watered.
One should water those combined with viḍaṅga and clarified butter with cold water.

246.s:
phalanāśe kulatthaiś ca māṣair mudgaistilair yavaiḥ /
:n
1 viprāṇāṃ jayamāvaheti kha..
2 gandhamālyair alaṅkṛtair iti ga.. , cha.. ca
:p 394
ghṛtaśītapayaḥsekaḥ phalapuṣpāya darvadā //
246.d:
फलनाशे कुलत्थैश् च माषैर् मुद्गैस्तिलैर् यवैः /
:न्
1 विप्राणां जयमावहेति ख..
2 गन्धमाल्यैर् अलङ्कृतैर् इति ग.. , छ.. च
:प् 394
घृतशीतपयःसेकः फलपुष्पाय दर्वदा //
246.m:
When there is loss of fruit, [one should treat] with horse-gram, black gram, mung beans, sesame seeds, and barley;
[...]
1. 'viprāṇāṃ jayamāvaha' in kha.
2. 'gandhamālyair alaṅkṛtaiḥ' in ga and cha.
sprinkling with clarified butter and cold milk always leads to fruit and flowers.

246.s:
matsyāmbhasā tu sekena vṛddhirbhavati śākhinaḥ /
āvikājasakṛccūrṇaṃ yavacūrṇaṃ tilāni ca //
246.d:
मत्स्याम्भसा तु सेकेन वृद्धिर्भवति शाखिनः /
आविकाजसकृच्चूर्णं यवचूर्णं तिलानि च //
246.m:
By watering with fish-water, however, the growth of trees takes place.
Powder of dung from sheep and goats, barley flour, and sesame seeds,

246.s:
gomāṃsamudakañceti saptarātraṃ nidhāpayet /
utsekaṃ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ phalapuṣpādivṛddhidaṃ //
246.d:
गोमांसमुदकञ्चेति सप्तरात्रं निधापयेत् /
उत्सेकं सर्ववृक्षाणां फलपुष्पादिवृद्धिदं //
246.m:
beef, and water—one should keep these together for seven nights.
This watering brings growth of fruits, flowers, and the like for all trees.

246.s:
matsyodakena śītena āmrāṇāṃ seka iṣyate(1) /
praśastaṃ cāpyaśokānāṃ kāminīpādatāḍanaṃ //
246.d:
मत्स्योदकेन शीतेन आम्राणां सेक इष्यते(1) /
प्रशस्तं चाप्यशोकानां कामिनीपादताडनं //
246.m:
Watering mango trees with cold fish-water is recommended;
and the kicking of a passionate woman upon aśoka trees is praised.

246.s:
kharjūranārikelāderlavaṇādbhirvivardhanaṃ /
viḍaṅgamatsyamāṃsādbhiḥ sarveṣu dohadaṃ śubhaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vāstvādirnāma
ṣaṭtacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
puṣpādipūjāphalaṃ
246.d:
खर्जूरनारिकेलादेर्लवणाद्भिर्विवर्धनं /
विडङ्गमत्स्यमांसाद्भिः सर्वेषु दोहदं शुभं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे वास्त्वादिर्नाम
षट्तचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
पुष्पादिपूजाफलं
246.m:
Date palms, coconuts, and the like grow from salt water.
Treatment with viḍaṅga, fish, and meat water is an auspicious nourishment for all [plants].
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and forty-sixth chapter, named 'Site Architecture and the Like'.
Now the two hundred and forty-seventh chapter.
The Fruits of Worship with Flowers and the Like

247.s:
agnir uvāca
puṣpaistu pūjanādviṣṇuḥ sarvakāryeṣu siddhidaḥ /
mālatī mallikā yūthī pāṭalā karavīrakaṃ //
247.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पुष्पैस्तु पूजनाद्विष्णुः सर्वकार्येषु सिद्धिदः /
मालती मल्लिका यूथी पाटला करवीरकं //
247.m:
Agni said:
Through worship with flowers, Viṣṇu is the granter of success in all undertakings:
mālatī, mallikā jasmine, yūthī jasmine, pāṭalā, oleander,

247.s:
pāvāntiratimuktaś ca(2) karṇikāraḥ kurāṇṭakaḥ /
:n
1 sekaḥ ucyate iti kha..
2 pāvantikātimuktaśceti ga..
:p 395
kubjakastagaro nīpo vāṇo varvaramallikā //
247.d:
पावान्तिरतिमुक्तश् च(2) कर्णिकारः कुराण्टकः /
:न्
1 सेकः उच्यते इति ख..
2 पावन्तिकातिमुक्तश्चेति ग..
:प् 395
कुब्जकस्तगरो नीपो वाणो वर्वरमल्लिका //
247.m:
pāvantī, atimukta, karṇikāra, kurāṇṭaka,
[...]
1. 'sekaḥ ucyate' in kha.
2. 'pāvantikātimuktaśca' in ga.
kubjaka, tagara, nīpa, bāṇa, varvaramallikā,

247.s:
aśokastilakaḥ kundaḥ pūjāyai syāttamālajaṃ /
bilvapatraṃ śamīpatraṃ patraṃ bhṛṅgarajasya tu //
247.d:
अशोकस्तिलकः कुन्दः पूजायै स्यात्तमालजं /
बिल्वपत्रं शमीपत्रं पत्रं भृङ्गरजस्य तु //
247.m:
aśoka, tilaka, kunda jasmine, and [leaves] derived from tamāla should be for worship;
bilva leaf, śamī leaf, and leaf of the bhṛṅgarāja,

247.s:
tulasīkālatulasīpatraṃ vāsakamarcane /
ketakīpatrapuṣpaṃ ca padmaṃ raktotpalādikaṃ //
247.d:
तुलसीकालतुलसीपत्रं वासकमर्चने /
केतकीपत्रपुष्पं च पद्मं रक्तोत्पलादिकं //
247.m:
tulasī and dark tulasī leaves, and vāsaka in worship;
ketakī leaf and flower, lotus, red water-lily, and others.

247.s:
nārkannonmattakaṅkāñcī pūjane girimallikā /
kauṭajaṃ śālmalīpuṣpaṃ kaṇṭakārībhavannahi //
247.d:
नार्कन्नोन्मत्तकङ्काञ्ची पूजने गिरिमल्लिका /
कौटजं शाल्मलीपुष्पं कण्टकारीभवन्नहि //
247.m:
Not arka, nor datura, nor kāñcī in worship, nor girimallikā;
kutaja, śālmalī blossom, and kaṇṭakārī must not be used.

247.s:
ghṛtaprasthena viṣṇoś ca snānaṅgokoṭisatphalaṃ /
āḍhakena tu rājā syāt ghṛtakṣīrair divaṃ vrajet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe puṣpādipūjāphalaṃ nāma
saptacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
247.d:
घृतप्रस्थेन विष्णोश् च स्नानङ्गोकोटिसत्फलं /
आढकेन तु राजा स्यात् घृतक्षीरैर् दिवं व्रजेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पुष्पादिपूजाफलं नाम
सप्तचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
247.m:
And bathing Viṣṇu with a prastha of ghee yields the true fruit of ten million cows; / with an āḍhaka one becomes a king; with ghee and milk one goes to heaven.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa the two hundred and forty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Fruit of Worship with Flowers and Other Offerings.”
Now the two hundred and forty-eighth chapter.

248.s:
dhanurvedaḥ
agnir uvāca
catuṣpādaṃ dhanurvedaṃ vede pañcavidhaṃ dvija /
rathanāgāśvapattīnāṃ yodhāṃścāśritya kīrtitaṃ //
248.d:
धनुर्वेदः
अग्निर् उवाच
चतुष्पादं धनुर्वेदं वेदे पञ्चविधं द्विज /
रथनागाश्वपत्तीनां योधांश्चाश्रित्य कीर्तितं //
248.m:
The Science of Archery.
Agni said:
O twice-born, the science of archery has four feet and is known in tradition as fivefold, / proclaimed in reliance on warriors belonging to chariots, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers.

248.s:
yanmuktaṃ pāṇimuktaṃ muktasandhāritaṃ tathā /
amuktaṃ bāhuyuddhañca pañcadhā tyat prakīrtitaṃ //
248.d:
यन्मुक्तं पाणिमुक्तं मुक्तसन्धारितं तथा /
अमुक्तं बाहुयुद्धञ्च पञ्चधा त्यत् प्रकीर्तितं //
248.m: That which is thrown [by machine], that thrown by hand, that thrown and held, / that unthrown, and hand-to-hand combat—thus is it proclaimed to be fivefold.

248.s:
tatra śastrāstrasampattyā dvividhaṃ parikīrtitaṃ /
:p 396
ṛjumāyāvibhedena bhūyo dvividhamucyate //
248.d:
तत्र शस्त्रास्त्रसम्पत्त्या द्विविधं परिकीर्तितं /
:प् 396
ऋजुमायाविभेदेन भूयो द्विविधमुच्यते //
248.m:
Therein, through the perfection of weapons and missiles, it is declared to be twofold:
[Page 396]
it is further stated to be twofold through the distinction between straight and illusory warfare.

248.s:
kṣepiṇī cāpayantrādyair yantramuktaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
śilātomarayantrādyaṃ pāṇimuktaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
248.d:
क्षेपिणी चापयन्त्राद्यैर् यन्त्रमुक्तं प्रकीर्तितं /
शिलातोमरयन्त्राद्यं पाणिमुक्तं प्रकीर्तितं //
248.m: That which is discharged by a sling, a bow-machine, and the like is called machine-thrown; / stones, javelins, engines, and the like are declared to be hand-thrown.

248.s:
muktasandhāritaṃ jñeyaṃ prāsādyamapi yadbhavet /
khaḍgādikamamuktañca niyuddhaṃ vigatāyudhaṃ //
248.d:
मुक्तसन्धारितं ज्ञेयं प्रासाद्यमपि यद्भवेत् /
खड्गादिकममुक्तञ्च नियुद्धं विगतायुधं //
248.m: That which is a barbed dart and the like should be known as thrown and held; / swords and the like are unthrown, and hand-to-hand fight is that which is devoid of weapons.

248.s:
kuryādyogyāni prātrāṇi yoddhumicchurjitaśramaḥ /
dhanuḥśreṣṭhāni yuddhāni prāsamadhyāni tāni ca //
248.d:
कुर्याद्योग्यानि प्रात्राणि योद्धुमिच्छुर्जितश्रमः /
धनुःश्रेष्ठानि युद्धानि प्रासमध्यानि तानि च //
248.m: Desiring to fight, having overcome exhaustion, one should make suitable preparations. / Archery battles are the best, and battles with darts are intermediate;

248.s:
tāni khaḍgajaghanyāni bāhupratyavarāṇi ca /
dhanurvede gururvipraḥ prokto varṇadvayasya ca //
248.d:
तानि खड्गजघन्यानि बाहुप्रत्यवराणि च /
धनुर्वेदे गुरुर्विप्रः प्रोक्तो वर्णद्वयस्य च //
248.m: battles with swords are inferior, and wrestling is the lowest of all. / In the science of archery, a Brahmin is declared to be the teacher of two castes.

248.s:
yuddhādhikāraḥ śūdrasya svayaṃ vyāpādi śikṣayā /
deśasthaiḥ śaṅkarai rājñaḥ kāryā yuddhe sahāyatā //
248.d:
युद्धाधिकारः शूद्रस्य स्वयं व्यापादि शिक्षया /
देशस्थैः शङ्करै राज्ञः कार्या युद्धे सहायता //
248.m: The right to fight belongs to a Śūdra when he is engaged on his own through instruction. / Mixed castes residing in the realm should render assistance to the king in war.

248.s:
aṅguṣṭhagulphapāṇyaṅghyaḥ śliṣṭāḥ syuḥ sahitā yadi /
dṛṣṭaṃ samapadaṃ sthānametallakṣaṇatas tathā //
248.d:
अङ्गुष्ठगुल्फपाण्यङ्घ्यः श्लिष्टाः स्युः सहिता यदि /
दृष्टं समपदं स्थानमेतल्लक्षणतस् तथा //
248.m: If the big toes, ankles, palms, and feet are close and joined together, / that stance is seen as samapada, according to its characteristics.

248.s:
vāhyāṅgulisthitau pādau stabdhajānubalāvubhau /
trivitastyantarāsthānametadvaiśākhamucyate //
248.d:
वाह्याङ्गुलिस्थितौ पादौ स्तब्धजानुबलावुभौ /
त्रिवितस्त्यन्तरास्थानमेतद्वैशाखमुच्यते //
248.m: When the feet stand on the outer toes and both knees and forces are stiff, / the stance with an interval of three spans is called the vaiśākha.

248.s:
haṃsapaṅktyākṛtisame dṛśyete yatra jānunī /
caturvitastivicchinne tadetanmaṇḍalaṃ smṛtaṃ //
248.d:
हंसपङ्क्त्याकृतिसमे दृश्येते यत्र जानुनी /
चतुर्वितस्तिविच्छिन्ने तदेतन्मण्डलं स्मृतं //
248.m: Where the knees are seen to resemble the shape of a flock of swans, / separated by four spans, that is known as the maṇḍala stance.

248.s:
halākṛtimayaṃ yacca stabdhajānūrudakṣiṇaṃ /
vitastyaḥ pañca vistāre tadālīḍhaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
248.d:
हलाकृतिमयं यच्च स्तब्धजानूरुदक्षिणं /
वितस्त्यः पञ्च विस्तारे तदालीढं प्रकीर्तितं //
248.m: That which has the shape of a plough, with the right knee and thigh stiff, / and five spans in breadth, is proclaimed as the ālīḍha stance.

248.s:
etadeva viparyastaṃ pratyālīḍhamiti smṛtaṃ(1) /
tiryagbhūto bhavedvāmo dakṣiṇo 'pi bhavedṛjuḥ //
248.d:
एतदेव विपर्यस्तं प्रत्यालीढमिति स्मृतं(1) /
तिर्यग्भूतो भवेद्वामो दक्षिणो ऽपि भवेदृजुः //
248.m: The reverse of this is known as pratyālīḍha. / The left [leg] is positioned obliquely and the right is straight.

248.s:
gulphau pārṣṇigrahau caiva sthitau pañcāṅgulāntarau /
:n
1 pratyālīḍhaṃ prakīrtitamiti ja..
:p 397
sthānaṃ jātaṃ bhavedetad dvādaśāṅgulamāyataṃ //
248.d:
गुल्फौ पार्ष्णिग्रहौ चैव स्थितौ पञ्चाङ्गुलान्तरौ /
:न्
1 प्रत्यालीढं प्रकीर्तितमिति ज..
:प् 397
स्थानं जातं भवेदेतद् द्वादशाङ्गुलमायतं //
248.m:
The ankles and heels are held at an interval of five finger-breadths;
[...]
[Footnote: pratyālīḍhaṃ prakīrtitam according to manuscript ja.]
[Page 397]
this stance becomes twelve finger-breadths in extent, [known as] jāta.

248.s:
ṛjujānurbhavedvāmo dakṣiṇaḥ suprasāritaḥ /
athavā dakṣiṇañjānu kubjaṃ bhavati niś calaṃ //
248.d:
ऋजुजानुर्भवेद्वामो दक्षिणः सुप्रसारितः /
अथवा दक्षिणञ्जानु कुब्जं भवति निश् चलं //
248.m: The left knee should be straight, the right extended well forward; / or the right knee becomes bent and motionless,

248.s:
daṇḍāyato bhavedeṣa caraṇaḥ saha jānunā /
evaṃ vikaṭamuddiṣṭaṃ dvihastāntaramāyataṃ //
248.d:
दण्डायतो भवेदेष चरणः सह जानुना /
एवं विकटमुद्दिष्टं द्विहस्तान्तरमायतं //
248.m: and this foot together with the knee is stretched straight like a staff. / Such is designated as vikaṭa, extending to an interval of two cubits.

248.s:
jānunī dviguṇe syātāmuttānau caraṇāvubhau /
anena vidhiyogena sampuṭaṃ parikīrtitaṃ //
248.d:
जानुनी द्विगुणे स्यातामुत्तानौ चरणावुभौ /
अनेन विधियोगेन सम्पुटं परिकीर्तितं //
248.m: When the knees are doubled and both feet are turned upwards, / according to this rule it is declared to be sampuṭa.

248.s:
kiñcidvivartitau pādau samadaṇḍāyatau sthirau /
dṛṣṭameva yathānyāyaṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulamāyataṃ //
248.d:
किञ्चिद्विवर्तितौ पादौ समदण्डायतौ स्थिरौ /
दृष्टमेव यथान्यायं षोडशाङ्गुलमायतं //
248.m: With feet turned slightly, extended evenly like a staff and firm, / it is seen as sixteen finger-breadths long according to rule.

248.s:
svastikenātra kurvīta praṇāmaṃ prathamaṃ dvija /
kāmukaṃ gṛhya vāmena vāṇaṃ dakṣiṇakena tu //
248.d:
स्वस्तिकेनात्र कुर्वीत प्रणामं प्रथमं द्विज /
कामुकं गृह्य वामेन वाणं दक्षिणकेन तु //
248.m: Here, O twice-born, one should first make obeisance in the svastika stance, / taking the bow with the left hand and the arrow with the right.

248.s:
vaiśākhe yadi vā jāte sthitau vāpyathavāyatau /
guṇāntantu tataḥ kṛtvā kārmuke priyakārmukaḥ //
248.d:
वैशाखे यदि वा जाते स्थितौ वाप्यथवायतौ /
गुणान्तन्तु ततः कृत्वा कार्मुके प्रियकार्मुकः //
248.m: Standing in the vaiśākha or in the jāta stance, or stretched out, / he who loves the bow, having then strung the bowstring upon the bow,

248.s:
adhaḥkaṭintu dhanuṣaḥ phaladeśantu patriṇaḥ /
dharaṇyāṃ sthāpayitvā tu tolayitvā tathaiva ca //
248.d:
अधःकटिन्तु धनुषः फलदेशन्तु पत्रिणः /
धरण्यां स्थापयित्वा तु तोलयित्वा तथैव च //
248.m: and having placed the lower notch of the bow and the tip of the feathered shaft / on the earth, and balanced it in that manner,

248.s:
bhujābhyāmatra kuñjābhyāṃ prakoṣṭhābhyāṃ śubhavrata /
yasya vāṇaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ puṅgadeśe ca patriṇaḥ //
248.d:
भुजाभ्यामत्र कुञ्जाभ्यां प्रकोष्ठाभ्यां शुभव्रत /
यस्य वाणं धनुः श्रेष्ठं पुङ्गदेशे च पत्रिणः //
248.m: with both arms, both hands, and both forearms, O you of auspicious vows— / the bow and arrow of which warrior are superior at the nock-end of the feathered shaft,

248.s:
vinyāso dhanuś caiva dvādaśāṅgulamantaraṃ /
jyayā viśiṣṭaḥ kartavyo nātihīno na cādhikaḥ //
248.d:
विन्यासो धनुश् चैव द्वादशाङ्गुलमन्तरं /
ज्यया विशिष्टः कर्तव्यो नातिहीनो न चाधिकः //
248.m: the distance in the placement of the bow should be twelve finger-breadths / measured from the bowstring; it should be neither too short nor too great.

248.s:
niveśya kārmukaṃ nabhyāṃ nitambe śarasaṅkaraṃ /
utkṣipedutthitaṃ hastamantareṇākṣikarṇayoḥ //
248.d:
निवेश्य कार्मुकं नभ्यां नितम्बे शरसङ्करं /
उत्क्षिपेदुत्थितं हस्तमन्तरेणाक्षिकर्णयोः //
248.m: Placing the bow at the navel and the bundle of arrows at the hip, / he should raise his lifted hand between the eye and the ear.

248.s:
pūrveṇa muṣṭinā grāhyastanāgre dakṣiṇe śaraḥ /
haraṇantu tataḥ kṛtvā śīghraṃ pūrvaṃ prasārayet //
:p 398
248.d:
पूर्वेण मुष्टिना ग्राह्यस्तनाग्रे दक्षिणे शरः /
हरणन्तु ततः कृत्वा शीघ्रं पूर्वं प्रसारयेत् //
:प् 398
248.m:
The arrow should be seized at the right breast-tip with the front fist; / having then drawn it, he should quickly extend the front [hand].
[Page 398]

248.s:
nābhyantarā naiva vāhyā nordhvakā nādharā tathā /
na ca kubjā na cottānā na calā nātiveṣṭitā //
248.d:
नाभ्यन्तरा नैव वाह्या नोर्ध्वका नाधरा तथा /
न च कुब्जा न चोत्ताना न चला नातिवेष्टिता //
248.m: [The hand] should be neither inside nor outside, neither high nor low, / neither bent nor supine, neither shaking nor excessively twisted;

248.s:
samā sthairyaguṇopetā pūrvadaṇḍamiva sthitā /
chādayitvā tato lakṣyaṃ pūrveṇānena muṣṭinā //
248.d:
समा स्थैर्यगुणोपेता पूर्वदण्डमिव स्थिता /
छादयित्वा ततो लक्ष्यं पूर्वेणानेन मुष्टिना //
248.m: even, endowed with the quality of steadiness, standing like a straight staff. / Having then covered the target with this front fist,

248.s:
urasā tūtthito yantā trikoṇavinatasthitaḥ /
srastāṃśe niś calagrīvo mayūrāñcitamastakaḥ //
248.d:
उरसा तूत्थितो यन्ता त्रिकोणविनतस्थितः /
स्रस्तांशे निश् चलग्रीवो मयूराञ्चितमस्तकः //
248.m: the archer stands rising with his chest, bent in a triangle, / with lowered shoulders, a motionless neck, and head tilted gracefully like a peacock.

248.s:
lalāṭanāsāvaktrāṃsāḥ kuryuraśvasamambhavet /
antaraṃ tryaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ civukasyāṃsakasya ca //
248.d:
ललाटनासावक्त्रांसाः कुर्युरश्वसमम्भवेत् /
अन्तरं त्र्यङ्गुलं ज्ञेयं चिवुकस्यांसकस्य च //
248.m: The forehead, nose, mouth, and shoulders should be aligned like a horse's. / The space between the chin and the shoulder should be known as three finger-breadths.

248.s:
prathamantryaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ dvitīye dvyaṅgulaṃ smṛtaṃ /
tṛtīye 'ṅgulamudiṣṭamāyatañcivukāṃsayoḥ //
248.d:
प्रथमन्त्र्यङ्गुलं ज्ञेयं द्वितीये द्व्यङ्गुलं स्मृतं /
तृतीये ऽङ्गुलमुदिष्टमायतञ्चिवुकांसयोः //
248.m: In the first [position] it is three finger-breadths; in the second it is considered two finger-breadths; / in the third, the span between chin and shoulder is taught to be one finger-breadth.

248.s:
gṛhītvā sāyakaṃ puṅkhāttarjanyāṅguṣṭhakena tu /
anāmayā punargṛhya tathā madhyamayāpi ca //
248.d:
गृहीत्वा सायकं पुङ्खात्तर्जन्याङ्गुष्ठकेन तु /
अनामया पुनर्गृह्य तथा मध्यमयापि च //
248.m: Having seized the arrow at the nock with the forefinger and thumb, / and seizing it again with the ring finger as well as with the middle finger,

248.s:
tāvadākarṣayedvegādyāvadvāṇaḥ supūritaḥ /
evaṃ vidhamupakramya moktavyaṃ vidhivat khagaṃ //
248.d:
तावदाकर्षयेद्वेगाद्यावद्वाणः सुपूरितः /
एवं विधमुपक्रम्य मोक्तव्यं विधिवत् खगं //
248.m: he should draw it back with force until the arrow is fully drawn. / Having begun in this way, he should release the shaft according to rule.

248.s:
dṛṣṭimuṣṭihataṃ lakṣyaṃ bhindyādvāṇena suvrataḥ /
muktvā tu(1) paścimaṃ hastaṃ kṣipedvegena pṛṣṭhataḥ //
248.d:
दृष्टिमुष्टिहतं लक्ष्यं भिन्द्याद्वाणेन सुव्रतः /
मुक्त्वा तु(1) पश्चिमं हस्तं क्षिपेद्वेगेन पृष्ठतः //
248.m: One of good vows should pierce the target struck by his sight and fist. / Having released, he should throw the rear hand swiftly backwards.

248.s:
etaducchedamicchanti jñātavyaṃ hi tvayā dvija /
kūrparantadadhaḥ kāryamākṛṣya tu dhanuṣmatā //
248.d:
एतदुच्छेदमिच्छन्ति ज्ञातव्यं हि त्वया द्विज /
कूर्परन्तदधः कार्यमाकृष्य तु धनुष्मता //
248.m: They desire this cut-off [release]; it must indeed be known by you, O twice-born. / The elbow must be brought down by the archer upon drawing.

248.s:
ūrdhvaṃ vimuktake kārye lakṣaśliṣṭantu madhyamaṃ /
śreṣṭhaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ vijñeyaṃdhanuḥśāstraviśāradaiḥ //
248.d:
ऊर्ध्वं विमुक्तके कार्ये लक्षश्लिष्टन्तु मध्यमं /
श्रेष्ठं प्रकृष्टं विज्ञेयंधनुःशास्त्रविशारदैः //
248.m: When drawn upward, the middle is clinging to the target; / this is known as excellent and superior by those skilled in the science of archery.

248.s:
jyeṣṭhastu sāyako jñeyo bhaveddvādaśamuṣṭayaḥ /
:n
1 tyaktvā iti ja..
:p 399
ekādaśa tathā kanīyāndaśamuṣṭayaḥ //
248.d:
ज्येष्ठस्तु सायको ज्ञेयो भवेद्द्वादशमुष्टयः /
:न्
1 त्यक्त्वा इति ज..
:प् 399
एकादश तथा कनीयान्दशमुष्टयः //
248.m:
The longest arrow should be known to be twelve fist-lengths;
[...]
[Footnote: tyaktvā instead of muktvā tu according to manuscript ja.]
[Page 397]
the intermediate is eleven, and the shortest is ten fist-lengths.

248.s:
caturhastaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ trayaḥ sārdhantu madhyamaṃ /
kanīyastu trayaḥ proktaṃ nityameva padātinaḥ //
248.d:
चतुर्हस्तं धनुः श्रेष्ठं त्रयः सार्धन्तु मध्यमं /
कनीयस्तु त्रयः प्रोक्तं नित्यमेव पदातिनः //
248.m: A bow of four cubits is best; one of three and a half is middling; / and one of three is declared shortest, always for a foot-soldier.

248.s:
aśve rathe gaje śreṣṭhe tadeva parikīrtitaṃ //38//
:e ity āgenye mahāpurāṇe dhanurvedo nāma
aṣṭacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athonapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dhanurvedakathanaṃ
248.d:
अश्वे रथे गजे श्रेष्ठे तदेव परिकीर्तितं //38//
:ए इत्य् आगेन्ये महापुराणे धनुर्वेदो नाम
अष्टचत्वारिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथोनपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
धनुर्वेदकथनं
248.m:
For a horse, chariot, or superior elephant, the same is proclaimed.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa the two hundred and forty-eighth chapter, entitled “The Science of Archery.”
Now the two hundred and forty-ninth chapter.
The Discourse on the Science of Archery.

249.s:
agnir uvāca
pūrṇāyataṃ dvijaḥ kṛtvā tato māṃsair gadāyudhān /
sunirdhautaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā yajñabhūmau vidhāpayet //
249.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पूर्णायतं द्विजः कृत्वा ततो मांसैर् गदायुधान् /
सुनिर्धौतं धनुः कृत्वा यज्ञभूमौ विधापयेत् //
249.m:
Agni said:
Having drawn it fully, O twice-born, and having worshipped those armed with maces with meat, / having cleansed the bow well, he should set it upon the sacrificial ground.

249.s:
tato vāṇaṃ samāgṛhya daṃśitaḥ susamāhitaḥ /
tūrṇamāsādya badhnīyādṛḍhāṃ kakṣāñca dakṣiṇām //
249.d:
ततो वाणं समागृह्य दंशितः सुसमाहितः /
तूर्णमासाद्य बध्नीयादृढां कक्षाञ्च दक्षिणाम् //
249.m: Then, having taken the arrow, armored, well composed, / having quickly approached, he should fasten his firm right waist-band.

249.s:
vilakṣyamapi tadvāṇaṃ tatra caiva susaṃsthitaṃ /
tataḥ samuddharedvāṇaṃ tūṇāddakṣiṇapāṇinā //
249.d:
विलक्ष्यमपि तद्वाणं तत्र चैव सुसंस्थितं /
ततः समुद्धरेद्वाणं तूणाद्दक्षिणपाणिना //
249.m: Even with target fixed, that arrow being properly set there, / he should then extract the arrow from the quiver with his right hand.

249.s:
tenaiva sahitaṃ madhye śaraṃ saṅgṛhya dhārayet /
vāmahastena vai kakṣāṃ dhanustasmātsamuddharet //
249.d:
तेनैव सहितं मध्ये शरं सङ्गृह्य धारयेत् /
वामहस्तेन वै कक्षां धनुस्तस्मात्समुद्धरेत् //
249.m: Holding the arrow grasped in the middle along with it, / he should lift the bow from that side with his left hand.

249.s:
aviṣaṇṇamatirbhūtvā guṇe puṅkhaṃ niveśayet /
sampīḍya siṃhakarṇena puṅkhenāpi same dṛḍhaṃ //
:p 400
249.d:
अविषण्णमतिर्भूत्वा गुणे पुङ्खं निवेशयेत् /
सम्पीड्य सिंहकर्णेन पुङ्खेनापि समे दृढं //
:प् 400
249.m:
Becoming free of despondency, he should seat the nock on the bowstring, / having pressed firmly with the lion's-ear grip, evenly on both sides of the nock.
[Page 400]

249.s:
vāmakarṇopaviṣtañca phalaṃ vāmasya dhārayet /
varṇān madhyamayā tatra vāmāṅgulyā ca dhārayet //
249.d:
वामकर्णोपविष्तञ्च फलं वामस्य धारयेत् /
वर्णान् मध्यमया तत्र वामाङ्गुल्या च धारयेत् //
249.m: He should hold the arrowhead resting near the left ear, belonging to the left [side]; / and there he should hold the arrows with the middle finger and the left fingers.

249.s:
mano lakṣyagataṃ kṛtvā muṣṭinā ca vidhānavit /
dakṣiṇe gātrabhāge tu kṛtvā varṇaṃ vimokṣayet //
249.d:
मनो लक्ष्यगतं कृत्वा मुष्टिना च विधानवित् /
दक्षिणे गात्रभागे तु कृत्वा वर्णं विमोक्षयेत् //
249.m: Fixing the mind upon the target, knowing the rules, / holding [the string] with the fist and bringing the arrow to the right side of the body, he should release it.

249.s:
lalāṭapuṭasaṃsthānaṃ daṇḍaṃ lakṣye niveśayet /
ākṛṣya tāḍayettatra candrakaṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulam //
249.d:
ललाटपुटसंस्थानं दण्डं लक्ष्ये निवेशयेत् /
आकृष्य ताडयेत्तत्र चन्द्रकं षोडशाङ्गुलम् //
249.m: He should place the shaft in line with the target at the level of the forehead; / having drawn back, he should strike the ring target of sixteen finger-breadths there.

249.s:
muktvā vāṇaṃ tataḥ paścādulkāśikṣastadā tayā /
nigṛhṇīyān madhyamayā tato 'ṅgulyā punaḥ punaḥ //
249.d:
मुक्त्वा वाणं ततः पश्चादुल्काशिक्षस्तदा तया /
निगृह्णीयान् मध्यमया ततो ऽङ्गुल्या पुनः पुनः //
249.m: Having released the arrow, one wishing to learn the firebrand [speed] should then repeatedly / check [the bowstring] with that [hand], with the middle finger.

249.s:
akṣilakṣyaṃ kṣipettūṇāccaturasrañca dakṣiṇam /
caturasragataṃ vedhyamabhyaseccāditaḥ sthitaḥ //
249.d:
अक्षिलक्ष्यं क्षिपेत्तूणाच्चतुरस्रञ्च दक्षिणम् /
चतुरस्रगतं वेध्यमभ्यसेच्चादितः स्थितः //
249.m: He should draw from the quiver at eye-level, keeping [the body] four-square and to the right; / standing firmly from the beginning, he should practice hitting a target that is four-square.

249.s:
tasmādanantaraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ parāvṛttaṃ gatañca yat /
nimnamunnatavedhañca abhyaset kṣiprakantataḥ //
249.d:
तस्मादनन्तरं तीक्ष्णं परावृत्तं गतञ्च यत् /
निम्नमुन्नतवेधञ्च अभ्यसेत् क्षिप्रकन्ततः //
249.m: Immediately after that, he should swiftly practice / sharp, turning-away, moving, / low, and high shooting.
Then, among these positions of the target, drawing the bow from the chest of courage, / he should threaten [the foe] with hundreds of varied arm-guard movements, even those hard to endure.

249.s:
tasmin(1) vedhyagate vipra dve vedhye dṛḍhasañjñake /
dve vedhye duṣkare vedhye dve tathā citraduṣkare //
249.d:
तस्मिन्(1) वेध्यगते विप्र द्वे वेध्ये दृढसञ्ज्ञके /
द्वे वेध्ये दुष्करे वेध्ये द्वे तथा चित्रदुष्करे //
249.m: When it comes to that target, O brahmin, two targets are known as 'firm', / two targets are 'difficult', and likewise two are 'variously difficult'.

249.s:
na tu nimnañca(2) tīkṣṇañca dṛḍhavedhye prakīrtite /
nimnaṃ duṣkaramuddiṣṭaṃ vedhyamūrdhvagatañca yat //
249.d:
न तु निम्नञ्च(2) तीक्ष्णञ्च दृढवेध्ये प्रकीर्तिते /
निम्नं दुष्करमुद्दिष्टं वेध्यमूर्ध्वगतञ्च यत् //
249.m: The low and the sharp are declared to be the two 'firm' targets; / the low and that which moves upward are stated to be 'difficult'.

249.s:
mastakāyanamadhye tu citraduṣkarasañjñake /
evaṃ vedhyagaṇaṅkṛtvā dakṣiṇenetareṇa ca //
249.d:
मस्तकायनमध्ये तु चित्रदुष्करसञ्ज्ञके /
एवं वेध्यगणङ्कृत्वा दक्षिणेनेतरेण च //
249.m: And in the middle of the head's path are the two named 'variously difficult'; / having thus arranged the array of targets, with the right and the other [hand],

249.s:
ārohet prathamaṃ vīro jitalakṣastato naraḥ /
eṣa eva vidhiḥ proktastatra dṛṣṭaḥ prayoktṛbhiḥ //
:n
1 asminniti kha.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
2 namrañceti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 401
249.d:
आरोहेत् प्रथमं वीरो जितलक्षस्ततो नरः /
एष एव विधिः प्रोक्तस्तत्र दृष्टः प्रयोक्तृभिः //
:न्
1 अस्मिन्निति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. च
2 नम्रञ्चेति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 401
249.m:
a heroic man who has mastered targets should first mount [his chariot or horse]; / this very procedure is taught, as seen by practitioners.
[Footnotes]
1. 'asminn iti' in manuscripts kha, cha, and ja.
2. 'namrañ ceti' in manuscripts gha and ña.
[Page 401]

249.s:
adhikaṃ bhramaṇaṃ tasya tasmādvedhyāt prakīrtitam /
lakṣyaṃ sa yojayettatra patripatragataṃ dṛḍham //
249.d:
अधिकं भ्रमणं तस्य तस्माद्वेध्यात् प्रकीर्तितम् /
लक्ष्यं स योजयेत्तत्र पत्रिपत्रगतं दृढम् //
249.m: Greater rotation than that from the target is declared for him; / he should firmly fix the target there, feather upon feather.

249.s:
bhrāntaṃ pracalitañcaiva sthiraṃ yacca bhavediti /
samantāttāḍayed bhindyācchedayedvyathayedapi //
249.d:
भ्रान्तं प्रचलितञ्चैव स्थिरं यच्च भवेदिति /
समन्तात्ताडयेद् भिन्द्याच्छेदयेद्व्यथयेदपि //
249.m: Whatever is wandering, moving, or stationary, / he should strike on all sides, pierce, cut through, or wound.

249.s:
karmayogavidhānajño jñātvaivaṃ vidhimācaret /
manasā cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭyā yogaśikṣuryamaṃ jayet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dhanurvede
nāmonapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dhanurvedakathanam
249.d:
कर्मयोगविधानज्ञो ज्ञात्वैवं विधिमाचरेत् /
मनसा चक्षुषा दृष्ट्या योगशिक्षुर्यमं जयेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे धनुर्वेदे
नामोनपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
धनुर्वेदकथनम्
249.m:
Knowing the rules of the practice of actions, knowing this, he should perform the procedure; / practicing discipline with mind, eye, and gaze, he can conquer death.
Thus ends the two hundred and forty-ninth chapter, entitled 'The Science of Archery', in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the two hundred and fiftieth chapter:
Account of the Science of Archery.

250.s:
agnir uvāca
jitahasto jitamatirjitadṛglakṣyasādhakaḥ /
niyatāṃ siddhimāsādya tato vāhanamāruhet //
250.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
जितहस्तो जितमतिर्जितदृग्लक्ष्यसाधकः /
नियतां सिद्धिमासाद्य ततो वाहनमारुहेत् //
250.m:
Agni said:
One whose hands are mastered, mind mastered, sight mastered, hitting targets, / having attained assured success, should then mount a mount.

250.s:
daśahasto bhavet pāśo vṛttaḥ karamukhas tathā /
guṇakārpāsamuñjānāṃ bhaṅgasnāyvarkavarmiṇām //
250.d:
दशहस्तो भवेत् पाशो वृत्तः करमुखस् तथा /
गुणकार्पासमुञ्जानां भङ्गस्नाय्वर्कवर्मिणाम् //
250.m: A noose should be ten cubits long, round, with a loop at the end, / made of sinew, cotton, muñja grass, hemp, animal tendon, or arka fiber;

250.s:
anyeṣāṃ sudṛḍhānāñca sukṛtaṃ pariveṣṭitam /
tathā triṃśatsamaṃ pāśaṃ budhaḥ kuryāt suvartitam //
250.d:
अन्येषां सुदृढानाञ्च सुकृतं परिवेष्टितम् /
तथा त्रिंशत्समं पाशं बुधः कुर्यात् सुवर्तितम् //
250.m: or of other very strong [materials], well-made and twisted; / likewise, a wise man should make a well-spun noose equal to thirty [cubits].

250.s:
kartavyaṃ śikṣakaistasya sthānaṃ kakṣāsu vai tadā /
vāmahastena saṅgṛhya dakṣiṇenoddharettataḥ //
250.d:
कर्तव्यं शिक्षकैस्तस्य स्थानं कक्षासु वै तदा /
वामहस्तेन सङ्गृह्य दक्षिणेनोद्धरेत्ततः //
250.m: Its position should then be made by teachers at the sides; / taking it with the left hand, he should then raise it with the right,

250.s:
kuṇḍalasyākṛtiṃ kṛtvā bhrāmyakaṃ mastakopari /
:p 402
kṣipet tūrṇamaye tūrṇaṃ puruṣe carmaveṣṭite(1) //
250.d:
कुण्डलस्याकृतिं कृत्वा भ्राम्यकं मस्तकोपरि /
:प् 402
क्षिपेत् तूर्णमये तूर्णं पुरुषे चर्मवेष्टिते(1) //
250.m:
forming a coil and whirling it above his head
[Page 402]
he should quickly cast it at a dummy made of straw covered in leather.

250.s:
valgite ca plute caiva tathā pravrajiteṣu ca /
samayogavidhiṃ kṛtvā(2) prayuñjīta suśikṣitam //
250.d:
वल्गिते च प्लुते चैव तथा प्रव्रजितेषु च /
समयोगविधिं कृत्वा(2) प्रयुञ्जीत सुशिक्षितम् //
250.m: Against one trotting, leaping, or charging, / having applied the proper method, he should employ it well-trained.

250.s:
vijitvā tu yathānyāyaṃ tato bandhaṃ samācaret /
kaṭyāmbaddhvā tataḥ khaḍgaṃ vāmapārśvāvalambitam //
250.d:
विजित्वा तु यथान्यायं ततो बन्धं समाचरेत् /
कट्याम्बद्ध्वा ततः खड्गं वामपार्श्वावलम्बितम् //
250.m: Having conquered [the target] duly, he should then perform the binding. / Then, fastening a sword at the waist, hanging on the left side,

250.s:
dṛḍhaṃ vigṛhya vāmena niṣkarṣeddakṣiṇena tu /
ṣaḍaṅgulaparīṇāhaṃ saptahastasamucchritaṃ //
250.d:
दृढं विगृह्य वामेन निष्कर्षेद्दक्षिणेन तु /
षडङ्गुलपरीणाहं सप्तहस्तसमुच्छ्रितं //
250.m: grasping it firmly with the left [hand], he should draw it with the right. / [A target dummy] six finger-breadths in circumference and seven cubits high,

250.s:
ayomayyaḥ śalākāś ca varmāṇi vividhāni ca /
ardhahaste same caiva tiryagūrdhvagataṃ tathā //
250.d:
अयोमय्यः शलाकाश् च वर्माणि विविधानि च /
अर्धहस्ते समे चैव तिर्यगूर्ध्वगतं तथा //
250.m: with iron spikes and various armors, / placed at half a cubit, level, oblique, and high:

250.s:
yojayedvidhinā yena tathātvaṅgadataḥ śṛṇu /
tūṇacarmāvanaddhāṅgaṃ sthāpayitvā navaṃ dṛḍhaṃ //
250.d:
योजयेद्विधिना येन तथात्वङ्गदतः शृणु /
तूणचर्मावनद्धाङ्गं स्थापयित्वा नवं दृढं //
250.m: listen now to how he should employ it by rule, limb by limb: / having set up a new, firm [post] whose body is covered in leather and a quiver,

250.s:
kareṇādāya lagūḍaṃ dakṣiṇāṅgulakaṃ navaṃ /
udyamya ghātayedyasya nāśastena śiśordṛḍhaṃ //
250.d:
करेणादाय लगूडं दक्षिणाङ्गुलकं नवं /
उद्यम्य घातयेद्यस्य नाशस्तेन शिशोर्दृढं //
250.m: taking a new stick nine finger-breadths [wide] with the hand, / raising it, he should strike it; by that, the destruction of a novice's [error] is assured.

250.s:
ubhābhyāmatha hastābhyāṃ kuryāttasya nipātanaṃ /
akleśena tataḥ kurvan badhe siddhiḥ prakīrtitā //
250.d:
उभाभ्यामथ हस्ताभ्यां कुर्यात्तस्य निपातनं /
अक्लेशेन ततः कुर्वन् बधे सिद्धिः प्रकीर्तिता //
250.m: Then with both hands he should cause its downfall; / performing it without strain, success in striking is declared.

250.s:
vāhānāṃ śramakaraṇaṃ pracārārthaṃ purā tava //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dhanurvedo nāma pañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 varmaveṣṭite iti gha..
2 jñātveti ṭa..
:p 403
:ś athaikapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dhanurvedakathanaṃ
250.d:
वाहानां श्रमकरणं प्रचारार्थं पुरा तव //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे धनुर्वेदो नाम पञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 वर्मवेष्टिते इति घ..
2 ज्ञात्वेति ट..
:प् 403
:श् अथैकपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
धनुर्वेदकथनं
250.m:
The training of mounts was taught to you previously for the sake of movement.
Thus ends the two hundred and fiftieth chapter, named 'The Science of Archery', in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnotes]
1. 'varmaveṣṭite' in manuscript gha.
2. 'jñātvā' in manuscript ṭa.
[Page 403]

Account of the Science of Archery.
